Isn't it weird to think that Devil May Cry originally was planned as a sequel in the long running Resident Evil franchise? It spawned from a lost concept intended for Resident Evil by one Hideki Kamiya. Ever since it has evolved into a bonifide and excellent action franchise, spawning 3 sequels, one ♥♥♥♥♥♥ reboot, an anime, probably a manga and a love pillow? You name it. It was dropped from being a Resident Evil game due to its supernatural elements and presence of "demons" not quite fitting the conservative tentacle-sausage monsters that look like they spawned from the deepest recesses of H.R. Geiger's soul, well enough
You could even be forgiven for thinking that recent Resident Evil titles seemingly bears striking similar elements to that of a Devil May Cry game with its radical tendency to burst into cinematic overload mode, with unfair quicktime events and ridiculous over-the-top stunts that defy all logic and physic laws as we know it. Devil May Cry 4 carries the term "over-the-top" with pride as it comfortably ravels in its glorious legacy as a great hardcore over-the-top action title.
The original Devil May Cry 4, however, had its share of issues like its nagging prediclection of repition in vein of Silent Hill 4. Half-way through the story you're bold-facely forced to walk in reverse order of the entire game's map and beat the same bosses twice along with the dreadful padded "board-game" section. The enemies are also a bit uninspired in comparison to the likes of Devil May Cry 3--Plus, can I just say that I hate camera sometimes? It's litterally the toughest enemy in the game to conquer. Bad, bad, bad, Capcom.
Looking past that however, Devil May Cry 4's combat is delightful. The ability to launch enemies in the air and litterally keep them there by filling every orifice with lead as Dante, or cutting them in mid-air as Nero while using the Devil Arm as a bolster for keeping the momentum in motion.
What is excellent about the Special Edition is the awesome addition of the 3 new playable characters. Lady, Trish and Vergil--All of them carry simply excellent movesets, unique to them and their personalities. Vergil borrows a lot of his abilities moveset from DMC3 and from Vorgil in the Ninja Theory's edgy reboot. He's ridiculously fast and precise with his katana "Yamato" which is balanced by his more brutal strikes with the gloves and boots he got in DMC3 (forgot the name) delivering powerful blows that will usually deal devastating damage at the expense of his speed-Oh, and of course Force Edge, which is more or less his father's sword, and grants him movesets similar to his brother Dante. Vergil relies on speed and precisition(as mentioned). The more precise you are with each attack, the faster he becomes, it is imperative that all attacks hit home while also attempting not to get hit in order to the get the most out of him.
Lady is a loaded powerhouse of ridiculous weaponry that will quite simply devastate all enemies, which makes her so much fun to play, but will probably diminish a lot of challenge from the game. But who cares? She's fun, damnit! Her shotgun and pistol attacks are similar to Dante's but vastly more powerful and packs quite a punch to enemies. Her shotgun can litterally make enemies bound off and on walls until they die should you position yourself appropriately for it to happen. She also has a form of grappling hook, which she can use to launch enemies into the air and smack them down again, or if you're a creative ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, to line them up for a shot with the rocket, in the air, and/or the guns for some extra Stylish points.
Trish is the character I have least experience with yet -- So far she seems to play a bit similar to Dante though she has plenty of interesting range attacks using the sword Sparda, or whatever hell they call that monstrosity of a sword. I have admittedly not a lot to say about her yet but safe to say she's just as fun as the rest to play. I assure you!
The inevitable failings of remasters, as mentioned, is that they are usually always put into the uncomfortable position of carrying all of the detrimental issues the original had with them. I've lined most of them all up already, though they are easily ignored when playing the new characters because said additions to the Special Edition outweigh anything bad I have to say about the game... Well, except for the visuals. Its age is still showing and the remastered visuals aren't really taking advantage of my powerhouse PC's capabilities, so I can't really vouch for it there.. Maybe I just haven't optimized it properly but I wouldn't say the looks are anything to jump in glee over
Having said that -- Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition has build upon what was a pretty good game and made it into a really fun game! If you love games from Platinum or action titles in general then you shouldn't cheat yourself out of the Special Edition for DMC4.. Buy it, whenever it goes on sale anyway!

This is how you re-relase something.
Devil May Cry 4 as it is, is practicly unchanged. Okay, that isn't true, the nextgen console port recieved higher resolution textures, 60fps and 1080p support, but for us PC players that was standard back when we got the PC version of the original relase on X360/PS3, and Legendary Dark Knight mode is also something we already had on PC. Other than that, there is a slight numerical rebalance for moves, but everything else is still the same, well optimized lightspeed running and beautiful Sick Smokin' Style we came to know.
Why would you want to buy this then?
Because DMC4SE has absolutely MASSIVE amount of new content, if you play DMC games for what they should be played: replayability and perfecting your fighting techniques in overly increasing challanges. Now you have on top of the original protagonists, Dante and Nero, 3, I repeat THREE new characters, returning characters from the classics, and each of them have drasticly different new gameplay mechanisms that are guaranteed to give even the most diehard DMC4 players a lot new things to learn, experiment with and enjoy. They all have their own intros and outros, but the campign is the same 20 missions for all from the main game (so same as DMC3SE method). You can skip the 1-2-3 parts if you don't want to read about new characters.
1. Vergil, the number one cold blooded honorable swordsman returns from DMC3SE with all his moves, plus about a dozen new ones, and a "focus" meter that translates to "how cold and badass you are meter". The less you move while an enemy is locked, the less unnecessary moves you make, the most perfect you play, this meter increases giving vergil a massive power boost (many of his moves even change when it's full), and you can pretty much wipe the screen with super judgement cut. He is insanely fast in both movement and diverse attacks, and yet the most powerful when you slow down and hold yourself back for the sake of being stylish.
2. Lady a.k.a Mary from DMC3's story, who is playable for the first time in the franchise's history. She fights only with varios firearms, such as double pistols, shotgun and her signature bladed rocket launcher and granades. Her moves and fighting style are so different compared to any other playable DMC franchise character ever that she didn't only earn the most unique character title in the franchise rightfully, but also the fact that I as a veteran DMC player had to learn absolutely everything from the basics to play with her. Your whole style, positioning, the way you exploit weaknesses of various enemies, everything is so different she could have her own game.
3. And last, everyone's teenage dream sexy demon, Trish. She is also playable for the first time, and uses electricity as static damaging "objects" in the game, drawing thunder in the air that stay there for a while and keeps hitting enemies, transforming each battle to more of an area control tactical battlefield, much like the reboot DmC. Sadly, most of her moves while function uniquely (that gold ball hitting combo with Sparda's transformed sword is hilarious, in a good way), sadly are reused animations from mainly Dante's moves.
So... basicly this is it. Compared to the old, original edition of DMC4, Special Edition also comes with various steamworks extras such as achievements, cloud saving, trading cards. If you have not bought DMC4 yet, definitly go for Special Edition. The replayability that these games are built for anyway, is so astoundingly increased I'm not even sure how to put that into my review. Doubled the playtime? Tripled? Quadrupled? Even more? Depends on how much you are into the other characters, but for the fans of DMC, this is the most vastly content packed game ever in the series.

I respect those that help a story continue living, and Transmissions: Element 120 is but one of many that continues the Half-Life story, and it does it well, though it is much like enjoying a slice of cake. To short to feel full, but sweet and delicious enough in its action to leave you sated.
=Gameplay=
Gameplay works off of the Half-Life source engine system, a system that, for the most part has not changed, and thus, like an m1911, it is one that works towards its own advantages and does so very well.
+Story+
I enjoyed the story, though simple, it continues the feel of the Half-Life world, and its distopian future, including further elements of resistance members fighting it out far and wide across the country, and maybe even the world.
+Additions-

You know I usually can find nearly at least one good thing about a game but here I cannot. Revolution Ace is a Vertical shooter in the vein of Raiden,Aleste and Star Solider...Too Bad the game play isn't even a speck towards those awesome shooters...let me explain why "Revolution Ace" sucks. First off,  The weapons you have are super weak and too expensive. Personally at first I thought it was neat to be able to experiment with what works for the player and purchase weapons to wreck havoc on enemies. However here is the fatal flaw with this is once you purchase and item and it happens to suck,you can sell it and get next to nothing back for that weapon and you better hope you have more funds because if you sold your old weapon to get the new one that you thought would work....You're screwed to the point were you will have to delete your game and start ALL over again. The weapons absolutely suck and This is bull*#$*! I had to restart 3 times to get anywhere and the more I play the game,the more I hate it because the balance between enemy and player are too great, the enemy is simply too strong!
Who thought the enemy movement games development was a good idea? Their TOO ERRATIC! What makes a vertical/horizontal shooter fun is the set enemy patterns so that the player can memorize and use a manuever to ensure survival and keep going. You can't do that here. All the enemies comes from all sides and pummel you with bullets and given the weak♥♥♥♥♥weapons and the prices given, Your defeat happens far too often (Some will say it's because I suck but I've beaten Raiden and Raiden 2 on hard with 7 credits!). This game is one of the best Diablo-esque games there is and in some ways is actually better than diablo! I've only put in 20 hours so far but after this short of a time, I can tell you it has tons of replayability, insane modding support to extend that even further, a very long and thought-out story, and pets! Now, pets may seem like a stupid thing to point out but they help solve the inventory you face in every game of this genre. This game also has that problem, but your pet can sell your stuff in town and bring you back the profit.
Now, there are some problems with this game. Multiplayer is somewhat empty in that there are very few massive servers so don't expect this to be an mmo or anything of that sort. The skill amount is also extremeley overwhelming in the fact that there definitley isnt enough hotbar space for all the abilities you may or may not get. This game is also no longer being updated by the devs, not that it's neccesary with the amount of content and the mod support. I whole-heartedly reccomend this game with all of my heart; as you play this game you'll encounter things that you didn't last time or references to things that will make you laugh. There are also a lot of awesome, and 'explosive' moments. If you buy this game and get bored just download the SynergiesMOD, its almost as expansive as the game itself and at least doubles the amount of content.

TL;DR: In Mankind Divided, the previous storywriter (Mary DeMarle) is replaced by a team of 15 year olds, highfiving eachother whenever another uninspired idea popped up at group sessions.
Recommended for fans of the series only!
***
Human Revolution is one of my all time favourites (as in overall top 10). So it saddens me to say that Mankind Divided is far, far away from it predecessor. It lacks the tempo, the powerful narrative, the thrilling story that kept us digging for more and more. It simply lacks the same DNA that made Human Revolution so unique.
This time around, players are stuck in the same area (Prague) for most of the game. No more travelling the globe and seeing new and exotic cities (except maybe a few places)... I wont be going into alot of plot details here, but overall the story feels less satisfying compared to HR. Oh, did i mention no more awesome boss fights?
The game is good looking, very much so infact, but lacks the same super-bold artistry and design that made Human Revolution so breathtaking. Theres also alot of cheap repeating, and overall it's clear that the team behind the design aimed for a more... standard'ish look. Take for example the stun-gun. HR had a futuristic 'TRON' like look, while MD went for a standard pistol look, with a silencer. Not gamebreaking, but it really lacks the vision the team behind HR had.
Mankind Divided took me 50 hours to complete on hard, exploring every area, reading every book, email, PS and datafile. HR took me double that (around 100 hours).
Difficulty wise, hard is easy. Especially later on. I took the 100% non-lethal route, and furthermore limited myselfe with no stealth, titan, or any of the new augs actually. And it was still a complete cakewalk. I ended the game with over 100.000 credits and 20'ish unspend praxis kits.
On the bright side, you will be put to some hard choices... well, atleast one or two times during the game... but even those can't make up for the rest. MD pretty much lacks everything that made HR so unique, but atleast retains the core mechanics. So... i'll cut it short here with:
Recommended for fans of the series only.

So I recently finished the title, and let's get my recommendation out of the way right now: I enjoyed it a lot.  I'll definitely be going back to do a proper pacifist run in the near future.  I loved the plot, the big expansive levels, and some of the new augs are so intensely useful they feel almost overpowered (lookin' at you, remote hacking!)
That being said, I have one enormous gripe with the game, to the point where it's almost ruined my opinion of the game: the ending.  What was shipped feels like the great first 1/3 of a much larger, much more ambitious narrative, and while it's a good 1/3, the ending is so sudden and abrupt I was genuinely wondering why they were telling me I unlocked NG+ after the first boss fight.  This abrupt ending also ensures that the story doesn't follow up on any of the multitude of subplots that the game starts, which perhaps angered me the most.  I REALLY wanted to know about certain characters and what's happened in the two years since Human Revolution.  I REALLY wanted to explore the all-aug city of Rabi'ah.  I also just really, really wanted to see Jensen and Aria Argento become aug-buddies.  But nope, none of that pans out in this game.
Maybe in the next game.  Or the DLC.
And that's my main problem with the ending, here, because that's what it feels like; it was deliberately shortened to force folks to buy another game in a few years, or to subscribe to the DLC.  If that wasn't the case, and this is the ending that Eidos/SE envisioned, then I'm just real disappointed.  If the ending shows up in DLC, I'm gonna be livid.

While I don't think the additional content of Special Edition really warranted its own game (it should have been DLC years ago), the extra characters are worth the low purchase price.
Unfortunately, there are no new weapons, no new missions, only a few cutscenes and no new modes over the Vanilla DMC4. Basically what SE is, is 3 extra characters added into Vanilla DMC4. Lady, Trish and Vergil.
Lady offers almost exclusively ranged gameplay (which isn't good in a game like this) but she plays so differently from the others that shes worth a go. She is playable in Nero's missions.
Trish is mostly a frankensteined moveset from Dante and a couple of Vergil's moves. Her unique mechanic is to throw her Sword for a few seconds and use alternate abilities. She specializes in mass AoE abilities. Playable in Dante's missions.
Vergil is largely his DMC3 moveset with a few ques taken from DmC's version of Vergil. He is so completely broken (in the right hands) that the other 4 characters cannot even come close to his potential. Vergil can clear Legendary Dark Knight missions (which have a staggering amount of enemies) in the same time that other characters take to clear Dante Must Die missions.
At the end of the day, it is still the half completed game that DMC4 was, but the new characters are so much fun to play as and the extra costumes still keep me coming back to Nero and Dante.
My personal recommendation is to new  comers, hardcore fans, or to those who never really put time into vanilla DMC4 because the entire roster of "Team DMC" is here and every single one of them is awesome to play as.

It's the superior version. Slightly less optimized than its original. With pasted on characters, doubled credits, and everything you love about the game intact.
Lady is the mage character of the game, and vergil is the cannon character. They do not have interchangable stories. So prepare to repeat the game 3 times to have some proper level and character selection. Vergil does everything alone, Trish and lady have one, and Nero and dante have another.
Playing as Vergil without spamming will in short, Make you appreciate every other character in the game. He's not bad, but his worthwhile combos take a very long time to complete, and almost every air move in his disposal requires you to change weapons to maintain style. His combos have been expanded upon, albiet in drawn out ways. tons of delay combos, hold combos, and teleporting. Personally, Someone who teleports shouldn't have combos that have you all over the place. Whoever was in charge of his moveset seemed to have decided that he should play like dante with a gimped trickster style that is tremendously offensive if you avoid using combos that will actually net you a score... Spamming flip kicks, chase stingers, and helm breakers will do massive damage, just as spamming the yamato air slash did in dmc3se. But will give you poor scores. So basically, playing just as vergil did as a boss in dmc3 is possible, but is tossed as a valid style. Good thing about that is that you won't have to stand in front of a s rank stylish candle for an hour mapping out the time where you can repeat your combo, Bad thing is that so much of these moves can do so well, if they weren't hidden behind pause moves and a teleport system that is less reliable than jumping out of a combo. You will enjoy it, but not without seeing his potential for actually being a vergil character, and not dante locked at trickster level 9000.
Vergil is probably the only character anyone will have a problem with that wasn't already in the game. fumbling at bonus stages without a double jump, getting hit relying on teleport, Beowulf being a gilgamesh clone. To be honest, I'm dissapointed to be amount of content that was added to the game compared to the original game. However, If you haven't purchased the original DMC4, and look for a adrenaline-filled hack-and-slash, this is a game for you. Even the difficulty is the same as before - well, somewhat.
You might be wondering, why am I dissapointed to this to this game, since my reason for it is the content. Well, allow me to explain:
First off, while the new characters bring new life to the game, all they did was they created Vergil, Lady and Trish, nothing else. Capcom didn't even bother making new levels, new bosses OR new combat soundtracks for new characters. Trish, Lady and Vergil's mechanics sure all solid, but my interest well apart at the time I was doing my first playthrough as Vergil. If you have watched the intro of Vergil, you can hear the soundtrack playing in the background that highly resembles the second fight against Vergil in DMC3. THIS SONG AINT HEARD ANYWHERE ELSE. The only ones you hear as Vergil and the rest of the new face smashers are the battle themes of Nero, Dante, and of course the songs you hear in boss battles.
How about the good things?
The combat system is still there with more stuff you can pull out since new head smashers were introduced, and the deepest and -maybe- the hardest to master Dante's combat style and it's also one of the most enjoyable ways to play. Vergil's playstyle is also a thing I enjoy lot - nothing beats the feeling when you nail that Judgement Cut final at the end of huge combo.
Difficulties. More difficulties to choose from. Well.. only one but it's bloody awesome and it's called Legendary Dark Night. More enemies to beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of but you will get destroyed if you haven't pumped enough adrenaline/coffeine/Dorritoes/Dew in your body when facing of large hordes that can fill up your whole screen.
Besides of music, the missions.. they aren't different in anyway. You will encounter same enemies in same missions in same places as in the original, Nero/Dante story. Even when starting the story of Lady/Trish, It could have began outside of the Devil May Cry.
However, even with these complaints, I recommend those to purchase this game if they don't already own the original version. If you do own the original, I'd consider buying this when it comes out for sale, if this ever does
Well.. you can always buy this game because it has Vergil.... Right? Are you now motivated?.
Also, DmC's Vergil story should've been something Capcom should have checked out. While it's not perfect, it's certainly NOT in the same levels as when playing the Dante's line.
Cheers

This is a fantastic little RTS. It's fairly simple to pick up and play, yet throughly addicting. The single player campaign, while perhaps not strong in story, ramps up the challenge very quickly, yet in a way that lets you become prepared for the next challenge. Sometimes, it feels almost like a puzzle; one ends up needing to evaluate each and every move/attack you make, lest some mutation occour that makes the bugs able to attack your holdings before you can respond to it. And, trust me, you WILL be forced to respond to these mutations, especially if the AI is set up to pick mutations. Some of them work so well together that it makes the mission nearly impossible to beat, but that's part of the fun, too. It's a solid game and I have recommended it to numerous friends.
Also, if you like Warhammer 40,000 and ever wondered what it would be like to command troops during a Tyranid invasion, this will give you a pretty good idea of what that would be like. Just saying.

In my book, this game has the same problem as Enstranged: It looks absolutely beautiful, but doesn't know what it wants to be.
The light-based stealth gameplay in the beginning sets the game up to be a stealth shooter, then you obtain the gravity concussion gun, which introduces what might be an element of puzzle solving to the game, which you think would go great with the stealth until the whole light-dark concept is abandoned in the next chapter. The next chapter does however, focuses more on the gravity concussion gun 'puzzles,' which consist of you breaking doors open, outrunning a zombie horde, and jumping onto one roof. Then comes the final level, where the game reverts back to vanilla half life 2 as you fight a handful of combine soldiers and three striders (Which the gravity concussion gun has zero effect on, what fun!)
Do I reccomend it? Yes, because this makes a nice concept that is fun to play with. I hope an SDK and steam workshop intergration is added in the future, so mappers can make their own levels revolving around the new concept.

Well, just got done playing this mod, gotta say. It was pretty impressive.
The Gameplay:
The gameplay is similar, if not exactly like half life 2 (and the episodes). However, this mod adds a few gimicks which I believe added to the gameplay. First, was the zombies in the dark, which was a neat concept. However, I feel like it could have been exicuted better. In fact in one part of the level you can just sit on something, flash your flashlight a few times, and just beat them all to death with a crowbar. Although that may have just been intentional. While I felt this concept was unique it suffered one crucial flaw. You only use this gimick once, and after that, the game just forgets it ever existed. It just dropped it, which didn't make it memorable. Although unique definatly, it was easily forgetable and at the point I began writing this review I finally remembered it.
The same can't be said for the next part though. This game's version of the Gravity Gun. I felt like this was exicuted wonderfully. I had a blast with it, quite literally. In fact I found myself using it a lot. And thats where the problem lies in this. You want to use it more than anything else. Its very overpowered. You could say it takes the same AUX power as the sprint, but half the time in this game you aren't sprinting to begin with, so you can basically use it over and over. Another feature of this, is the rocket jumping mechanic. I felt that this was absolutely perfect. Being a pretty big TF2 fan I was happy to see this in the game. Although I feel like the rocket jumping could have been more implied. As in, players being able to figure out that its a feature. I found it by complete accident, it isn't very implied that it exists, and thats my main problem. In fact, in one part its required to proceed. If you don't get it the first time, tough♥♥♥♥♥♥ figure it out.
Now lets move on to The Aesthetics:
The looks of this game are fantastic, I dare say they look better than Half-Life 2, and thats saying a lot. The maps had plenty of things to look at. There were some parts that were somewhat bland, like the underground areas, but even then, those still looked rather impressive. I liked the idea of the glow in the dark paint. I thought that was pretty memorable, which we could have seen more throughout the rest of the game. But just like the zombie gimick it was completely abandoned. Which really upset me. The QR codes scattered among the walls was a fun addition, that was only native to the underground areas. Which half the fun content in this mod were at the begining levels, and quickly died off when the protagonist gets the new gravity gun. But I digress. The Aesthetic looks aboslutly great, and I think any self respecting Half-Life fan should give this mod a try.
The Finale (Boss level if you can call it that, also spoilers):
The final "boss" of this game, is a group of combine soldiers, and with your newly aquired gravity gun, that should be pretty easy, right? ♥♥♥♥ NO, INSTEAD, DITCH THE GRAVITY GUN, WE'RE USING RPG'S NOW! I get it, the Gravity gun would be too easy to use on the striders. But the use of the RPG is just dumb. You have to find more ammo for the RPG scattered about the level. While striders and combine soldiers are shooting you from everywhere. I think this is more of a cluster♥♥♥♥ rather than a boss fight. At this point maybe use of the gravity gun could be used for something useful. Granted you still need to rocket jump to some areas in the stage. But could the Gravity gun at least have stunned them for a while? Like, to maybe get some time to find more rockets? Because they are on roof tops, in locked doors and some are just out in the open. After defeating all the Striders, the GMan appears, and says something. I don't remember what it was. But it was something interesting, you'll have to see for yourself.
The Final Verdict:
Whats the verdict? I think Transmissions: Element 120 is a well polished mod, with some fun mechanics, and great level design. While incredibly short, it is still a fun game none the less. I think that any self respecting Half-Life fan can find it enjoyable and fun. I sure had fun jumping around and killing zombies in the dark! Highly Recommended!

Good game with a terrible community. I've played this game since the Steam release, played in most servers/regions, and have seen so many people come and go. The game has been abandoned by the original developers and sold to a company that, so far, has only made sure the servers stay up and running. This, however, does not stop the community from  playing. The good matches that you can get into between legitimate players and games with friends are the only reason I can still enjoy this game.
The combat is great, movement is fluid, glitches (for the most part) and unintended merchanics add to the gameplay, and good matches can be very thrilling. The game isn't impossible to learn, but many new players make the mistake of thinking this is a melee game. Good movement and aim will get you farther than anything else.
Practice rooms also exist and provide most players with what they need to learn the game, if they are willing to ask. That being said, it is also possible to simply learn the game by just constantly queuing normals and base everything off what you experience in matches. More experienced players in this game often play together, but there are many who solo queue just to balance out the matchmaking. You will fight the same people often, no matter which modes you play, and most people know who each other are.
The biggest issue is that the game has no anti-cheating measures and the community is filled with players that hack, or are willing to party with those who do. That being said, there's still a good amount of players who play fair. You can still get good games more often than not by arranging premade games between groups or from just queuing, but many hackers in this game go out of their way to ruin the experience for others.
Overall, the game itself is fine, but can take a while to get the hang of. If you have decent aim and learn the movement mechanics, you'll be fine. If you run around trying to melee better players, you won't have much fun. At the time of writing this, I have the most kills in ranked/normal match queue at almost 70,000 and roughly 3,400 hours of playtime. Although a lot of that time is waiting in queue, I have experienced and tried pretty much everything the game has to offer. I hated this game at first and can now say it is the most enjoyable game I have ever played. GunZ 2 is, at the very least, worth trying.

I run Torchlight II on Linux (Ubuntu 14.04 LTS 64 Bit) with and AMD APU integrated graphics and all settings maxed out at 1920x1080: it runs very smooth (even though it just uses 1 core) and looks great! Only when dozens of enemies are fighting with me, the graphics sometiomes slows down - but not by stuttering but by some "slow-motion" that slows everything down but very smoothly.
The game itself has more to offer than fighting and solving simple (or harder) puzzles. It's wrapped into a bigger story that is told by computer characters that you meet (or miss ...). You can choose between several characters and companions, little pets that you can also morph into strange creatures by feeding them with different fishes. You gain more and more power & abilities the more experience you have. You can buy items or gain them by killing enemies that you can equip your character with. The hundreds of misc clothes, helmets, weapons are awesome and your character can look very coll in many different outfits.
The isometric 3D world can also be zoomed in and out with the mouse wheel. The world get bigger and bigger and the enemies stronger and stronger. You have to setup your characters equipment and abilities good enough to win some boss battles. These battles are not too hard, as the AI is not too sophisticated. But you will have a hard time battle those monsters by just blindly firing/slaying your weapon.
It's a good timewaster with good graphics, nice story and lots of fighting. And it looks great in Linux!

So much like Diablo that you sometimes wonder where they weren't sued to ♥♥♥♥ for copywrite! Torchlight 2 is actually a just as good game. Although more comicy and friendly, it's not a serious nor does it have a lot of features that Diablo has (Especially Diable 3).
You get to choose from 4 classes;
- Engineer, who gets to summon a few robots to assist him and the team. Can exell in 2 handed melee, weapon and shield, or cannon. Engineer is both a tank and support, healing the team and shielding them.
- Embermage, as the name implies, this is the one who throws fireballs, snowballs, or batteries... I mean thunder, at his enemies. Comes equipt with wand or staff, and a veriety of spells. Great at dealing with crowds and singular targets. Remember, when a mage gets angry he throws a fireball, when he gets really angry he beats his enemies with a very large stick (the staff).
- Outlander, the rootiest, tootiest and the shootiest of the group. The Outlander is at his best when holding a gun... Or two... Or a bow... Basically at range. Although they can be honest to go up close or use some spells. They're not the strongest, but by far the most accurate.
- Beserker, it's all in the name. Run in screaming your enemies to death and you mash their heads in. Use knuckle dusters to deal with many enemies at once or claws to eat at one oponent at a time. They are masters at duel-weilding, but don't let that stop you from using a 2-handed instead, they're still just as strong!
Plus, what wins this game for me, is the fact that every character can get a pet. This ranges from Cats, to dragon creatures, to British Bulldogs, to Wolves, to the Headcrab from Half Life. They can carry things and even go on shopping runs for you and sell your gear for you whilst back in town. They always fight for you and will die if need be, but they will always come back to life, and you can give them health potions, so there's no need to cry when they go down.
It's a much friendlier game for all ages too, don't be afraid to give your kid a go! Unless you don't have kids, in which case you should be questioning who is on your lap at this moment of time. Travel from area to area, fighting the different monsters along the way. Level up your characters as you do so too, all the way to 100! Learn new spells and master the skill trees, it really is a game for everone to enjoy.

I really suck at RTS, but this game has just the perfect scope for me. Few units, but a lot of choices to make. Should I invest in different soldier weapons, turrets or buy the ability to call in airstrikes? What hive should I capture next to gain the most advantage? Later on in the same game I might sell the airstrike in favor of a minigunner or sniper, and so on.
As you play, the enemies mutate and become different and you suddenly need to adapt your strategies.
Small bite-sized (15-30 minutes for me) levels with a lot of depth, and when you play the Campaign mode you earn money to unlock new upgrades between each mission even if you were to fail, so it always feels like you're making progress.
The music is wonderfully thumpy and deep, and I'd recommend the game just for that even if all else sucked, which it doesn't.

A suprisingly well made blend between your standard rts and tower defense genre. Infested planet's premise is that you command a team of marines on a mission to wipe all bugs from "I can't believe it isn't Klendathu".
Pros
-Gameplay with a simple mission, but a great degree of freedom in accomplishing it
-AI that seeming reacts to your style in how it mutates(upgrades) which makes for a good challenge
-Simple yet deep tech tree that is open to the player and allows for easy blending of equipment and tech for different strategies
-A custom mission maker which lets you set match parameters to whatever you like( starting marine number, number of hives, alien ferocity, etc...)
Cons
-As the matches heat up and your number of bases and marines increase it can be easy to start to lose track of everything(and the AI will abuse that)
All in all, this games meets my golden rule of one hour of fun for every dollar paid, a great way to have some fun when you want to play a strategy game, but don't feel like doing anything that needs more than an hour.

At first glance, this one seems to be nothing more than eye candy. Don't be fooled, this is an excellent puzzle-platformer. The game controls smoothly and never uses the same puzzles twice, most of which tend to have multiple ways of solving them. I wish I could say the same about the bosses, but they all get recycled at some point. The hack-n-slash elements are extremely basic and, to me, underwhelming, but don't let that stop you from getting this game.
The story stands on it's own merits, for the most part. The only thing you need to know from the first game is that the Trine is an artifact with a mind of it's own, guiding the heroes and reviving them when needed. The rest of the story is fairly standard, and if you find the hidden clues, the big twist is foreshadowed.
Of course, the graphics are incredible, especially for a game that first came out in 2011. All of the environments are vivid and colorful, and character movements are lively and detailed. The soundtrack is whimsical and memorable and generally does a great job of setting the mood while also standing well on it's own. The voice-acting is fairly standard and somewhat lacking in emotion, but it does it's job.
Perhaps my biggest complaint is that as you get more skills, the regular game gets a little too easy to break. Other than that and the overly basic combat, I cannot recommend this game enough. Every playthrough will bring something different to the table and will always have something for everyone.

Blood Dragon is a great experiment by Ubisoft, a nostalgia trip back to the 80's as a total conversion of Far Cry 3.  It feels like a blend of Tron, Terminator, and a typical 80's action movie wrapped into the Far Cry island.  At the same time, the game parodies modern games with simple repetitive missions and a long, mandatory tutorial that your character complains about while you do it.
The game is a lot of fun, though I'm glad it's a small title.  The nostalgia trip only gets you so far and certain things like looting corpses gets tiring by repeating the same long animation every time.  The bad 80's action hero one-liners get quite tiring after a while too.
It took me about 8 hours to complete everything available in the game, which I think is pretty reasonable for the price and a good length for this sort of game.  Any longer and I don't think I'd want to finish it, though at this length it is quite enjoyable.  If you think you'd enjoy the nostalgia trip or just want some more open world fps action, this is definitely a good title to pick up.

Even though it looks and feels like Mankind Divided is a Deus Ex game, it rapidly becomes apparent that something is missing. Or maybe a few things are missing even.
First of all, the scale of the game's story has been deliberately reduced. If you do all the side quests, it's still about the same length as Human Revolution, but rather than touring Hong Kong and whatnot you are limited to one city for the entire game (Prague). You aren't really fighting a worldwide global conspiracy here, but rather just making some chess moves in a longterm game of influences and such. And well... that's okay I guess, but it feels like a step down from the previous installment, ya know?
Second, the game's lacking a certain human element. In DX1, you had your brother Paul, Tracer Tong, pilot dude and Alex who weren't just JC's support crew, but rather his friends. Human Revolution had Malik, Frank and even Sarif who Jensen had real personal connections to. This has... uh. Well, a black lady whose identity and presence in the game is not adequately explained.
I still love Adam to death as a character, but it feels like this whole plot is just him putting in his 9-5. He doesn't feel like he's really involved in this story at a personal level because none of his friends are here.
Third, it doesn't feel like the world is very organic. I remember in the first Deus Ex I looked for three or four ways to approach the weapons dealer Mouse, enjoying how each method got a different reaction and different prices from the guy. In this, it felt much more stiff. You complete missions by either being stealthy or shooting everyone. Anything you do beyond that is sort of ignored.
For instance: Two cops are arresting a neighbour in some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t anti-aug crackdown. I took them both down and tried to free my neighbour, but... well, I couldn't. The game didn't expect that so it has zero consequences or impact on the game.
Same thing goes when I see a bunch of augs being held by police later that night. I can't free those guys apparently, even though I had a subquest to free another group of dudes just 10 minutes before. Those NPCs don't have names I guess so they're deemed Not Important.
Now, did I like the game anyway? Sure did. The stealthing is fun, Adam Jensen is a superb character and the plot is quite intriguing. But while I appreciate it for what it is, one cannot help but wish this had been something more.

1.) Microtransactions are OPTIONAL. Giving people the OPTION to enhance their characters should mean absolutely nothing to you if you don't want to use them. Is that a better world? I strongly disagree.
3.) These extra things you can purchase optionally (you can even wait until you know you like the game) are paying money to the people who made it. If you like the game enough to want more of it, why are you being pissy about the people who made it getting paid a little extra? A worthy sequel. Let's address some of the complaints. People keep complaining about microtransactions, the game's length, the game's story and bad performance.
1. Microtransactions don't affect me, as I don't buy them. The game does not gimp you in terms of credits, weapons, ammo or Praxis points. After robbing Prague, I was swimming in credits, weapons, ammo and Praxis points. The microtransactions are there for people who think games are disposable—one-time deals, play it once very quickly, toss it and move onto the next. If you're that type of player, you'll love the microtransactions. If you're not, if you're the kind of player who approaches a game in a careful, methodical manner, you won't be affected.
2. The game's length is perfectly fine. I played 47.6 hours and beat it once, doing all the side missions. Sure, some of that was spent soaking in the atmosphere of the city, but isn't that expected? You've got a great little world to explore, so why wouldn't you take your time and explore the entirety of it? People who rush through with little care will get what they put in. As expressed at the end of point 1, if you're the type of player who explores and likes to get lost in a strange new world, you will likely spend a lot more hours than the rushers. Sure, the game could use another hub, but at the end of the day is that make-or-break material? Hardly. Prague is big and diverse. And you'll visit other locations for missions. The Swiss Alps looks damn gorgeous when you get that little time outside.
3. The game's plot is, again, perfectly fine. People who complain about the ending, or who claim that nothing happens, obviously weren't paying attention. There's so many little details that progress the series, little things that move towards the first game's plot and themes. Depending on how you do one side mission, you'll get a little bit of info at the end of the game that states the group moved to France and formed Silhouette. Remember Silhouette? If you don't, you have no right to complain, because you don't even pay attention to the games you ♥♥♥♥♥ about. The events of the game are major, but you obviously won't think so if you think of them in the all-too-common mentality these days of what a "big event" is. No, you won't hijack an airplane and take out the terrorists who are trying to crash it into the summit meeting and kill all the countries' leaders. Instead, you'll attempt to thwart an Illuminati-sanctioned plan to suppress the augmented minority. Hack the computers, read the emails, read the datapads, pay attention. There's so much here, but you have to dig deep to find it all. Just like the first game.

There are far superior forms of AA to utilize, so if you need your precious AA at 4k resolutions (why you would even need AA at a resolution that high, I'll never know), choose something other than MSAA.

I love geese and I love ducks -- however, generally speaking, geese are definitely a lot meaner. In this game, you are a lone duck pitted against an increasingly large (and mean) "gang" of nazi-geese that will not rest until they have all of your eggs. Your objective is to collect as many eggs as possible "for glory". The geese do not make this easy, they are always right on your♥♥♥♥♥ attempting to take any eggs you may have collected. As long as you are alive and collecting eggs your score will increase, regardless of the geese snatching your eggs -- but you can also take your eggs back from the geese. If you collide with a goose and you have less eggs, you will lose a life.
My only experience so far is in Classic Mode. To unlock other modes you have to complete objectives (example: Score 200,000 in Classic Mode to unlock the next mode of play). The controls are really simple, and you can even use a controller if you want to, but I found that I ended up preferring my keyboard for this one. The duck can move and "turbo" (shift on keyboard) but speed will not save you from losing a life if you collide with a goose while carrying less eggs. In terms of the field of play, the top and bottom of the map are locked but the sides will loop you back around, kind of like Pac-Man.
I guess a few people complained about the "flashing colors" in this game -- I on the other hand, really appreciate how the randomized palette lends to the overall chaos. The music and sound effects are more than adequate and complete the overall package. This game is great to play if you only have a few minutes but it's also potentially addicting. I expect that I will probably play a lot more of this game and it only costs $0.99 (but I got it on sale).

I'm pretty sure many people would have similar feedback about this game, especially for those who have played the first GunZ the Duel, and many comparisons would be made there. I didn't play this game much to be honest and in fact, this review came late: I played this game last year when it first launched.
1. As before, ping plays a big role, and at that time, I was playing in Australia. The drawback was that my network was quite terrible and the fact that I could not connect to servers outside Oceania meant that I could not play with some of my friends from other games. Some of the "solutions" were to use VPN, but honestly it was a terrible mix anyway.
Comparison to GunZ the Duel: It didn't matter where you are playing from because you are all connected to the same server (official servers = ijji and Aeria back then, or others would be private servers). Old GunZ 1: Second Duel 0
2. Movements are bloody rigid.. HONESTLY. It just feels like a simple run and shoot game. It helps if you have a spray weapon in case of you or your opponent lagging, Melee is now worse...but then again a gun should always win vs melee...
Comparison with old GunZ: Precisely because movements can be exploited, it makes the character movement more fluid.  It makes the game REALLY FAST-PACED, not to mention many finger-breaking moments (I'm sure everyone knows what I mean) as compared to the sequel. Old GunZ 2: Second Duel 0
3. Storyline. Now this is where the Second Duel sort of triumphs over the previous game because the previous game has no particular storyline. Old GunZ 2: Second Duel 1
4. Customisation. The Second Duel is all about classes. You can't configure your weapon loadout a lot, so if you picked a class you don't like, you gotta start over.
Comparison with old GunZ: When you first create your character, it allows you to select "classes" with different loadout. However, you can customise it to something out of the ordinary, meaning players have more freedom to explore the choices they are best suited to. Did I also mention you can also add elemental colours and attributes to your melee weapon? Old GunZ 3: Second Duel 1
Overall... I plead Steam to host the old GunZ: The Duel, please!

Transmissions: Element 120 is a game set in the Half-Life 2 universe, according to the website "at a mysterious date & location after the events of Half-Life : Episode 2". It's not just another mod however, this game offers something new to play with. It replaces the 'Zero Point Energy Field Manipulator' with another type of gun, which shoots strong pulses of pure force. You can use it to jump taking no damage from what I noticed, but it can be used to damage enemies directly. Another new element that the game introduces is that certain enemies can't see in the dark, and to top it all of the game makes numerous inprovements to the Source Engine to make the experience a complete one.
The game tries to sell using the phrase "Where are you? Why have you been sent?". To me, they totally sold that. From the start I wanted to know where I was, and as I progressed through the (obivously) linear path I became more and more confused as to where I was, and why I was there. The game tries to one-up the Source Engine by making it look slightly better and giving it better AI and physics systems. I deffinitely did notice it looking a lot nicer and a lot more modern, and the physics where something I never experienced before.
Once again you wake up in a train, wondering where you are and how you got there. The world looks the way you would expect, dark and dirty. As you progress you make your way through tunnels that have some sort of writing in them, in ink that can only be seen in the dark. You meet some zombies and learn that they can't actually see you in the dark tunnels of the cities sewers. You walk along and meet some turrets, painted and placed by rebels. Never the less, they shoot you. But luckely, turrets can't see in the dark either. You progress further and end up in some sort of lab, where you find the force-pulse gun. The game now opens up to you.
When I first got the gun, I spend about 10 minutes just shooting at random things. Making a huge mess of the lab I just entered. For some reason, I was angry at whomever put me in this situation but making a mess of everything helped me rest my anger. Everytime I got to use the gun to jump up to something, I was surprised to find what I found. The game never felt like it was out to get me, the game just wanted me to enjoy the sights and also play around with the new engine and gameplay mechanics. One thing I was sad to discover was that the game did not allow me to shoot out the lights, even though one of the core new gameplay elements was hiding in the dark.
The game does suffer from some downsides, like being able to jump to area's you were never supposed to go to or having some props not being actuall physics props, but for the most part the game feels incredibly dynamic and real. Some puzzles where hard to solve (most of them were just figuring out where to go or what to shoot in order to progress) and the game might confuse you at times, but for it's incredibly low price of nothing and it's short length, it is worth to just try and play. Do note that the game has some downright bugs in it, which are small and neglectable.

Revolution Ace
Arcade Jet Fighter
Laser Guided Games
Laser Guided Games
is an arcade jet fighter game developed and published by Laser Guided Games.
The game, developed with Unreal Engine 3, looks just fine: there is a good amount of particle effects, enemy variety and high-quality textures, but, as with many of these games, the background gets really repetitive really fast. Still, the performance is quite good, with solid 60fps even with multiple explosions on the screen.
You control a customizable ship, and your objective is to get to the end of each map and defeat the boss. There are two types of attack: one to destroy flying vehicles and bombs, the other to destroy land vehicles and enemy bases. You can also acquire powerups and new weapons (as well as ship upgrades)through the shop using the money and XP that you gain at the end of each level.
If you like this genre, you will love this game: it is formulaic but fun. If you never liked this type of games when they were popular in the arcades, I find it hard that you will enjoy it now.
The game is very challenging on every difficulty setting, and it can get really frustrating the more you play it: sometimes dodging enemy fire seems impossible, and some of the boss fights will require more luck than actual skills.
The sound effects are very good and each weapon and ship has its unique sounds. The soundtrack fits the game and, while it is forgettable, it does give you enough strength to keep going.
Even though there is small amount of Steam achievements (only 19), multiple difficulty settings, online leaderboards, local and online multiplayer will keep you coming back to this game more than once.
While it lacks in a story and the gameplay is very formulaic, there is much to enjoy in this game and you will spend mutliple hours trying to improve your ship and get higher scores. I highly recommend this game to fans of the genre and to those looking for a challenge. If you are new to the genre, I recommend waiting for it to go on sale.

This is a game to be played! A game that is both simple in design and gameplay, yet heavy on story and control as well. You are two brothers, looking to save their father's life. To do this, they embark on a journey, where the two brothers must be one. One cannot perform without the other. And you don't swap between the two, you control them both AT THE SAME TIME. And you would think that would require amazing skills, but all you need is a controller, and good hand/eye coordination, as well as paying attention. The graphics are very sweet, colorful, and brings worlds to life, as well as what you interact with it. The only thing you need to also keep in mind, is that this game is very short. That 3.1 hours on record is not what I've played so far, it's what took me to beat this game. But unlike games that are more about cinematic simulation like Everyone Goes to the Rapture, Gone Home, and Dear Esther; Brothers is constantly having you do things, with really simple gameplay that requires a good bit of thinking since you are using 2 characters at the same time.
This is a true marvel of simple/complex in almost all aspects. TotalBiscuit once declared this, his game of the year winner, and he considers this, to be favorite game, of all time. Over his former one, which was Deus Ex. I don't think this one trumps my favorite, which is Mass Effect; but if you see this game on sale, get it without thinking twice. You will not regret it.
Pricetag is a bit steep for 3 hours of game, but this offers more than any walking simulator does. Pretty much all of them. But that is my opinion.

Now, I'm going to review this rather critically, and it will certainly spoil some of the game's features, and possibly plot.
This game is well done. I'm assuming it was designed by one guy using Game Maker Studio. I thoroughly enjoyed the game. The gameplay mechanics were okay. I really liked the physics used in the glide ability. The uniqueness behind each level kept my attention. The soundtrack was only really three tracks, but I'll assume the dev wasn't very good with composing pieces? Anyways, the game was colorful, fun, and well worth the 37 minutes I put into it.
However, it isn't exactly perfect. Many issues and bugs were present, as well as recurring events that I found rather obnoxious.
Sometimes enemies, specifically the jumping spider, jumped into spikes, making progression easier. Not that I'm complaining, but it just takes a bit away from the difficulty. I noticed some quirky texture work at some points, but this is most likely one person who made the game, so I won't criticize too harshly. I found the boss tracks rather unfitting, and for the first boss fight, the music only works because the boss is a snake. On the topic of snakes, the snake boss was ridiculously easy. Both times I faced it I defeated it with no issue. Whereas the other boss enemy, the UFO, is another story altogether. The UFO boss wasn't too difficult, it was more annoying and tedious. Several factors played into the UFO fights not being too enjoyable. Firstly, and arguably the most obnoxious, the damage hitbox on the UFO is a square. I have worked with Game Maker Studio before, it is not difficult to mask the hitbox to fit the object's sprite. I call that either forgetful editing, or lazy design. Another issue was the fact that the UFO's health bar regenerates every time you die. This makes the battle all the more tedious, especially in Level 21, when the boss has MORE health. And I did not get hit by the beams it shot unless I was trying to attack it, which bothers me that I have to time the jump, but I'll let that slide, seeing as it was obviously intended for a more intricate fight.
All in all, I give this game a
7/10

I'm a massive fan of the Devil May Cry series. I've at least finished each game once or twice, even the reboot. I loved every game, yet Devil May Cry 4 was always a big favourite of mine. When I heard that the special edition was being released, I got super excited and pre-ordered it straight away.

There are a lot of things to unlock in this game which can take a long time to do, such as complete all of the difficulties (which I found almost impossible to do since I was so bad at the game). It's still a very enjoyable game to me even if I played for hours and hours for each day of the week.
I can't say that there is anything bad in the game. The game itself runs very smoothly and I haven't caught any bugs in the 1000 hours I have played in my life.
If you're a big fan of the Devil May Cry series and isn't sure whether it's worth buying this again but in the special edition OR you're just a big fan of hack and slash games, I definitely recommend this game to you and I guarentee you that you will love it.

Fun gameplay, with the kind of stealth and non-lethal options we've come to expect from Deus Ex. It in fact expands on the non-lethal options, including even a Typhoon mode which is nonlethal.
Many Deus Ex games up to this point have been better at disguising the linear nature of their respective stories; this game doesn't perform that particular bit of prestidigitation as well as some of its forebears.
You may find the obvious linearity as opposed to subtle linearity upsetting. It didn't bother me, as I've found all Deus Ex games tend to exist in a model of the illusion of choice. I've never had a decision in a Deus Ex game have any impact on the next game, and rarely am I faced with a extremely serious, diametric choice within the game either. In fact, in this game, there are three distinct points at which you must make what are rather significant choices in the game, resulting in life and death consequences (beyond simply lethal vs nonlethal gameplay). I won't share the details beyond a very broad comment of how you have to weigh some rather serious ethical theories at least three different times. There are also sufficient side-quests to fill out your experience moreso than I found true for Invisible War, for example.
The game ends... Abruptly. It seems as if there were some very strange choices made at the publishing end of the process, or perhaps a deadline encroached and hard decisions had to be made. I didn't expect it to end when it did, and I was rather disappointed by it.
A disappointing ending does not a bad game make, in my opinion, and even in being disappointing it was still not terrible. I'd give the ending a C, maybe a C+. Not awful, not great, just average. In my opinon, the rest of the game deserves a B or B+. I wouldn't fail a research paper for having a poor summary, I won't fail a game for having a lackluster ending.

Did you ever hear of the tragedy of RWBY: Grimm Eclipse?
The game started life as a hack and slash indie game based solely around the Red Trailer, but had since been picked up by Rooster Teeth and made into an official game. While I enjoy the series immensly and think it is a fantastic story, I can't help but simply revile the game. RWBY: Grimm Eclipse keeps the hack and slash Dynasty Warriors type of gameplay which I can assume it carried over from the original indie version, in addition toa dding all new things to it.
There's a new story which places this game between volume one and two, new gameplay, more chaarcters, a DLC I reviewed seperatly (I will not review the costume DLC but I will mention them in this review) and you know what this game does with all of that? Absoloutly
This review may change depending on what Rooster Teeth games does with it.
- Back in the day, the characters models didn't look all that great, I recall them being cartoony like in the series, but over time they were fleshed out and now they look amazing. Although I still can't help but feel that Ruby looks like a porceline doll.
- A lot of the artwork in this game has been done very well, although not as great as Volume cover art, which is a shame. Althought, the art style used in this game only compliments a few of the charcters, Yang and Nora have a much more cartoony look than the other character artwork, and are the only characters I feel could have been drawn better on the selection screen.
- This game employs a hack-and-slash Dynasty Warriors style gameplay which never changes throughout the course of the game. Almost every level but two ends the same way, you come to a big open space with a lone object at its center which you msut protect from four waves of Grimm. The only different one sinvovle pushing a cart to beat a time-limit, and the last one is a boss fight, but yous till have to fight your way through four waves of annoying opponants before hitting it.
- A friend bought this game for me way back when, before the combat overhaul, and back then it was well done, you had the standard attack, right click was shoot and I think Q was still used for the Ult attack, but I don't remember now. Anyone who has played the game back then will have mentioned in their reviews that the combat, as it stands now, is a major step back, and one of the poorest decision put into this games development.
- Music is largely fine, however, there's nothing new that I know of, save for the end credits song. Although there is nothing new, I do still enjoy hearing the soundtrack, especially the volume one music. I, however, think that the wave battles should have had some fo the major songs in plece of the generic combat music, e.g.
and
- There really is no way to defend against threats, it's more like a dash out of harms way, and it doesn't always work. It works well only when timed, but when facing Lancer Robot's there's really only one use for it, and that is getting as much distance away form them as possible. Once they start attacking, it takes a little bit for them to stop, but in that time your health is gone.
- You would expect the upgrades to amplify the character, right? Well that really isn't the case here, upgrades are mostly supportive and do nothing to change the gameplay dramatically, or dynamically, they can be useful in providing an edge, it does grant aditional ult slots, alternate ammunition and faster team revive times, but that's about it.
- This game wasn't made with singleplayer in mind, the game, and developers favore multiplayer above all else. Evidence that points tot his include the lack of team bots in the singleplayer, as if the rest of Team RWBY or team JNPR took the day off and left whomever you play as to do all the work. The singleplayer almost doesn't matter, like they never intended it to be a thing.
- Singleplayer is separate from multiplayer which you can't obviously pause as that would be unfair to other players, it's common sense, case and point. But, why does stuff still happen in the game when I hit Esc in singleplayer?!
What reason could your development team have for not including the most basic of nessecities of a singleplayer mode, the ability to
- Other issues with this game are largely minor, I cite Ruby's cape as the most glaring, it seems to clip through itself frequently, and as far as I know it's been in the game for as long as anyone can remember with no fix ever been introduced.
In the end, RWBY: Grimm Eclipse was a valient first attemp at a game on Rooster Teeth's part. However, I must ask them to stick with their web show's, and leave the games to companies that know what they're doing. I cite Bandai Namco Games, and Koei Tecmo as the perfect companies to produce a game based on RWBY.
Rooster Teeth game's seem more focused on downgrading this game and adding skins, over listening to the playerbase and trying to improve it, regardless of what they may say about listening to us. This game could have been so much better, to me it is largely unfinished and always will be. From what I understand there is only one guy who has been working on this game, which explains why it never officially left the beta stages, it could have been so much more with a larger team, a better engine and proper thought and vision.

Honestly, while I do like RWBY, I get the strong impression that whoever wrote the description of this game for the Steam store has never played it before.
The controls are seemingly random, I glitch across the battlefield all the time, and more often than not I end up surrounded by Grimm and, subsequently, getting cut to pieces and dying.
Now, let me specify: For this example, I will pretend I chose Blake as character, mainly because that´s what I usually do.
So, the game starts, and I´m already annoyed. The most basic feature of a third-person game, the abbility to zoom in and out with the camera, is not there. Blake takes up most of the screen, and more often than not, the camera either glithes into her torso or she stands so close to a wall that the only thing I see is her bellabooty.
Gambol Shroud, in its gun form, has a far too powerful recoil, and there isn´t even any form of hint at where the bullet would hit, making it quite difficult to actually shoot enemies. Also, Blake tends to turn in random directions when I shoot, meaning that the Grimm I intended to shoot has enough time to land a few hits, while I try to get Blake under control.
Blake´s abbilities aren´t much help either, mostly because they´re not really well described and anything. Sure, the controls options tell you how to use which attack, but those descriptions don´t match with the skills you can choose at all, meaning that you´ll have to take a good guess, pick a skill, and then see which of your three means of attack has changed.
Overall, this game needs some serious re-working. Decreased enemy strength, managable controls, and a hint at what skills are used when you press which key.
As of now, however, the only thing I´m glad about is that I already bought the game, so I don´t have to buy it again once it gets actually playable, and most likely more expensive.

I want to address some of the negative comments. Most peoples problems boil down to them not having worked out how to play the game properly. By the sounds of it, the extent of their strategy is deciding do I build 7 shotgunners, or 5 flamers, and then do I attack this point or that point. No wonder they can't complete the later levels.
This game requires constant 'recycling', and effective use of the limited resources. You need to do things like recycle old turrets and advance them forward, or turn your soldiers into snipers to take out the turrets, and then quickly switch them to flamours to rush in.
Sometimes you have to let some of your bases get captured, so you can focus on capturing the enemies in a specific pattern. For example, allow a base that is being attacked from 3 directions to be captured, so you can work your way down 1 of these of these directions, then return to your original base and only have to fend off aliens in 2 directions.
To claim this game lacks in strategies is absurd. The aliens will constantly beat you and cap your bases, so it is regularly 2 steps forward, 1 step back. If you can't handle 'losing for the greater good', then this game might not be for you.
Saying this though, the full price does seem a bit steep, and I did get on special.

The UI is challenging and you will more than likely accidentaly purchase a weapon twice or salvage something you want before fully understanding  the shop/equip menu. The art is quite bad overall with uninspiring visual designs in enemies, VFX and environment.
There are a few really good boss encounters and some of the enemy patterns keep the gameplay feeling somewhat unique throughout.  The majority of the regular enemies and the bulk of levels are fairly bland and the pacing feels flat. There are very few highs and lows which makes the game start to feel boring too quickly.  Ground enemies shoot up at you and its very unclear when you will get hit so it can feel cheap at certain points.

This game is an amazing one.
You go on an adventure as two brothers, controlled(at least in my case) with the WASD keys and the arrow keys. You can also play with a controller, if you're into that sorta thing. You go through a series of event and puzzles that you must solve to move on.  You must save your sick father by going on a quest to find a mystical liquid.
Story & Chracaters - The story isn't anything new and original. But it isn't always how the story is, but rather how it is told. In this case it is told extremely well. You go through mountains,tundras, and various other landscapes. Each one reinforcing the feelings of being farther away from your home. The brothers work together to solve every puzzle and even disagree at times. They get along or bicker, but they always care. Even without a spoken word of English every message in this game goes through.
Graphics - The graphics of this game are pretty good for the art style. The landscapes are beautiful. Everything is pretty original. There were a few seams I noticed in the world building. They sky in the tundra has one. There was a lot of recylcing of assets. (Which is fine, because that's what you are supposed to do) But it doesn't break any of the immersion.
Mechanics - This is where it really hits you. The mechanics and puzzles were amazing. Some of these puzzles i've never seen before and they were fun to try and solve. Anything from climbing on ledges, slinking through gates only the little brother can do, or pulling big levels only the older brother could. Everything each character could do really sunk in. That's where you know the game has begun to take hold. In the end
Overall - This game was so good. You get to have a great time and
Even though I have a short playtime on this game and beat it.That doesn't undermine what it was able to accomplish. I would say its worth the money that it is going for now. I am going to go back eventually and do the rest of the small side quests.

Devil May Cry is one of my favorite game series of all time.  When I heard about DMC4 Special Edition, I felt the hype.  For me personally, Vergil was my favorite character back in DMC 3, I was better with him then I was with Dante.  So How does this version hold up? Does it surpass the ever infamous DMC 3 Special Edition?
No
No it does not
But that doesn't mean that this game is bad, quite from it, DMC 4 Special Edition was that extra little polish the DMC 4 needed to make it a great game.  It has costumes, a feature that was lacking in the original version of DMC 4, new characters. Vergil, Trish, and Lady.  Each character has unique gameplay that really adds to the replayability of DMC 4. Before delving into the characters and the story, first the port.
In my personal experiance of the 32 hours I have put into this game, I have not crashed once, no weird graphic bugs, nothing, and it runs smooth as butter. Though there are people reporting that they are having issues, I run a GTX 960 and have no problems. Other then that, it's a great port. At least for me.
The three new characters as said before is Vergil, Trish, and Lady.
Vergil is an absolute speed demon on 20 different kinds of drugs, all of his attacks can be followed up with an immediate teleport.  This reincarnation of Vergil is much MUCH more powerful then the DMC 3 Counterpart, that being said, I do have an issue with Vergil (Personal issue, not deducting points from the game for this.)
Vergil is much faster yes, but I do not feel like I have as much control over him as I did in DMC 3, this might be due to the fact that Vergil's Dark Slayer style, does not have all the added benifits from DMC 3. All dark slayer does now is teleport to enemy, and act as a double jump, that's it.  While back in DMC 3, we could teleport to an enemy, teleport away from an enemy(You have no idea how much I miss that move) and act as a potential triple jump, if a wall kick was used, if not, then it was just a double jump.  One more thing about Vergil is that he can sometimes feel very "easy button."
Through my playthrough of the game, I discovered that activating DT and spamming Vergils dash attack with Yamato would cause some bosses to lose half of their health before the DT gauge was empty. Yes, this was on normal, I did attempt this on Legendary Dark Knight, still does decent damage, but it still feels "easy button." but that is my own personal gripe.  Besides from those two things, Vergil is an extremely fun character, espically on LDK.
Trish is bascially a rehash of DMC 1 Dante, for those of you who have played it will know what I am talking about.  Core moves from the first game make a reappearance along with some new moves for Trish to play with.  She is very fast, her combos can be brutal, espically if you time your combos well with the lingering lighting effects.  Sparda is a great sweeper and can keep crowds in check, I have not played with her on LDK but I am looking foward to it.
Lady...Dear god Lady. She has EXTREMELY OP range, considering her character though, that makes sense, but charging up that shotgun and going into a big crowd just rips fools apart. Lady does not have a standard DT, but rather she has a grenade Gauge, I two shotted the first boss using this
IT WAS AWESOME
Still though, Lady was awkward to play with at first since she is so unconventional in terms of DMC gameplay, but just give it some time and practice and she might very well become your favorite character.
Vergil will always be number one in my book though.
The story is this, you demon hunter, demons, go kill.  Let's be honest, the story has never been the strong point of any DMC game, but this games story is as follows.
Your first character is Nero, you have a weird arm, you are a knight of some order or whatever and ummm....Dante comes in and kicks♥♥♥♥♥ Look, I watched the cutscenes like one time and always skipped after that.
A bit of catioun though, if you are buying this game to learn more about Vergil's story but are not a huge fan of DMC 4 I would not reccomend this game to you. The "New Vergil Story" has a total of 2 cutscenes.
TWO CUTSCENES
I thought I was going to get intervals of Vergil's journey through out the game but nope
1 cutscene in the begginning, and 1 cutscence at the end, and to be honest it does't really explain much at all, but I won't spoil that...what little there is to spoil anyway...
All in all, DMC 4 SE put some fine tuning and polish one, and it make a good game(DMC 4) a great game(DMC 4 SE)

If anyone enjoys the Western anime-style 3D animated Rooster Teeth production RWBY, then it is very likely that you will enjoy this game. I would recommend this to anyone who happens to like beat-em-up games in general.
When I first got this game, it was on Steam Early Access (one of the Four Horsemen of Terrible Games), but since I loved the show (and most things related to Rooster Teeth, for that matter) I decided to buy this game for the very reasonable price of $14.99. The price is very good considering that you get the entire campaign with all Team RWBY character right off the bat. There is, however, DLC for Team JNPR and other cosmetic content.
The game turned to be well-made and the gameplay that does well enough. That doesn't mean at all that this game is without its flaws. For example, there's one achievement where to earn it one must not take any damage at all throughout the entirety of a level. This would not be so bad if not for two things. The first being that the game does not have any checkpoints to speak of. When playing you would notice that there are pretty clear "stages" or encounters within each level, so it would be logical to include checkpoints here to save progress in each level. So whenever I got hit at all, I am forced to exit out of the level entirely and start completely over (since there's also no restart function in the menu for single player mode). Either that or let the enemies kill me. It might seem unreasonable to just let the enemies have their way with whatever virtual character I'm playing as, but that leads to my second point. That being whenever you die, you get sent all the way back to the beginning of the level. This combined with the lack of a checkpoint system make playing it painfully annoying at times. Even a notoriously challenging game like Dark Souls will have the player stop and rest at bonfires so that when they die they have some place close to start back from. I honestly don't know how the developers overlooked this simple little mechanic.
Even with all that, I still enjoy playing this game. It gives everything that could be wanted out of a RWBY game and still leave more to be expanded on in potential sequels. The biggest idea for a sequel would be to allow for a PvP mode or perhaps story modes made specifically for the individual characters in the show. You could even allow for the a campaign just for the villians of the show. It would suit very well to play as Cinder or Roman in their own separate campaigns.
Anyways, I recommend this game.
