Revolution Ace is an Indie Shoot'em Up reminiscent of other, older, games like Tyrian or Raptor. The game is made in the Unreal Engine so it has some quite nice features, one of which would be actual game depth as opposed to a "drawn" background. Graphically speaking it isn't the top, but it isn't the worst. Some projectiles look nice, while then you have others which look like a brown Big Bullet Bills which could've and should've been handled differently. The music is mediocre, but it could get boring after playing it for a while. Some of the things that disturbed me the most was the lag/skipping of the music in the Main Menu, which didn't happen in-game but as well the fact it takes so long to unlock weapon slots and for some Achievements did not unlock. Some ground units seemingly just passed through impassable terrain making it a lot more confusing and for some reason some of the air units look like containers, furthermore confusing me about which projectiles to use because of the way they all look alike. Sometimes the combat feels clunky and slow, while the enemies just rush past you(most of the time you won't clear the waves, even when the enemies return). Shields will also regenerate only when you aren't shooting, but the whole point of the game is to shoot and destroy enemies, so that might need a rework. I also noticed the first two bosses were easier than normal enemies. Overall this game has high potential but it need some polishing, or so I believe. One of the most fun things is the upgrades the game offers for your Aircraft. I'd suggest buying it on sale, probably.

An great example of the hack and slash genre. I got introduced to this sort of game playing Bayonetta, then Bayonetta 2 and Wonderful 101. Despite some differences in the combat mechanics between this and Platinum hack and slash games, the core element that makes all these games fun is still there: a complex combat system and an invitation (and motivation) to master it. Playing through this game once on normal mode is hardly the full experience of this game. You will experience some sense of mastery of the mechanics, but you can get even more out of this by going for higher rankings, secret missions, playing as different characters, and all sorts of other stuff.
That said, after playing this, I'd still say I prefer Bayonetta 2. First, I had issues with the camera during combat, which is especially problematic due to the presence of enemies that can charge at you or hit you from a distance. It's something that you can overcome with experience, though. Second, I was really used to the heavily dodge and counter based gameplay of Platinum games, and I felt that there wasn't so much of an emphasis on that in this game (at least with how I was playing). It doesn't really seem to reward you with anything (like Bayonetta's slow motion) when you dodge stuff, and I found the controls for dodging to be a little unpleasant. You have to press to the left or right of an enemy and press a button, and if you don't get the direction right you'll end up jumping up or back. Compare that to Bayonetta, where you can just press one button and any direction and you'll dodge. It adds an element of execution to the dodging that I didn't really appreciate. I didn't find any sort of counter mechanic in my playthrough (maybe it had something to do with Royal Guard). So, basically, I'm just saying this game is different than Bayonetta 2 in some ways I didn't like.
Overall, if you like hack and slash games, you'll find there's a lot to get out of this. If you don't know whether you like those sorts of games, this might not be the best introduction.

Devil May Cry 4 got a lot of flak when it first came out. Nero wasn't Dante, lackluster visuals, the enemies weren't designed very well, and the levels were poorly designed as well. But there is one thing everyone agrees on, and that's that DMC4 has the best gameplay in the series. Both Nero and Dante were filled to the brim with combo depth, and it was an absolute blast to slice through demons.
Devil May Cry 4: Special Edition takes everything that made the original great, and expands on it. You liked mastering the two playable characters from DMC4? Well, now you've got five of them, each with unique stories and cutscenes. Yes, now aside from the two leads from the original, you can play as Dante's brother Vergil, Dante's girlfriend Trish, and their devil-hunting compatriot Lady. Each character brings something new to the table, each with just as much depth and potential as the original two leads.
The new visuals are absolutely stunning, in crisp 1080p. Everything looks much nicer than the original, and it's incredibly well optimized, too. Even with my admittedly very poor set-up, I'm able to get a consistent 60 FPS, even in the middle of graphically intensive boss fights.
This is easily the definitive version of Devil May Cry 4, while it didn't fix everything, it did add a substantial amount of content, making it more that worth a buy. It's worth full price, and even better on a sale.

I used to absolutely love GTA V, I played it a fair amount of hours and enjoyed both the single player and online experience with friends.
The first few weeks of doing heists felt amazing and walking away with solid cash after we all worked together as a team flawlesly felt like a totally new experience. Even the times when we messed up a heist in a hilarious way it still felt worth it.
Hours of freeroaming never got boring either, and with the constant DLC updates adding new cars, races, guns, houses and so on they kept the game feeling fresh.

First of all, the hackers, it started with money hacks, people spamming bags of cash everywhere. This obviously wasn't the worst but then came the aimbots, godmode and at the end of the hackerfest came the button that made an entire server die. Server being innacurate as the way the servers are run are still peer-to-peer as far as I know. (This being a huge part of the problem).
The comunity has never been the most friendly one but has still become more salty as time went by. Rockstar seems to have implemented more and more of a pay-to-win policy where vehicles with high prices are virtually indestructible and have over the top weapons and abilities.
As a final nail in the coffin for me I recently got word that one of the most famous modding tools for GTA V has received a cease and desist, forcing them to shut down their tool completely or risking a huge expensive lawsuit if they didn't comply.
The way Rockstar treats the fanbase and the modders who are only trying to create new and fun experiences on a game that seems to be dying slowly is just a big no-no to me.
Policies like this seem to have been a trend in the industry for the last years and I highly encourage everyone to let companies know this is not the way to handle things.

Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is an answer to Deus Ex: Human Revolution's questions - what does it mean to be human? Do you stop being human if you replace parts of your body with technology? At what point? In a lot of ways, Mankind Divided is also the wrong answer to the questions asked by its predecessor, and that's definitely the intent; where Human Revolution waxed poetic about potential, Mankind Divided sees it squandered.
For both games, even before their release, concerns were voiced about how various issues and questions were posed: where Human Revolution was almost entirely black and white about augmentation vs. purity, Mankind Divided is blunt about discrimination; simply put, there wasn't a whole lot of nuance. However, I think that works to both game's benefits - I think that a nuanced approach to both topics doesn't fit well within the type of game both are, which is a mass market, AAA release. When you need to cast a wide net to bring in as many buyers as possible, you have to plan for lowest common denominators. And that's where Mankind Divided not only goes above and beyond, but also might open a few eyes.
Where Mankind Divided's linear narrative feels oddly paced and strung out, it's world narrative is a masterpiece; from the moment you start the game, you're treated as an other, first by prominent figures in Task Force 29 (TF29), and then by a wayward officer working for the Prague State Police. MacReady, the TF29 agent, can be easily written off as an isolated case of discriminatory views when you first start, but that State Police officer is where your position as an augmented human starts to become apparent, as the game stops you, engages you in a fairly slow conversation that feels entirely unnecessary, and condescends to you at the same time.
maybe that officer is just a jerk, like MacReady, though. There're always characters in games who are antagonistic and you don't like. But then you get stopped outside your apartment for the same thing. And then you get stopped each time you walk through the wrong line, or take the wrong train - and it's easy to not understand why you're being stopped, sometimes. When you play a game like Mankind Divided, you're chasing objectives, personal or provided, and you try to find the shortest line to those objectives. So when something seemingly arbitrarily stops you, it can get frustrating. Eventually you notice the typically understood rule of "right lane, left lane" traffic doesn't apply - "Augs" have a single lane for both directions, while "Naturals" have the other two lanes to themselves. Once you start running through the right gate, you never get stopped. You might not realize it (especially if you turn objective markers off), but the game always directs you to the "Aug" train with the objective marker. If you take the wrong train, the loading screen makes it apparent you do not belong there. When you get off, you're stopped by State Police, interrupting your flow again. You take the right train, though, and you don't get bothered.
But the game is pervasive in its decision to denigrate you. Everywhere you go, it's "your kind," "your people," "aug," or the slur "clank." The shop keepers call you that. The gangsters call you that. The citizens call you that. And the State Police call you that. You literally cannot walk down the street in Prague without someone calling you a "clank" - sometimes you can't even avoid seeing an augmented person being detained, and a brief listen will let you know it's for no real reason. And while that stuff is easy enough to ignore in the moment, over the course of an entire game it adds up - it makes you an eternal "other," and you are only accepted by fellow sympathizers, and to a somewhat limited extent within TF29.
You'll also see the opposite occur, but in vastly fewer instances. You'll run across augmented people who despise the "fleshys," or you'll see some posters or graffiti supporting augmented rights - one even being "Aug Lives Matter."
That's all the "how," but the "why" is what makes this approach important. Leading up to the release, Mankind Divided's marketing drew criticism for co-opting the language of the Black Lives Matter movement for the "Aug Lives Matter" statement in the game; it was seen as unfairly capitalizing on a legitimate social movement aiming to help end oppression for black Americans in order to try to sell a product. However, I think such a tactic works in the favor of both Mankind Divided, and progressive social agendas, because Mankind Divided isn't a good preach for the choir - it's a good lesson for the uninitiated.
If you look at the opponents of a given social movement, a lot of times they lack the empathy necessary to understand the plight of the people pushing for social change. With Black Lives Matter, it's white people not understanding how pervasive and real racism is; for feminism, it's dudes not quite getting that, yeah, there really are a myriad of sources of harassment towards women. The blunt nature of Mankind Divided's world makes it so almost no one can disregard the discrimination you experience as Adam Jensen - you might be able to ignore it while it's happening, but you'll certainly remember it if prompted in any way. It puts the players in a situation where they experience a more severe form of the discrimination some groups already face in real life, in a tangible way within the game that will draw their attention.
And then the "Aug Lives Matter" poster grounds it in reality. It draws the necessary parallel to the real world, to drive the point home that what's happening in the game isn't just made up. The verbal harassment, the unjustified detainments, the violence, the general prejudice - these are all things experienced by marginalized groups today.
And in doing that, I feel Mankind Divided is triumphant. Is it an eloquent thesis on the current state of various race/gender/etc relations? Absolutely not. And it was never intended to be - the average player wouldn't understand it. Instead, it takes its fundamental existence as a AAA game, a mass market piece of media, and uses that to make sure no one can walk away feeling okay with how they're treated while playing as Adam Jensen.
And maybe - hopefully - the virtual discrimination will be so shockingly brazen, blunt, and pervasive that the privileged people in the audience have their eyes opened a bit. Even if that comes at the expense of the already enlightened scratching their heads a bit at how basic the simulation is.

I will start out by saying there have been times I have enjoyed GTA5 but sadly that has all been tainted by a recent ban and recent from the online section with no reason given but I can only assume from having been in a game with hackers who dropped cash on me. I'm not usualy the type to go in for these negative review waves but this was the straw that broke this camel's back and since I have some spare time now, I will break down main the issues I have with GTA5:
1. If your game has hackers in it, why not fix it rather than simply banning everyone who comes into contact with them.
-seriously, why is there a $40k item in the game with seemingly no legitimate reason for its presence?
2. The recent single player mod bans by T2 (even if Rockstar did talk them out of this, we don't know what really went down)
3. The loading times - I really won't miss these. Not just the initial load times but the amount of time spent waiting between matches in playlists.
4. The number of disconnects - hardly a session went by without being disconnected from playlists or mid game to be faced with another long loading screen or more often than not face a loading screen that hung indefinitely.
5. The apparent greed in the pricing of online content. Yes, in theory all content online can be gained freely through a process of grinding but for someone who doesn't have hundreds of hours to sink into a game, much of the content was locked to me unless I succumbed to the evil that is:
6. The Cash Cards - I will start by saying that I can understant the principle of having cash cards - they help fund further development and can provide a way to avoid the grind for those whose time is worth more than their money. However the pricing is excessive. Lets take the example of the super yacht - a base price of $6M, to buy this with cash cards the cheapest option would be the $8M card. With the current sale that would be a cost of £36 in real cash, MORE than the base cost of the game! Outside of the sale we would be looking at a cost of £60, more expensive than the release price of a brand new AAA title on steam - for a virtual yacht with no significant gameplay value. Even in a less extreme case a good car with mods would set you back £12+ in terms of real money. The recent gun running update added some fun new toys that could set you back over £100 to buy unless you can devote hundreds of hours to grinding. No wonder T2 and R* are so touchy about hacked cash.
As the official description notes: "Cash is king in this town"
I have more, smaller issues with the game but in all honesty I might one day play a few rounds in the future. But my quest for virtual content is ended. I will devote no more time to accruing virtual currency and I will never buy a cash card; this is perhaps the main reason why T2 and R* won't give a damn about this but for me their reputation will forever more be sullied.

Here are some things that really caught my eye when starting up and throughout:
Graphics - I’m not really a stickler when it comes to graphics, so some of the simpler textures in this game didn’t bother me; I actually enjoyed how the game presents itself, as it is pretty much all you would need from a game of this caliber. Besides, why bump everything into the graphics when the only thing you will be looking out for is enemy fire? All joking aside, the graphics in this title actually surprised me, looking into how the defeated enemies scar the landscape and at the intriguing water physics. I understand some individuals are only interested in games that present themselves with AAA graphics, but that mindset should really be looked past with this title.
Controls - From the beginning, you are presented with two modes of fire: air-vs-air and air-vs-ground. These two modes of fire can be accessed separately by clicking LMB or RMB, respectively, but can be remapped if needed. Movement remains standard in Revolution Ace, with your classic WASD keys or Arrow keys representing the various direction. I know I cannot speak for everyone with this, but the craft in this title controls quite nicely as dodging enemy fire while utilizing quick reflexes becomes more important as you progress. You will learn what MMB is used for later. I don’t want to spoil the fun.
Gameplay - There’s a reason it’s called bullet hell. Revolution Ace is a side-scrolling (for lack of better terms) shooter with the objective of scoring enough points to ultimately better your ship and-subsequently-bring more pain to the bombarding enemy forces. As stated previously, the ship controls nicely from my perspective and the gunplay is fantastic. What I found of particular interest (described in the next segment) was the customization, which allows you to upgrade specific components of your ship to fit the scheme of play you want. For instance, do you want to stick to the classic missiles and guns on your ship and use the basic shield? or would you prefer utilizing an automated laser turret mounted on your craft with a chain-gun mounted on front and heat-seeking missiles primarily for enemy aircrafts?
Upgrade/Customization System - Here’s where the game really shines. Remember the mention of only starting with a basic gun, missiles, and shield? As you progress through the campaign, both Experience and Scrap Points-which acts as a currency-are gained. Starting at an early level, ship upgrades-such as improving damage by 10% as your ship drops below 25% hull-can be chosen to better customize your level of play; be warned that once you select a ‘Perk’ you cannot reselect, though you gain more as you progress. Along with these permanent upgrades, you also unlock Slots on your ship, which allow for even more guns and other attachments-such as the aforementioned automated laser turret. From where I am in the game, this system of upgrades and customization has really impressed me, as I have been intrigued enough to switch my style of play so that I can buy different weapons. What also sets this system apart from others is that each gun, though different, is necessarily better than another so it really just depends on how you use each one. Did I mention there are things known as Super Weapons that can be used when clicking MMB and are cooldown based? Those are also really fun.
TL:DR - There may be things I left out, but I have not been able to play the various game modes as of recent, which-by concept-are very intriguing. Though I did not mention it in the base review, I did enjoy the fact that there are no Achievements in the game pertaining to beating the Campaign at multiple difficulty settings, which allows the player to go at their own pace. At this stage, I’d highly recommend Revolution Ace for its fast-paced, over-the-top gameplay. Just remember: you will get hit. A lot. Thanks for reading.

Revolution Ace is a PC Shoot Em' Up that, as far as I can tell, tries to reconcile the differences between old school western shmups, where the right equipment saves the day, and new style shmups where location is everything, and hits are incredibly hard to come back from. It also tries to modernize itself with a league of features, some good, some bad. To give a quick, and concise conclusion to this review? I would PERSONALLY rate RA as a "Maybe/When Cheap" where you're paying cheap for the game itself. I got it for 20 cents, and my friend and I enjoyed ourselves. But for the majority of that time, we were enjoying each other's company in Co-op and not the game itself. Unfortunately, since Steam has only yes or no as an option, and I feel Yes is too strong an affirmation for this game, I'm picking no. Now I'll explain the Pros and Cons:
Pros:
- The game has functional co-op for the most part, and while I'm sure the Devs might argue otherwise, I feel it was built with co-op as a main intention. I believe enemy HP is cut down somewhat in single player and the ship number is based on difficulty and not whether or not it's SP or MP. Also, the way the gameplay works, it has encouraged teamwork between the two of us beyond "both of you shoot at it until it dies."
- The game's versus ideas are great. The idea of being able to do offline challenge modes that escalate between you and your opponent, while done before, seems competently done. Direct versus is fun as you watch your partner do better or worse than you in certain areas, constantly trying to outdo one another's score and take advantage of competitive-only upgrades and modifications to equipment. Kudos to the dev for making their random levels work with this system as well by supplying the same seed to both clients.
- The game DOES fill a niche that we haven't seen met recently. At the heart of it is a game that wants to be "Raptor: Call of the Shadows" if it were made today, with technological and game design advances. However, it can and DOES need improvement, the sort a Revolution Ace 2 would hopefully present.
Cons:
- The perk system hurts the game because you cannot respec them, either grind ridiculous hard to have all of them or start over with another profile. It also directly gates off better weapon variety, weapon slots on your ship, and eventually, objectively superior weaponry/equipment.
- Weapons (and WEAPON SLOTS) being locked off by leveling means you don't actually do as much damage as you need to until you hit those high levels. And even then, it often doesn't feel like enough unless you've properly specced yourself. Another casualty of this is the feel of these weapons. They have generic sounds and since they don't tear through ships HALF as well as Raptor's or Tyrian's do? They not only feel weak, but are confirmed so. Complicate this with a A2G and A2A system where you specifically have to choose between the two (EVEN IF YOU HAVE WEAPONS THAT CAN DO BOTH, UNLIKE RAPTOR!) and the game makes you dance to its tune more than it needs to.
- A regenerating shield system that attempts to harp Raptor but falls flat because it requires you to stop firing, a bad idea for the following reason. It would've been better to just make it regenerate if you avoid being hit for a while to let you choose between staying in the fray and keeping it from getting out of hand or waiting for half to full regeneration in relative safety.
- Enemies come back again. Depending on the difficulty they can come back once, twice or thrice, or infinite times. You WILL have moments that feel less old school American shmup like Tyrian 2000 and more Japanese Bullet-Hell Shmup like Crimzon Clover, without the tiny hitbox grace that the latter trades off for dying on hit. Being overwhelmed is not only a very real possibility, it's a very real likelihood if you're not doing so well.
-Some enemies are incredibly annoying to deal with. Later levels involve enemies that quickly fly across the screen spamming bullets. I can only imagine the nightmare of Nightmare Mode, where you're trying to hit them knowing they'd stick around indefinitely if you didn't.
-Very inconsistent artstyle means you'll be facing enemies that look hobbled together from a variety of artists...because the credits demonstrate they WERE. This also means garbage like white bullets hidden by clouds and bright blue bullets that nearly match the background sky.
-A pointless storyline. Yes, shmups are usually games that don't need a plot, but the random blurbs you get every few levels hint at a mastermind and/or cause between the malfunctioning war machines...but doesn't at all elaborate, instead constantly presenting WHODUNIT? possibilities. Having no plot at all is actually BETTER than that.
-Their amazing water effects sounds great until you drop a super bomb on it and it goes through the grounds. They wanted to make that a special note? I'll make it a special one here.
Overall it's a game that I feel is playable, outside of a few bosses who apparently don't have synced up attacks in co-op. But it's a game you'll play through and occasionally pick up again for co-op purposes, not a game you'll keep coming back for more. Hence why I'd rate it as a Maybe, but since there's no Maybe and the cons outweigh the pros, a No is a must.

Normally, I could agree with Heroes and Generals, with their FPS optimization update/fix in one of the recent updates though; in-game performance has declined for me and becomes less and less enjoyable. In the past, even on the larger maps, I could play on High Graphics at 120-150 FPS and that includes during intense firefights and high-object battles. With the FPS patch update, I can no longer breach 100 FPS and during intense fights I tend to drop to 40 FPS, that in which, if you are like me and have grown accustomed to playing games at 100+ FPS, you will understand just how terrible the recent update is for people experiencing the same issue.
Even if you play at just 60 FPS, you can still recognize just how bad it feels to drop to 40 and below.
It is a horrible experience and I am very disappointed in how they have tweaked their engine, the game is still good; albeit essentially a B2P game, still offers an enjoyable experience through the difficult leveling system and availability to grind for currency (if you like that sort of play-style). Overall, the game has improved much since the intial stages of release. The customization options for your weapons are simple yet very effective. The one downside to this game, I would say, is the fact of how expensive in-game purchases are for equipment; such as weapon attachments. Vehicles I understand the cost of seeing as having 1-3 tanks on a battlefield can completely shift the tide of the fight. Weapon attachments like scopes, barrels, and even a few of the weapons themselves are completely over-priced in accordance with how difficult it is to earn in-game currency.
This game would probably attract a much larger player-base if it wasn't so difficult to obtain good weapons and vehicles.
Pros -
Excellent and immersive playability-
Great vehicle and vehicle weaponry mechanics-
Excellent and semi-realistic movement system-
Goofy physics-
Effective and simple weapon customization options-
Cons-
Somewhat clumsy animations-
Rate of currency earned in proportion to KDR and points earned is low-
Highly overpriced weapons and vehicles in accordance with earned income-
Current engine optimization may or may not boost performance, in my case, it lowered it severely.
I recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun Massive Scale Battle Experience, and already have done so to a few of my friends. There is room for much improvement but it is still a fun way to pass the time. My self-determined overall rating is 7/10.

I am not recommending this game in order to help grab the devs' attention. The game as an idea is fantastic. The feel of the game is great and concealment actually works! The issues surrounding the game are a few broken weapons that have recieved no attention on every faction (there is three currently: US, GE, SU). Mainly, however, it is that the mods installed on weapons are too useful without enough of a drawback. For example, you can kick up your MG's rate of fire by over 100 rpm and the only downside is that you recieve an almost unnoticable amount of extra recoil. The tanks in this game are also both over and underpowered. They feel like they have 10 horsepower and have issues turning. However, they have pinpoint accuracy and their short reloads allows them to hail infantry with nonstop HE rounds. The other drawback to tanks is that the infanty can quite literally run up to a tank ALONE with a couple (yes, just two) of magnetic grenades and destroy the tank while it helplessly attempts to even begin moving. As far as planes, since the new update they are easy to fly and did not lose any sort of power. They need adjustments to be more on par with other vehicles.
BREAKDOWN OF TEAMS:
US:
-Useless teammates that rarely are able to accomplish much.
-Most weapons have small mags and do not like to actually hit their target
-Johnson LMG is the broken US weapon (high rof, damage, and stability), and thompson is an easy spray-and-play
-US tanks are not great, as they have thinner armor, lower penetration weapons, and less accuracy
GE:
-Teammates are usually more coordinated than the other factions
-Most weapons have a little more recoil, but larger mags and a higher rate of fire as well as more accuracy
-STG 44 is a very broken weapon (it is effective at any distance and is able to spray with ease) and MP40 is too stable and accurate for its high rate of fire
-Tanks are more armored and hit hard, often penetrate targets easily. PANTHER tanks are ridiculous and are hated by anyone that has to rid themselves of them
SU:
-Teammates are usually fairly coordinated
-Weapons commonly have drum magazines that promote holding the trigger until the enemy's body despawns, weapons are also accurate and commonly have a high rate of fire without instability to counter it.
-Broken weapons are the AVS-36 (which will kill you without even having to turn and look at you), and the PPS-43, which is too stable for such an unreasonable rate of fire and 35 round magazine.
-Tanks are commonly quicker than the other factions' tanks and fire very quickly. The "Tier 1" Soviet medium tank outdoes the other "T1" mediums in any scenerio. Soviet heavy tanks also hit very hard and their armor is unreasonably hard to penetrate by many of the tanks in the game.
All in all, this game CAN be saved and fixed, but the devs need to listen to the community by making adjustments to weapons, tanks, explosives, and planes, in a way that will make gameplay more authentic and not a "highest rate of fire wins every time" situation.
Try this game with caution, the balancing alone may turn you away instantly.

I've always been a fan of the Sims franchise, and at first was confused about why so many things were missing from the Sims 3 (in comparison to the Sims 2) and then I realized that my hidden items were scrambled about in all of the expansion packs. Good marketing ploy to get fans to buy the extra material, not so great when you're expecting otherwise.

If you like The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Second Life, but you want more family interactions, you're going to love The Sims 3! As you all know, in The Sims 3, everyone has the ability to create his or her own family, build epic houses for their sims, and play their lives out. But now, anyone who has this awesome game has more options for their Sims and Households than ever before! Depending on which expansion packs one has, the Sims can have magic, pets, become a celebrity, and even experience weather patterns!
Gameplay-Simpler than you may think, but not smooth all the time. See the section on graphics below to find out why. Gameplay Score-7 out of 10.
Items-Plenty of stuff to find, use, wear, and so on. This includes items you can buy from The Sims 3 shop. There are a lot of items you may have to buy from there, so be aware. Items Score-8 out of 10.
Weapons-If you count all the wands your witches can use, then yesh, there are weapons. People have provided guns to download free also...Nice! Weapons Score-8 out of 10.
Ammo-The only form of 'ammunition' is the mana bar all (Or most) Supernatural Sims have. Therefore, it's not enough to warrant an actual score. Ammo Score-N/A.
Armor-The only 'armor' Sims have is their clothes, and they don't offer any protection. Sims don't really need it anyway. Armor Score-N/A.
Plot-With an uncanny ability to create your own plot (or plots) by making use of pictures and videos, the possibilities of having a 'perfect plot' in The Sims 3 are endless! Plot Score-10 out of 10.
Characters-Once again, depending on how many Expansion Packs and/or Stuff Packs you purchased, you can surely create just about any character in The Sims 3. Characters Score-9 out of 10.
Sound-Most of the sounds here are easy on the ears, except maybe for humming a tune or perhaps releasing noxious...Yeah. This is it. Sound Score-7 out of 10.
Music-Like many other games of the 2010's, the music isn't really of the best quality, but some folks may disagree with me on this one. Music Score-4 out of 10.
Graphics-Well, there may be some problems here, as the graphics may result in much lagging or even crashing. Sometimes, I've even had to reset my EA password over this! Not cool. Otherwise, the graphics are nice to stare at. Graphics Score-6 out of 10.
Final Score-The Sims 3 can be a truly great game...If you can afford all or most of the expansion/stuff packs it comes with. And even if you have all those, you'll still have to make additional investments from The Sims 3 Store to make your Sims, their homes, and skills unique in your own way. Final Score-9 out of 10.
Sure, the game and its expansion packs together will cost a lot of money, but if one were to carefully save up a little money every month (Even $25 would be enough) then they could have a near-complete collection in a relatively short frame of time...If one is patient. Yes, the game has its fair share of glitches, but unlike in Skyrim, one can have more pets and more children! Plus, those children and pets can have children of their own once they're old enough. The possibilities are nearly endless in The Sims 3!

Been playing The Sims 3 for two weeks now. I played it two times with the same customized household. Only because the first save was deleted when I reformatted my laptop, so I have to repeat it ALL OVER again. (Imagine my patience.)
My findings:
- game still crashes even after it's reformatted, even if I followed all the troubleshooting steps mentioned on both Steam and The Sims 3 forums
- still end up getting my data corrupted after leaving The Sims University and going home, even after I followed all the do's and don'ts of what should be done before and after graduating
The second one I mentioned above, seems to happen after my Sims get their second degree. Their lifetime wish is to be a Major Master (three degrees).
My work around for this is: once they got graded and affirmed that they passed their degrees, I save them as a new household. Then, I move that new household to a house in town, and playing it as a new game. I haven't gone past that. Meaning, I haven't explored any other glitches after that.
Because I didn't play the game for a day now due to the sadness of loosing their friends. They still have all their money, items, skills, and degrees. But they lose their friends, which takes time to build!
I say, don't get too attached playing the game.
But why not? I loved The Sims and The Sims 2. It's addicting that I don't even recall the last time I ate or took a bath. But, well, if you want to play the game, you should:
= be okay with it crashing sometimes, then talking at your computer, praying for it to work continuously this time.
= still love the game even after the number of times that you tried to troubleshoot some glitches.

Brothers is one of the best games I've ever played. It was instantly memorable, immediately engaging, and impossible for me to put down once I had begun. The single player co-op design is unlike anything I've experienced in a videogame - playing on a dual analog stick controller is practically a necessity as you are controlling the titular brothers independently using the left & right analog sticks & shoulder buttons. There is a learning curve to this ambidextrous design, as you'll be getting the brothers to work together to solve puzzles and navigate a variety of terrain, often from separate locations. Being able to play an instrument that requires independent hand movement helps, though most players should get the hang of it relatively quickly. The difficulty is very consistent, steadily increasing without ever being too easy or too hard, and the puzzles are remarkably intuitive & creative. They are close to perfect in design, and solving them is sublimely gratifying - there are many "Eureka!" moments in which a lot of varied elements suddenly gel together like clockwork, and never once did I find myself needing to look online for a solution or getting stuck on a puzzle long enough for it to be an annoyance. Equally compelling is the immersive world in which you play - for such a short game (taking my time, I finished it in a single 3 hour sitting), you traverse a vast variety of settings including idyllic farmlands, haunted forests, snow-covered hills & icy rivers, and an enormous castle near a battlefield littered with the bodies of dead soldiers hundreds of times your size. Brothers' art design & score draw from Swedish, Nordic, and Scandanavian influences, and much like its dialogue (delivered in a fictional language in which the characters' feelings & motivations are expressed entirely by how they emote the gibberish they speak), they help tell a story, create a densely detailed world, and establish a strong, emotionally-driven narrative. Brothers manages to do a lot with very little and never overstays its welcome. It really feels like a labor of love from developer Starbreeze.
This game is special to me in the way my favorite books, movies, and records are; the level of wonder and intrigue I felt playing it is largely unrivaled in the world of videogames, even in many titles that were made by bigger developers working with a much larger budget. Its art design and music are staggeringly beautiful and creative, it has some of the most unique and fun gameplay I've ever experienced, and the journey undertaken is filled with high emotional peaks and analogous of the journey of life itself. The final ten minutes in particular moved me to tears with a climax that utilizes the unique core control mechanic to express the completion of a character arc - something I've never seen prior or since. This game comes with my highest recommendation as an unforgettable experience and work of fine art.

In Infested Planet you command a team of five elite soldiers against an endless horde of aliens. Surrounded on all sides, you must outmanoeuvre and outsmart the enemy. It's a real time strategy game. You start at a base called hive. And while you only hold a single hive your enemies hold a dozed hives.
As soon as the game starts the enemies multiply rapidly and start moving in your direction to attack. You need to protect your hive and every conquered hive and at the same time you need to conquer all alien hives. This can get pretty tricky but it's a lot of fun.
You start with a small amount of money. Money can upgrade your soldiers, buy air support, mines, mortars, cannons or healing and many other things. You are free to experiment because the game allows you to remove any upgrade and buy or build something else instead. Every time you conquer an enemy hive your total amount of money increases.
Then there are mutations. The higher your difficulty level the more often the aliens will mutate. Every mutation makes things worse
Infested Planet has a good story and is an extremely clever balanced game. It looks nice, is very addictive and in my opinion is a must have game. It's simply amazing.

If you have the ability and systems to do so, play Bayonetta. It's Devil May Cry 4, except good. No, really; the concepts are there, but actually developed: the main character isn't muscled out of her own series by an embarrassing, poorly-designed stand-in, and you get to control a demon-touched protagonist against angelic foes whose bizarre religion controls a largely isolated city.
If 'anime' were a singular style -- which it isn't, but if it were -- Devil May Cry 4 would be a prime example, a poster child, of that style. It tries so hard to be everything you'd expect from an upmarketed, glossy, designed-for-consumption experience that it forgets what made Devil May Cry any good in the first place. The first three games? Increasingly good! Some will whine about 2 being different, but most of them are sheeple. The plain fact of the matter is that all of them performed well, and 3 was probably the fan favorite of the whole series. So what do you do when a game basically embodies everything people love about the series?
If you're Capcom, you throw away what they liked and make something you for some reason believe they'll embrace despite that. They did it with the humiliating DmC, and they did it here.
Dante is shoved aside by newcomer Nero, who is basically a bland, unlikeable cardboard cutout of a protagonist. You will know his entire story by seeing five minutes of it. No, really. There is nothing about him that is original or surprising. He feels like the hero of some just-serviceable fanfiction. He's not fun to play, he's painful to watch and listen to, and 4's story is best forgotten utterly and brushed under the rug.
But you aren't here for that. You're here for the Special Edition, which adds new things! Vergil, Lady, and Trish playable, and more! Is it worth it?
In short, no, not really.
Devil May Cry 4 is a clunky game with a bad plot that's hard to enjoy. Even though I admittedly skip the cutscenes now -- sitting through them once, years ago, was enough -- none of the extra characters actually has any real story of their own, and they're lucky to get even one cutscene. There's a premise, but then they're put into exactly the same stages as Nero and Dante are, with exactly the same situations. It's a big yawn, and it's a big shame, mainly because the level design in this game is also pretty poor; you spend your time advancing with Nero, and then once you finally get to play as Dante, basically the other half of the game is backtracking.
So if you wanted to do that with Lady and Trish, congratulations! Your dream has come true. Get this game immediately if that's the case. The same is true with Vergil, though he's alone in his mode. For some reason. So if you wanted at least half a game of backtracking -- congrats! Here it is.
Okay, okay, so I have to admit that Trish, Lady, and Vergil are fun to play as. This is the first time Lady's really playable, and she's a blast...no pun intended. Trish returns to playable and she's a joy. Vergil's playable again.
But in all honesty, it just makes me think of the games where you could play as them and have a bit more fun. Trish was unlockable in 2 and a lot of fun in it. Vergil was playable in 3's Special Edition. They're both better and more enjoyable games than 4, and they feel far more distinctive than the samey kind of high-gloss, low-substance experience that 4 gives you.
I got this to support the release so that maybe, just maybe, Capcom will get the message that we want to see more Devil May Cry, with Dante, Trish, and Lady, and less of the humiliating and inexplicable attempt at a redux they tried. I'm not going to hold my breath, though, since Capcom are notorious for handling franchises poorly and especially being contemptuous towards fans.
I really can't recommend it to anyone who isn't trying to support the actual Devil May Cry. If you want to play better games in the series, get the HD collection of Devil May Cry 1-3. If you want to play a better game in general, get Bayonetta. It essentially takes the basic elements of Devil May Cry 4 and makes them an engaging, enjoyable, fun experience that you will find memorable and a classic of modern gaming.
As for Devil May Cry 4, it's just not a good game. It's not terrible, but it's easily the least enjoyable in the 1-4 series, and it has the least amount of character and interest to it. It's just a bland exercise in going though the motions, and the Special Edition's extras don't really add anything to that or make it much better.
Give it a miss, unless you just really want to have this game on your PC for some reason, or feel like buying it may send Capcom a message that they need to get back to the roots of what made the series great. 4 isn't what made it great, but at least it had the actual Dante in it, along with his supporting cast, even if he was pushed out of the spotlight temporarily by some derpy twerp with a lazily similar character design.

I used to absolutely love GTA V, I played it a fair amount of hours and enjoyed both the single player and online experience with friends.
The first few weeks of doing heists felt amazing and walking away with solid cash after we all worked together as a team flawlesly felt like a totally new experience. Even the times when we messed up a heist in a hilarious way it still felt worth it.
Hours of freeroaming never got boring either, and with the constant DLC updates adding new cars, races, guns, houses and so on they kept the game feeling fresh.
But I hear you say: But that's all positive why are you giving it a bad review!?
First of all, the hackers, it started with money hacks, people spamming bags of cash everywhere. This obviously wasn't the worst but then came the aimbots, godmode and at the end of the hackerfest came the button that made an entire server die. Server being innacurate as the way the servers are run are still peer-to-peer as far as I know. (This being a huge part of the problem).
The comunity has never been the most friendly one but has still become more salty as time went by. Rockstar seems to have implemented more and more of a pay-to-win policy where vehicles with high prices are virtually indestructible and have over the top weapons and abilities.
As a final nail in the coffin for me I recently got word that one of the most famous modding tools for GTA V has received a cease and desist, forcing them to shut down their tool completely or risking a huge expensive lawsuit if they didn't comply.
The way Rockstar treats the fanbase and the modders who are only trying to create new and fun experiences on a game that seems to be dying slowly is just a big no-no to me.
Policies like this seem to have been a trend in the industry for the last years and I highly encourage everyone to let companies know this is not the way to handle things.
I hope this review has been useful be it that you agree or not.

The second installment of trinity: galactic expedia unleashed, breaks new ground in the gaming landscape. Trinity, or Trin for short is a tale about Duncon Stone, a recently rehabilitated drug addict recovering from severe trauma at an asylum in baltimore. Duncon, or dunk as the inmates call him was a former software engineer for microsoft but after raising a mutiny against steve jobs he was publically executed on the streets of johanesberg where he worked. What they didnt expect was that his corpse was exported to colombo where the doctors worked on him. they utilised various new implants and turned him into a man like machine called the Trine. Trine is a code name for the project, Transplant Ressurected infantry of new Eden. New eden is a bioengineering cartel that spans oceanic borders that funnels billions of dollars worth of biotechnology and unlicensed equipment into key geographic areas. The TRINE project is an attempt to create a global po-lice force designed to implement a new regime once individual governments topple following an expected economic collapse post global financial fiasco. As a Trine unit you are subordinate to your task master, some inglorious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who goes by the name of "the cammel's muel".  CM is what the guys in the lab call him, but to Duncan stone he is the epicentre of a world of suffering under his rule. CM send you all over the globe doing secret missions to merge and consolidate important equipment under his roof. On one uneventful escort mission to secure a new type of balistics device, Duncon gets hit by the typical natural disarster employed in all games these days, you guessed it.. lightaning!. that's right, he takes a bolt to the head which fries the inhibitor chip that CM daddy uses to control him. But the other players know this. and they're coming for you. The game then turns into its multiplayer feature here, which is essentially a treadmil of experiance grinding in order to gear up for the boss fight back in the New eden facility. Its very uninspired and doesent add much to whats already out there in terms of Trinity's mian competitors, namely farming simulator 2000 and football manager 2014. In any case you get some cool guns and the matchmaking system is okay. Once youre geared up you get to face off against the cammels muel in an all star battle of the ages. We're back to single player here now guys just for the record. after a grindy battle of tearing down his health and toking up on heal potions through the entire fight you eventually kill him. Unfortunately for stone, the facility does actually explode trapping him in the compartment underneath. THe game ends with duncon stone putting himself into cryosleep since he is faced with no other alternitive. This sory arc therefore is the prequel of Demolition Man, which aired in the 80's.
Overall, not a bad film. Demolition man had some cool plot twists and the actor played the part well. 4/10 in terms of special effects, the 80's dont really compare to where we are today. Either way, if youre keep to tune into some good old fashioned film, Demolition man is the way to go.
Until next time, stay snazzy!

Revolution Ace is a throwback to old
game play that many experienced on the classic NES console. Revolution Ace lets you chose your own difficulty, and offers a great deal more entertaining game play; without the controller throwing and raging that I experienced with the classic
games.
There isn't much to say about the story in this game... as you play through the game occasionally some text pops up speculating on why you're shooting down all these enemy planes.
You have two "shooting" buttons, one for
and one for
. The rest of the controls are simply movement controls,
. As you progress through the game you get "Scrap" from your various missions that can be use to purchase upgrades for your aircraft in the Armory. There are plenty of upgrades to chose from; bullet weapons, laser weapons, rocket weapons, shields, and super weapons.
There are 19 achievements within the game, all of which are quite obtainable, the last 3 achievement do need a few tricks or repeatedly playing through certain levels to meet the required objectives.
I earned close to 50% of the achievements on my first play through. It's also worth noting that all the achievements are able to be earned by yourself. So this is a nice easy "100% Achievement" game.
Revolution Ace is priced at $4.99 that's a fair priced for how much time you can spend playing the game. I put in 7 hours before I had all the achievements (05/19/15), and if you really enjoy playing these types of games, it's definitely a good genre to add to your steam library.
I can't remember the last time I played
game, but this one was definitely a winner, I recommend this game to anyone who misses playing old classic
games, however with less difficulty. Unless you like difficulty, in that case you can simply play Revolution Ace on a harder difficulty.

Brilliant. Finally a game that can satisfy Quake 3 Nightmare level players and alike. The developers have done an excellent job here creating a game that can be played with no charge for those who cannot afford costs, but also allowing those who have the money to progress quicker to a level suitable to the individual. You can reach nearly every aspect of the game without spending any money, providing that you are patient and willing to take the long and hard road to becoming a "Hereo or General".
Game at present provides 3 factions - German, American and Russian with each faction subdivided into Infantry, Reconnaissance, Paratroopers, Armour(tanks), Pilots and finally (Generals - which play a strategy game rather than getting dirty with the troops - have not tried it myself yet as there is to much fun elswhere). When you join a faction, you start as an Infantry soldier. After accumulation of "in game cash", you can spend the cash on weapons upgrades, purchase a soldier within a different faction, buy planes, trucks, motorbikes, tanks etc.
The developers, at present,  have also been generous by providing new players a Gold initial payment after the first day of playing with 4 Gold units added for every other day you play the game. Gold can also be purchased using your credit card in case progress for you is to slow.
New players also get a 24 hour Veteran Status which increases the amount of internal game cash, experience and skill, faster ribbon accumulation and a few other perks included. They offer package deals for Veteran status but in my opinion is not worth it as for example, paratroopers and pilots only get one additional slot for adding a skill or weapon. If they increased it to 3 or 4 skill slots, then I would very much consider it.
Sounds effects are extremely well done. If a grenade explodes near you but does not kill you, a great deal of your health is lost and  just like in the real world, when a person starts to faint, first your hearing goes followed by a blur in sight - this is in the game and you WILL experience it from time to time. Do not worry, if you die, you are able to spawn at the nearest point of your choice and continue the game until your faction has captured all primary points or run out of resources etc. Other sounds of guns, tanks, planes, anti-aircraft guns etc is very well done. You can even hear the rolling effect of the Sherman tank as it reloads the barrel for another salvo.
Game development is still on-going with improvements, patches, enhancements and changes. Many players get frustrated but very often due to not understanding how and what they should be doing. Only negative I have had is my poor network connection as it causes tremendous network lag, resulting in delayed visuals on enemy positions. Sometimes I empty a complete magazine on an enemy, the game catches up to the server and I find my opponent was 3 metres to the left or right. So ensure your network is good and "ERROR free". Game does not require much bandwidth, mainly clarity of network service.

I feel it's quite unnecessary to review this, since it's age, however this review is aimed at the people who are fans of the Sims 4, and would like to buy the Sims 3.
Of course, The Sims franchise is amazing, and I won't doubt I had extreme fun playing this game back when I had it installed. However, if you already own Sims 4, I wouldn't recommend buying this one too. If you're made of money, and have the cash to waste, then go ahead, but the game and all the DLC's that make it complete, isn't worth it.
Compared to the Sims 4, Sims 3 load times are extremely tedious. I can assure you, when you load the game up, you'd be waiting at least 2 whole minutes for the game to load the World. If you can bare the loading times, the game-play is fun, however compared to The Sims 4, it lacks elements that you'd be used to, and will won't feel as natural.
The DLC's in this game is what makes up Sims 3 as a finished game. Without these, the game just feels like it's missing some serious details. In my own opinion, I think Sims 4 has reasonable DLC's that bring things you don't necessarily need, whereas Sims 3 certainly lacks things that feel as if they should be a requirement to have.
In conclusion;
If you're wanting to buy this just for the sake of having it, I wouldn't. It's too expensive, and if you're anything like me, you'd get bored and turn the game off before it even loads, from the amount of time wasted.
If you're wanting to buy this because you have played Sims 4, I would take a hard look at your paycheck and look at the DLC's you'd be buying to make it close to what you're used to.
If you're wanting to buy this because you've played on Console, I would highly recommend it. The game is easier to control than the console version, and has Mods you can download to make it feel better.
If you're wanting to buy this and you haven't played a Sims game before, I highly recommend buying The SIms 4. It's the up-to-dated and newest version, getting regular updates and DLC's that aren't too expensive, graphics and functions are better, and overall just a faster and more fun game.
Overall:
Playability: 5/10 (Too slow)
Graphics: 6/10 (Was good for it's time)
Entertainment: 7/10 (Provided you can bare the loading times,)

Admittedly fun at times, but overall, not a very noteworthy game.
For the most part, the controls are tight. Moving around and jumping on enemies feels very natural, like a Mario game. However, the hover mechanic feels very quirky. It seems to only work when it feels like it; sometimes you'll hover in mid air, sometimes you'll fly upward, and other times it won't do anything. This leads to unnecessary difficulty at times. I don't recall the exact level, but the broken hover mechanic made trying to traverse through a narrow tunnel of spikes very infuriating. Some gamepad support would be nice, but its absence isn't a deal-breaker.
The difficulty is all over the place. I was able to complete the game and get all of the achievements in under 20 minutes. The boss fights are a complete cake walk (there's 4 boss battles, and only 2 are unique. I'm not saying I expect a huge variety of boss battles from an indie game, but the battles themselves are not very unique.) The actual levels have no pattern in difficulty, but in general, they're pretty easy. Some levels have some dickish designs (I go back to the tunnel of spikes mentioned earlier, where you fall through some fake blocks into a pit of spikes once you get through the tunnel), but they're not much more than a minor inconvenience.
If you're looking for some mindless fun, give this game a try. It's simple, short, and fun to play if you're on a coffee break at work or something like that.

: The first section is a review aimed at people who have never played a DMC game in their life, and the second section is aimed at returning fans.
Allow me to congratulate you for not playing a DMC game yet! You poor, poor soul, you.
DMC4 is a spectacle fighter. Basically, a spectacle fighter is just a really, REALLY flashy beat-em-up. What this boils down to is a game where you spend all of your time juggling enemies in insane fashions, with combos that are as badass as they are impractical, and weapons to match. You get bonus points for varying your combos up, and being as stylish and awesome as possible. The flashier your moves, and the cooler you look, the more the game rewards you.
Out of all of the games, this one is probably the easiest to just pick up and play with no frame of reference or context for who the characters are. I'd say that's the best way to play this game, to be honest, because then you get to feel what Nero feels as he's meeting all of these iconic characters for the first time. You won't have any idea who Dante is, or Gloria, but neither does the guy you're playing as. This doesn't apply to the "bonus" campaigns though, those being Vergil, Lady, and Trish. The game doesn't really properly introduce those characters to you, so you'll be totally lost. But there really isn't much to the story in DMC, and these bonus campaigns don't really have their own storyline, so you don't really need to know them to have a good time.
The game is definitely the easiest in the franchise, but it's still Devil May Cry. You're gonna die a lot at first, and you're gonna get lost, but you'll take to it eventually. Once you get used to them, the controls are REALLY ♥♥♥♥ing good--everything you want them to be in a specular fighter.
The only thing I can really compain about is that this is one of those "Where the hell do I go" kind of games. Expect your first playthrough to be a lot of running around aimlessly, very frustrated, trying to figure out where the ♥♥♥♥ you're supposed to be. This is made even worse by the fact that, because it has roots in the Resident Evil series, you will see a lot of things in the levels that you can't interact with yet. These things will come in handy two or five levels down the road, but they only serve to make your first playthrough even more annoying.
Overall, it's a very niche game, but it's also a very fun game. Considering you can get refunds very easily and quickly now, I recommend at least buying it and trying it if you have any interest at all, even if it isn't on sale. Trust me, you'll probably thank me for it.

My dear frodo...The Lord of the Rings
The Fellowship of the Ring, the first volume of The Lord of the Rings, begins with Bilbo's "eleventy-first" (111th) birthday (on 22 September), 60 years after the beginning of The Hobbit. The main protagonist of the novel is Frodo Baggins, Bilbo's kinsman, who celebrates his 33rd birthday and legally comes of age on the same day.
In T.A. 2989 (S.R. 1389), Bilbo, a lifelong bachelor, adopted Frodo, the orphaned son of his first cousin Primula Brandybuck and his second cousin Drogo Baggins, and made him his heir. Though Frodo was actually "his first and second cousin once removed either way",[1] the two regarded each other as uncle and nephew.
All this time Bilbo had kept his magic ring, with no idea of its significance, using it mostly to hide from his obnoxious cousins, the Sackville-Bagginses, when they came to visit. Gandalf's investigations revealed it to be the One Ring forged by the Dark Lord Sauron. The Ring had prolonged Bilbo's life beyond the normal hobbit span, and at 111 he still looked 50. While the Ring did not initially corrupt him as it had its previous owners, it was beginning to affect him; over the years, it had begun to prey on his mind when out of his sight, and he lost sleep and felt "stretched out and thin",[2] as he said to Gandalf.
On the night of his and Frodo's birthdays, Bilbo announced his intent to turn his home and estate over to Frodo, put on the Ring and vanished from sight. As Bilbo prepared finally to leave the house, he reacted with panic and suspicion when Gandalf tried to persuade him to leave the Ring with Frodo. Bilbo refused to give up the Ring, referring to it as his "precious" – just as Gollum had in The Hobbit. Gandalf lost his temper with his old friend, talking some sense into him. Bilbo admitted he would have liked to be rid of the Ring, and he left it behind, becoming the first person to do so voluntarily. He left the Shire that night, and was never seen in Hobbiton again.
His earlier adventure, his eccentric habits as a hobbit, and his sudden disappearance lead to the enduring figure of "Mad Baggins" in hobbit folklore, who disappeared with a flash and a bang and returned with gold and jewels.
Freed of the Ring's power over his senses, Bilbo travelled to Rivendell, where for the next 17 years he lived a pleasant life of retirement: eating, sleeping, writing poetry, and working on his memoirs, There and Back Again, known to us as The Hobbit. He became a scholar of Elven lore, leaving behind the Translations from the Elvish, which forms the basis of what is known to us as The Silmarillion.
When Frodo and the other Hobbits stopped in Rivendell on their quest to destroy the Ring, Bilbo was still alive but now visibly aged, the years having caught up with him after he surrendered the Ring. Upon seeing the Ring again, he suddenly tried to take it from Frodo; he returned to his senses when a terrified Frodo backed away, and he broke down in tears, apologizing for bringing the burden of the Ring onto Frodo.
After the quest to destroy the Ring was fulfilled in The Return of the King, Gandalf and the four Hobbits visited Rivendell on their way back to the Shire and found Bilbo still living there. He gave Frodo a set of manuscripts that later became Translations from the Elvish, and also gave Samwise Gamgee a small bag of gold that represented the last of his share from Smaug's vast hoard. Two years later Bilbo accompanied Gandalf, Elrond, Galadriel, and Frodo to the Grey Havens, there to take ship for Tol Eressëa across the sea, on 29 September, T.A. 3021. He had already celebrated his 131st birthday by this time, surpassing the Old Took by one year and becoming the oldest living Hobbit ever in Middle-earth. (The average life expectancy of hobbits who survive to adulthood is about 100 years.)

+ Missed enemies that return for a second pass are highlighted, indicating a drop in value; this is a useful feature that encourages target prioritization, although this feature (strangely) seemed to make few appearances after the first level
+ User interface, while not aesthetically sensational, is functional and unobtrusive
+ A combination of unlockable perks, a straightforward leveling system, and myriad upgrade components available for purchase make for a refreshing level of customization
+ Gameplay and ship customization does much to reward forward-planning and a tactical mind-set
+ Boasts an attention to detail uncommon for the genre, such as ripple effects when firing into bodies of water, or trees being felled when strafed by machine gun fire
+ Though few people seem to be taking advantage of it at the moment, the multiplayer is excellent; in particular, the 'Battle Chains' option is absolutely ingenious, and incredibly addicting (this mode lets the player run through a stage, then challenge a friend to the same stage, at which point their progress will be compared to yours and a return challenge issued, building to potentially better and better matches)
+ The combination of air/ground combat is a breath of fresh air for the genre, and adds immensely to the challenge
+ Agreeably lengthy campaign for an arcade shooter - not too long, not too short
+ Healthy variety of enemy units that introduce new patterns and weaponry, building on top of those from previous stages, keeping the game fresh throughout
+ Between ship modules and unlockable perks, the number of combinations at your disposal for tackling enemy units is staggering
+ Visuals are par-for-the-course; they are a bit lacking by today's standards, but they are far from disappointing
- There are occasional, and seemingly random drops in frame-rate (although they are, admittedly, very minor drops, and more casual players are unlikely to be offset by it)
- Music, while not inherently terrible, suffers from a lack of variety; none of the scores really stand out, and they quickly fade into the background during gameplay (sound effects, also, were somewhat uninspired)

I used to absolutely love GTA V, I played it a fair amount of hours and enjoyed both the single player and online experience with friends.
The first few weeks of doing heists felt amazing and walking away with solid cash after we all worked together as a team flawlesly felt like a totally new experience. Even the times when we messed up a heist in a hilarious way it still felt worth it.
Hours of freeroaming never got boring either, and with the constant DLC updates adding new cars, races, guns, houses and so on they kept the game feeling fresh.
But I hear you say: But that's all positive why are you giving it a bad review!?
First of all, the hackers, it started with money hacks, people spamming bags of cash everywhere. This obviously wasn't the worst but then came the aimbots, godmode and at the end of the hackerfest came the button that made an entire server die. Server being innacurate as the way the servers are run are still peer-to-peer as far as I know. (This being a huge part of the problem).
The comunity has never been the most friendly one but has still become more salty as time went by. Rockstar seems to have implemented more and more of a pay-to-win policy where vehicles with high prices are virtually indestructible and have over the top weapons and abilities.
As a final nail in the coffin for me I recently got word that one of the most famous modding tools for GTA V has received a cease and desist, forcing them to shut down their tool completely or risking a huge expensive lawsuit if they didn't comply.
The way Rockstar treats the fanbase and the modders who are only trying to create new and fun experiences on a game that seems to be dying slowly is just a big no-no to me.
Policies like this seem to have been a trend in the industry for the last years and I highly encourage everyone to let companies know this is not the way to handle things.
I hope this review has been useful be it that you agree or not.

TL;DR: This game is a mess. In the least possible words, this comes down mainly to the gameplay mechanics and overall tedium. Buy for five dollars or less.
Don't get me wrong, you can enjoy yourself while playing the game. My friend who I bought this game with, for example, absolutely loves it. I, too, had
fun with the game. But on the whole, as you can see, my overall review is negative.
First off, and most importantly, the gameplay and controls felt clunky and the camera control felt awful at all times, both with keyboard and controller. All the moves are dull and repetitive, and the same can be said for the four or five enemies you encounter on loop forever.
Throughout the game, over and over, you get swarmed and then hit your foes until you can aoe (area attack) them down. Gunplay is all but nonexistent, with autoaiming light-light-heavy ranged attack patterns. Spamming this is long and boring, but effective.
I feel that his game would be great with the controls from Deadpool, a similar but much better game, as they let you shoot while aiming and don't ignore characters completely.
Second, to the previous point, the story is weak and boring, with generic foes and boring environments. You'll recognize them if you watched the show, but they have nothing interesting or special at any point.
Third, the voice acting and music is from the show, but on repeat the same phrases over and over get annoying fast.
And lastly, the price. Though I usually don't harp on the price, I believe this game's worth about five dollars. The only reason I'd purchase this game at any price above that is to support the creators of the show.
I kind of wish I'd listened to the reviews I read and watched. (shoutout to Shammy, the discovery of whose youtube channel was the only good thing to come out of this purchase)
As an afterword, I feel the need to say that I enjoyed the show, and got at least three friends into it. It was never my absolute favorite, as I dislike excessive goofiness and the monsters, the Grimm, were fun for about the first fight. But on the other hand the weapons, character design, and general positivity were quite enjoyable.

Frozenbyte gives us a second helping of the trifecta in Trine 2. Same as last time you play as a the wizard, the knight and the thief but this time you have to restore balance to the land from an evil witch.
The story is fairly thin and only serves as a mean to stitch the 13 levels together. You could breeze through them but you would be missing most of Trine 2's puzzles. As it's predecessor, they remain at the heart of the game. There is a fair bit of combat but it is repetitive and shallow, the fun resides in solving the puzzles. They range from the obvious to the rage inducing but the vast majority stand between the two. All feel rewarding once solved and thanks to video walkthroughs littered over the web you won't get stuck for long.
The main star of Trine is it's visual and art direction. Quite frankly, this is one of the most beautiful game I have ever seen. Every sub-section of every sections of every levels is filled to to the brim with gorgeous detail. The amount of visual elements present in every screen is stupyfiyng. You could close your eyes, move the left stick forward for 3 seconds, open you eyes and see a brand new scene.
The music, with it's assortment of medieval themes is right on par. Character animation on the other end is superb. For instance I loved how the wizard would bend and hold his hat when standing close to a venting shaft. I was surprised how new animation would show up even late into the game.
I do have a couple of gripes with the game. First, the knight feels completely superflous, one could easily beat the game without ever using him. Boss fights repeat themselves and finally, some powers cannot be unlocked until you've played through the entire game.
Pros :
-Perfect visuals
-Character animation is rich and varied
-Solving puzzles is satisfying
Cons :
-Lack of balance between the characters
-Combat seems like an aftertought
-Achievements and completion needs a second playthrough
Final note :
If you love to look at beautiful things then buy this game, it is a feast for the eyes. Solid puzzles, endearing animation and art style makes this game a joy to play.

A beautiful, magical, deeply emotional game that will take you back to the fantasty-adventure movies of your childhood.
Brothers is a story told without words, using motions to convey ideas and a nonsense language to convey feelings. You control the titular brothers with each half of the controller: the Older Brother on the left-stick and trigger, and the Younger Brother on the right. This can get a little confusing when they're not on those sides of the screen, so you'll likely be correcting their positions accordingly throughout. My journey lasted three hours, and not a moment of that time was wasted - every second is filled with beautiful, cinematic views or a basic puzzle to solve.
The diffculty is low, almost trivial, but you're not playing this game to push yourself. This is a journey of the spirit, of the most traditionally fantasy kind. I can't express how beautiful this experience is, and I'm not talking about the graphics -  this really should be experienced by everyone, gamers and non-gamers alike.
PS. Don't forget to Hold Trigger to Pay Respects.
PPS. I'm just waiting for the Payday 2 Crossover DLC, so I can play as Dallas and Houston, and end the game before it begins by telling the dad to "Get da ♥♥♥♥ up".

Grinding in a Shoot-em-up? Yep, and not the fun kind either.
For starters Revolution Ace is very unfriendly to new players. I've played for 2 hours and my weapons were just as useless as when i started despite numerous "upgrades".
Also if you like playing this kind of game with a mouse, forget it; the sensitivity is way too low even on its maximum setting.
There are a lot of dopey design decisions, chiefly:
Power-up's having a delay between their appearance and their availability.
Enemy ship types which are impossible to destroy on their first pass without you taking more damage than them.
In-game power-up's which don't last long enough to be of any use.
Super-weapons which are either ineffective or take so long to recharge that you only get to use them once per level.
Ship and weapon upgrades that don't appear to make your foes any easier to kill or your ship any harder to damage.
Level-up 'perks' which are so ineffective that one questions their inclusion in the game.
There is an auto shield-recharge but by the time the game has realised that you're not shooting anymore, the screen has filled up again.
And occasionally the game crashes on exit and prevents you returning to desktop.
What's good about it?
Some of the music is cool and I like the 3-dimensional landscape.
Overall Revolution Ace is more frustrating than is really necessary. With so many excellent shooters available, there really is no room for this title; at least not for money.

I decided to give the game another chance when older and wiser, and after numerous patches. And i can honestly say hand on heart....

So, I was gifted a copy of this from the developers publicist in exchange for a fair and honest review.
I've put about an hour into it so far, which given the nature of the game seems like a reasonable amount of time to draw some conclusions. I will update this review if I reach different conclusions later.
Anyway, this game seems fairly accessible at first. It is a pretty basic shmup that also later on features some lite bullet hell aspects. The actual movement of your ship is a little slow, and at first, your weapons arent very powerful either. However, as you gain credits via finishing missions and generally blowing stuff up, you can buy upgrades to your weaponry and shields that make this a bit more effective and a bit easier EXCEPT the games difficulty scales more quickly than you can upgrade, and so this actually becomes a pretty challenging game after the first couple missions. I'm level 7 right now and have wrapped up something like 8 or 10 missions so far. At this point, I'm dying pretty quickly even after my upgrades (which you can swap out between missions as well btw) and even though powerups are readily available. Still, I havent reached the point of frustration yet, as I feel the right combo of upgrades is really all it takes to get past the levels despite the fact that they seem scaled beyond your present capabilities as you progress.
As you level up, you also occasionally earn perks, which are basically permanent upgrades to your ship. There is actually a wide variety to choose from, so you will need to choose wisely here.
The graphics are pretty much on par with what you expect. They arent mind blowing, but they do look nice and fairly well represent the genre and the era the game hearkens back to. Speaking of....the music is also well in line with this. It gets a bit repetitive but still remains listenable throughout.
All told, I would normally give this about a 5.5 out of 10. However, the game is presently featured for under 30 cents, and it has trading cards as well, the value of which pretty much are equal to the cost of the game. So...despite the 5.5 out of 10, it's still pretty much a must own if you make use of the marketplace...and lets be real...for 30 cents or so, you will end up owning this at some point anyway.
