I used to absolutely love GTA V, I played it a fair amount of hours and enjoyed both the single player and online experience with friends.
The first few weeks of doing heists felt amazing and walking away with solid cash after we all worked together as a team flawlesly felt like a totally new experience. Even the times when we messed up a heist in a hilarious way it still felt worth it.
Hours of freeroaming never got boring either, and with the constant DLC updates adding new cars, races, guns, houses and so on they kept the game feeling fresh.
But I hear you say: But that's all positive why are you giving it a bad review!?
First of all, the hackers, it started with money hacks, people spamming bags of cash everywhere. This obviously wasn't the worst but then came the aimbots, godmode and at the end of the hackerfest came the button that made an entire server die. Server being innacurate as the way the servers are run are still peer-to-peer as far as I know. (This being a huge part of the problem).
The comunity has never been the most friendly one but has still become more salty as time went by. Rockstar seems to have implemented more and more of a pay-to-win policy where vehicles with high prices are virtually indestructible and have over the top weapons and abilities.
As a final nail in the coffin for me I recently got word that one of the most famous modding tools for GTA V has received a cease and desist, forcing them to shut down their tool completely or risking a huge expensive lawsuit if they didn't comply.
The way Rockstar treats the fanbase and the modders who are only trying to create new and fun experiences on a game that seems to be dying slowly is just a big no-no to me.
Policies like this seem to have been a trend in the industry for the last years and I highly encourage everyone to let companies know this is not the way to handle things.
I hope this review has been useful be it that you agree or not.

The polygon count is so low that Superhot makes this game jealous. Sometimes I turn on the Benny Hill theme during siege battles. I've spent an entire year following my king around while he roams the countryside and lets whatever poor, useless fief he gave me get razed for the third time.
And yet, this is one of the best games I have ever played.
It's not that deep of a medieval simulator, all things considered. There's no real way to trade, sieges are laughable, pledging your loyalty to a lord can turn the game from a fun combat simulator to a weird version of Oregon Trail where all you can do is watch as your food gets deplenished and your money dwindles because your lord demands you follow him as he rides in circles around a mountain that will, by Jove, someday be a threat to the free world.
But it's also a fun medieval simulator. You start with nothing, and have to build your way up to wealth, prestige, gear. You can be a bandit or a bandit hunter. You can drive cattle from town to town or rescue prisoners from outlaws. You can fight in arenas to earn fame and fortune, lay siege to castles and then claim them as your own. You raise up your own elite force of Sword Sisters and Knights and charge into battle alongside them, shattering enemy ranks with a furious charge.
I can't wait for the sequel. In the meantime, I'll just have to help the vikings conquer the world, one more time. If we can stop circling this mountain.

The dialogue, while occassionally entertaining, is unspiring and short whenever it isn't your generic RPG speech about a damsel in distress followed by some surprised responses from the protagonists.
The puzzles were decent; Not extremely complicated, but nothing you really get done in two seconds at every single one you see, either. That said, both the elements you use through them, as well as most of the platforms and enemies are recycled a little bit more than they should; and with such a

I was constantly expecting to find more interesting backgrounds, such as maybe a city (which you don't see any of past Zoya's introductory chapter) or any non-goblin (they really beat the idea to death here) related fortress at some point.
Another thing is that one of the three playable characters, the comic relief knight dude, was probably the least useful or interesting character out of the three avaliable. His sole purpose was for the sake of making the (extremely stupid) combat system easier and destroying certain walls.
All in all, I can't really say I enjoyed it. It was a very inetresting take on platformers, and during the few times you could see something besides forests or fungi-infested swamps or caverns, it was gorgeous. The music is something else I can moderately praise, but other than that, I'd honestly want to have my money back.

GTA V's single player is really cool, the gameplay is fantastic and may offer the pinnacle of open world game play.
I thought the story was a bit short and some aspects of it shallow compared to the likes of Red Dead Redemption but it still a decent single player campaign.
Modding games can greatly enhance the gameplay experience and can drastically transform the game.
Players have total freedom with their game and can have even more fun with the world Rockstar has created.
There’s so much mods which transform the gameplay, you can even find or create mods which make gameplay adjustments such as adding fuel simulation to vehicles. You can also have mods which add new weapons and vehicles to the game. I also know of a mod where someone is developing a split-screen modification for the game, so you can play with your friends from the same computer should this mod be completed!
If you want to survive in a Zombie Apocalypse you can also do it!
The Online mode has various issues such as glitches, bugs, long loading times, connectivity problems and online cheaters running around causing havoc and disrupting the experiences of other players. There has been some times when an update releases and you have peaceful sessions without these crazies running around, but then sometimes they're out in full force. Unfortunately the anti-cheat system they use in this game appears to be greatly ineffective, possibly due to the Peer to Peer nature of GTA Online.
The grinding in this game can be really tough, I find the grinding in this game harder than all of the many MMOs I have played. Seriously, it's insane! It looks like the game has been designed to maximise the playtime of players, putting many hurdles in their way as they try to grind, be it players or the how some missions are designed to slow you down.
One way of grinding in the game is selling some stock that you have accumulated from things like illegal drug operations and the selling of weapons. But you have to do this in a public session, a public session where other players can destroy your stock which you may have spent hours getting together. Seriously, hours! As to accumulate the stock you have to source supplies, by stealing them or buying them and then waiting for your stock bar to fill up. People can also destroy your stocks and supplies and get rewarded for it so those hours can just go to waste and cause much grief to players.
You’ll want to bring friends with you on the grind to speed things up, as grinding solo can be slow and risky, I encourage you to obtain a vehicle warehouse as it is one of the most profitable ways of grinding in this game, with it you have to source and sell vehicles.
If you can bring some friends along with you that’s great, as you can sell 4 cars at once which can make you a nice amount of money. But there will be players who will want to destroy your efforts.
Heists are another thing you may want to participate in as you can make a nice amount of money as well.
Not only is the grinding incredibly long and hard, but the prices of some of the new content additions are so high that it would take many hours for you to obtain. As I said before, it looks like the game has been designed to maximise the playtime of players, due to this design shark cards can become alluring to those who want to save themselves from the stress of grinding.
About cheaters, for the longest time it looked like Rockstar weren’t serious about combating cheaters but now it looks like they’re taking this more seriously.
Unfortunately, as a result of this seriousness the single player modding community has come under attack from Take-Two. OpenIV is a single player modification tool which is predominantly used to modify the single player portion of the game, the team behind it had a C&D (Cease and Desist) sent to them on allegations that their modding tool affects the online mode of the game and supposedly allows third parties to defeat the security features of their software. Losing this tool would do great harm to the single player modding community. They’re going after the wrong team, they should be going after the people creating online mod menus/cheats!
Unfortunately, I’m leaving a negative review.
This is due to the issues with the Online mode such as the bugs and glitches that haven’t been fixed, the seemingly unstoppable cheaters due to the ineffective anti-cheat system, and the attack on the single player modding community. Should one or more of these things improve I’ll adjust my review.
I want to give this game a positive review but it has so many issues, mostly pertaining to GTA Online that I can’t say I recommend playing this game for GTA Online, and if the single player modding community is under attack I can’t recommend it because it’s so wrong to attack this community and it harms the single player experience that people have spent over 2 years building upon and improving. Fortunately Rockstar has spoken up for the modding community recently and has said that they’re not going to pursue various single player mods, this is really good, hopefully OpenIV can make a return!
I could probably write a novel about this game, and the issues the online mode has, I’m just scratching the surface with the things I’ve mentioned in my review. I really wish they would fix the problems in GTA Online. :(
Review Update 30/08/2017:
Rockstar and Take-Two have backed away from attacking the single player modding community, I’m now leaving a positive review mainly for the single player portion of the game. The gameplay is phenomenal and this game offers some of the greatest gameplay in an open world game ever, this is enhanced greatly further by mods.

GTA Online still has various issues but there is fun to be had, if you do play it I highly recommend playing GTA Online with friends as a solo experience can be quite challenging depending on what you’re doing. Otherwise I don’t recommend playing GTA Online but it’s up to you as an individual, you may like it.
I’ve had fun playing GTA Online in the past but it’s just becoming more hectic and there are still various issues with the online mode, and unfortunately the grinding is still insane.
What bothers me quite a lot is that Rockstar encourages causing other players grief, this is done by players destroying things such as the stock you have spent time accumulating in free mode to try and make some money. There’s no repercussions for theses hostile players, only rewards which aren’t even worthwhile. And if you even think about getting revenge, destroying their weaponized vehicle is going to cost you.
The Oppressor, a recently added weaponized vehicle is one of the worst things you can encounter, it’s a nimble bike which can glide through the air with the help of the thruster on its back. Sounds great right? No, this nimble bike can fire homing missiles at you while you’re minding your own business and decimate you in seconds. You could be on your grind, trying to sell some stock when someone decides “Oh this player is trying to make some money, let me blow them up and get shillings for it!” The location of what you’re trying to sell is broadcasted to all the players in the session so they have the opportunity to destroy it and cause you grief, the rewards aren’t even worthwhile.
The game also has a variety of imbalances, one of which is that the health your character has is dependent on your rank, as a result lower ranked players are at a huge disadvantage as they can be killed quicker than higher ranked players, if I recall correctly this spreads across the whole of GTA Online, from free mode to death matches, I’m not sure if it spreads to all of the death matches though.
I don’t like the direction the free mode of GTA Online is heading, you spend a lot of time grinding just to have it all blown away by some big meanie in a death machine.
But if you put the grinding aside and play some of the many game modes you can have fun.

I will start out by saying there have been times I have enjoyed GTA5 but sadly that has all been tainted by a recent ban and recent from the online section with no reason given but I can only assume from having been in a game with hackers who dropped cash on me. I'm not usualy the type to go in for these negative review waves but this was the straw that broke this camel's back and since I have some spare time now, I will break down main the issues I have with GTA5:
1. If your game has hackers in it, why not fix it rather than simply banning everyone who comes into contact with them.
-seriously, why is there a $40k item in the game with seemingly no legitimate reason for its presence?
2. The recent single player mod bans by T2 (even if Rockstar did talk them out of this, we don't know what really went down)
3. The loading times - I really won't miss these. Not just the initial load times but the amount of time spent waiting between matches in playlists.
4. The number of disconnects - hardly a session went by without being disconnected from playlists or mid game to be faced with another long loading screen or more often than not face a loading screen that hung indefinitely.
5. The apparent greed in the pricing of online content. Yes, in theory all content online can be gained freely through a process of grinding but for someone who doesn't have hundreds of hours to sink into a game, much of the content was locked to me unless I succumbed to the evil that is:
6. The Cash Cards - I will start by saying that I can understant the principle of having cash cards - they help fund further development and can provide a way to avoid the grind for those whose time is worth more than their money. However the pricing is excessive. Lets take the example of the super yacht - a base price of $6M, to buy this with cash cards the cheapest option would be the $8M card. With the current sale that would be a cost of £36 in real cash, MORE than the base cost of the game! Outside of the sale we would be looking at a cost of £60, more expensive than the release price of a brand new AAA title on steam - for a virtual yacht with no significant gameplay value. Even in a less extreme case a good car with mods would set you back £12+ in terms of real money. The recent gun running update added some fun new toys that could set you back over £100 to buy unless you can devote hundreds of hours to grinding. No wonder T2 and R* are so touchy about hacked cash.
As the official description notes: "Cash is king in this town"
I have more, smaller issues with the game but in all honesty I might one day play a few rounds in the future. But my quest for virtual content is ended. I will devote no more time to accruing virtual currency and I will never buy a cash card; this is perhaps the main reason why T2 and R* won't give a damn about this but for me their reputation will forever more be sullied.

If you've been a fan of the franchise since the first Deus Ex, then you'll enjoy this installment as well. Yes, the game has a few issues here and there, such as the massive technical issues the game had at launch, and the extremely controversial microtransactions, but that doesn't mean the game itself isn't fun. Many of the bugs have been fixed with patches, and while I personally don't agree with it and feel as though it's a bad addition, the microtransactions are just there to assist you when you're in a bind. However, I've heard that the microtransactions you purchase only sticks with you through one game playthrough, which adds insult to injury in some manner, but if you play through the game, explore all possibilities at obtaining XP, and are smart with your praxis purchases, you'll never need to buy any.

Well, finished it, and have to say - the impressions are mixed.
It is definitely Deus Ex, with all expected attributes. However, when you look closer it appears that although all parts are in place each individual one is a bit shallow (mainly because of product "DLC business model").
Overall story leaves the feeling of deja vu, key characters are sketchy, some of gameplay mechanics are questionable ("Q"), maps look artificial and far-fetched (Prague is the worst). And one of the biggest dissapointments is rough contols, specifically mouse finese&sensitivity.
On the bright side - the overall game world feeling is good, music is authentic - "deus-ex like", visuals are satisfying.
Even with a short and shallow story - I'll give it 8/10, just because it is Deus Ex and I am a fan.
But for regular players (giving all the flaws of the game) it probably would be only 6/10.

Revolution Ace is an Old School bullet hell inspired game, but with a couple modern twists.
The core gameplay itself is basically the same, lots of enemies and lots of bullets, and you gotta shoot them all down.
And at the end of the level there is a lovely boss battle awaiting your arrival.
If you are a fan of bullet hell shooters, this is a sure go for you.Especially since this game possesses a few extra things to it.Like ground targets, a level up system, bizarre water physics, a nice co-op mode, a versus mode, an "offline" versus mode(basically like a highscore system, where you challenge your friends to beat it) and Hank your trusty engineer.
If your not a fan and got some spare cash, you might just give it a try, it is a nice and fun time killer.But the main campaign does drag itself a bit, possibly due to the leveling mechanic.
The game can also double as a nice bonding experience with a brother of friend due to some stages an insane mode being quite challenging, thus possibly requiring the aid of a partner to best them.
All in all it's a solid game, but it haves some issues, but it stays true to the genre besides it's added components.
I'd recommend it, but don't expect a masterpiece.

Very nice tactical minigame. You can hire marines, equip them with 7 different weapons, build 7 offensive/defensive buildings and 7 research buildings which provide passive buffs. All of those have to be unlocked by completing missions and buying it in the shop. The shop also offers one use buffs for the next mission such as extra marine or a weapon (you normally get them in game by using your resource points).
Nice thing is that you can pause the game and issue orders. Missions are rather short, they take usually a few minutes, however whenever you destroy aliens hive they mutate and generally become stronger. There are dozens of various mutations. I had one mission which took me about an hour and when I destroyed 9th of the 10 hives the aliens became so strong that they crushed me. However, I still got a pretty decent reward ($89k instead of $90k I would get for a victory) as it was random side mission, not campaign (in those you get reward only for victory).
The game doesn't have full screen mode, however if you set the resolution to your screen's resolution, the window will be placed correctly - i.e. you will not see the window's borders and the bottom will not be cut. This is a very nice thing especially for multi screen setups.
There are some minor interface bugs, soldiers (and aliens) occasionally get stuck when walking close to walls, but it doesn't kill the fun. It's a good game.
PS I really recommend buying Trickster's Arsenal DLC - it adds special actions such as rally point, grenades, teleport, stimpack etc. Also a few extra side missions and new alien structure.

Honestly, a really great little gem. Controls as strong, it's easy to understand, and the final package is a great mix of shoot'em up with difficulty that definitely makes you happy to succeed, though occaisionally it does go a little over the line.
I still recall one of my toughest battles. It was a side mission, where you had to wipe the map clean of aliens. The game works, essentially, by taking over base points, most of which are already under alien control, and they are spread across the map. However, you get a relative handful of soldiers(you can buy some more), while aliens spawn in infinite, encroaching hoards that move toward your bases in insane numbers. They may be weak, but I usually get tens of thousands of kills on the later missions, easy.
Back to the side mission. The bases occaisionally get mutators as they are destroyed. This mission, they had a mutator that spawned a beast on base destruction which could spawn another base elsewhere. This power combined with some other bases caused a 3 or 4 base spawn pileup in one corner of the map.
It was a nightmare - My troops were slugging it out non-stop, guns always firing at the oncoming hoard, and whenever I pressed them, they has ANOTHER mutator that made them spawn extra bugs when attacked.
RESULT: complete insanity. Eventually, I broke them, but DANG was it rough. However, it was certainly satidfying, and it's a game that makes you be strategic about your troops, weapons, and emplacements against an unrelenting adversary.
8.5 or 9 out of 10. (MINEFIELD FOR THE WIN)

This is a great game, probably my favourite RTS. Solid gameplay where you take a squad of marines around destroying aliens and their hives, but combined with some tower defence elements where you protect your own bases or the chokepoints leading to them and upgrade your abilities. The interface is crisp and well thought-out, it's well-balanced with the marine types and upgrades, and it's kept interesting by the aliens mutating to adapt to your tactics, but you can also always recycle everything to change your tactics accordingly. It also has great sound effects. Tactical and fun - you can't go wrong for the price.

OLD REVIEW: This game feels like a really lite version of Starcraft, which isn't a bad thing.  It's really easy to pick up, and is a lot of fun. I'd thoroughly recommend it for full price. If it's on sale, it's an even better deal.
I've been reworking some of my reviews, to be slightly better. As you can see above, my original review was pretty uninformative.
So when I think of this game, I think of it as a Starcraft Lite. What I mean when I say this is Starcraft is a very skill heavy RTS game; it has kind of a high skill floor. Infested Planet does not. It's a top down RTS that's very simple.
You start with a base and a few marines, and some money to spend on the marines or your base. Your objective is to capture all the points on the map (usually, campaign stuff varies). You'll have to kill the bugs in your way to do that. To do this, you can upgrade your units via indirect upgrades (buildings that upgrade your marines) or directly upgrade your marines. You can spend money to change your starting marine from a marine to a flame trooper, or a scout, or a shotgunner. From there, you can send your marines to their death, just to have them respawn in roughly 10 seconds. Your army constantly replenishes. If you have 5 marines, and they all die, they'll respawn at the nearest control point after a short timer. They keep their classes and everything. So marines dying really isn't that big of a deal. If you also decide you don't like building A, and you don't like that the one marine is a flame trooper, you can refund both, and get all your money back. The game is very flexible, in regards to what you can quickly do to change your strategies.
There are also commander abilities you can use by using commander points. Commander points slowly come back, or you can pick up items in the game that refresh it. The abilities all do different things, like a helicopter strike. All of them can be incredibly useful, depending on your end goal.
This game also has dlc that adds some more abilities for you to use. I bought it for $2.50 and it was totally worth it.
If you want a simple but fun RTS, I'd highly recommend picking up this game. It's a good bargain at the price.

Classic Mahjong. You don't know japanese? That's unnecessary. You don't know its rules? This could be a good starting point.
They could have made a classic mahjong game, with tiles organized with random schemes but actually the game starts with a girl walking on a path looking for her beloved. You will stop sometimes to talk to some characters that will give some words of wisdom, or because reasons, and in that moment a new mahjong scheme will pop up. The game really starts from the basics, and slowly progresses and increases difficulty explaining new rules and situations. This makes the game a good starting point to learn how to play mahjong.
Made with unity, it doesn't exactly shine in any way, models are low-poly, textures are simple and there are no particular lighting or effects. However it does its job and doesn't get stuck nor crashes.
Music is simple and quiet but not outstanding. Even though the purpose is to relax while playing I've heard older games with better music better fitting a japanese traditional game like mahjong.
Not much, the only thing is that the sidestory doesn't capture too much attention and the difficulty curve is very slow as it takes various sets to get to more complicated and challenging schemes. The biggest risk is for those who already know mahjong like me, who would just like to play it, but have to start from zero.

Great hack-n-slash game.
Reminds me a lot of the PSP game Untold Legends, but considerably better.
Pros:
-Original. You can tell someone (or a group) spent a lot of time thinking up this world.
-Well-made. Responsive keys, movements, attacks, once you get use to the click-to-act mechanics. Shift-click and Ctrl-click help a lot.
-Good Graphics. Not perfect, but very detailed and colorful.
-Character System. How much damage you take/do and why you take/do it is very complicated and varies widely based on several factors. This game lays it all out for you on an accessible in-game screen (available even while you're fighting). Now you know exactly why you fumbled that hit, or why that new enemy is doing so much damage, or how to improve yourself exactly how you envision.
-Items. The number of items in this game is mind-boggling.
Cons:
-The click-to-act style of play doesn't respond very well for those who want to continuously run a certain direction and shoot in another. WASD is my preferred method of movement, so this was frustrating.
-If you set your pet to "aggressive", it's like your pet is the main character and you're just it's sidekick, particularly on Casual difficulty. Very entertaining but frustrating if you wanted to actually get to kill something yourself..... Then you give your pet spells, and the game's as good as done.
-Almost impossible to get a full set of special armor the first go-around. There are so many different sets and so few drops that you basically have to have multiple characters looking for any special pieces and putting them in the Shared Box, and eventually you'll get a set. Any by the time you're finished with the set, it's obsolete for your more powerful characters, so you have to pick it up with a new or low-level character.
All in all:

As a fan of the anime, I do like the game; however, this is not worth the price, especially for those who haven't seen RWBY.
Fun at first, but quickly gets boring. Very shallow.
Each character can counter attacks depending on the situation. There will be a heads-up for this.
Heavy attacks and plain strikes can be inflicted. The combos are consecutive, the same everytime.
Jumping, dodging, and sprinting are all possible.
Aiming is automatic. The first few shots will be a plain ranged hit. When repeated enough, a special ranged attack is activated. For example, Blake will launch a crescent with an AoE that knocks back enemies. This pattern remains the same.
Each hero has their own ultimate which they can activate if provided enough energy.
When fully depleted, the player is vulnerable to being killed. Think of this as a regenerative shield.
The player can invest points into upgrading their passives and abilities. This is a streamlined tree.
The campaign can take around 4 hours to complete depending on what difficulty you play on.
Your objective will be repetitive, but the voice-acting and setting at least make it more bearable.
: Either protect something, or kill everything. Rarely anything unique will happen, for example, leading a time bomb away.
Even with others, the game can still become boring.
There are a few modes, but they feel the same as the campaign.
Survive, kill, protect. That's it.
The game lacks in content for its price.
DLCs also limit players from what should be free.
The game looks great with its vibrant art style.
I haven't experienced any performance or bug issues.
6/10
Only buy if you're a fan who would like to support Rooster Teeth, otherwise you will be disappointed.

A truly fantastic nostalgia trip back to the world of jet fighter games.
Had a brill run through on this game, got to Campaign +2 in about 10 hours, then went ahead and started challenging people. If anyone has played the SNES game Super Strike Gunner, then this game is for you, it feels exactly the same as SSG did when I played it all those years ago.
There are some very nice ideas in this game, the verses and battle modes where you can compete against players are very fun indeed, along with the customizing of your aircraft, perk system, leveling system and NG+, it does give the game some replay-ability, although when you reach later levels (20+), I found the game just turned into level-grinding to get those extra perk levels.
There are some arguably minor bad points I got from this however, the main one being how short the game actually is. While I personally don't mind a nice casual game to pass the time, a little more content and a more challenging difficulty would have helped a bit, (you can easily go straight to the highest difficulty setting and ace the game).
Another point I would like to mention is how easy the achievements are to get, while some may see this as a good thing, some hunters might not enjoy the lack of challenge in acquiring the full set of achievements, again though I think this is more about personal preference than anything.
Overall I was very happy with the game, even at full price I would have still bought this when it came under my radar, so 96% off was a total bargain for me. Putting the minor issues aside, I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a nice casual game of this genre without a doubt, especially if you enjoyed SSG and the like all those years ago.
In conclusion, my personal rating for Revolution Ace is :
8.5/10

Revolution Ace is an astonishingly enjoyable arcade shoot-em-up.
The graphics is at full HD 1920 x 1080p and there is eye candy in abundance with a huge array of effects and transitions.
Playing with an X-box 360 controller is fully supported and the game play is fluid and accessible.  There are four difficulty settings to cater for players of varying skill levels.
The menu system is well laid out and easy to use.
The sound tracks are great metal riffs providing a good audio adrenaline pulse.  Game sounds are well sampled and well synchronized with what is observed on screen.
Stages have beautifully textured terrain and plenty of variety.  There are a good assortment of units to destroy including air units, ground vehicles and turrets.  Buildings and terrain take damage too.  Floating collectible bonus spawns on destruction of certain units or buildings.
This game is well polished and has a good replay value.
Rating  9.5 / 10

Let me start off this review by saying this, 'Clumsy Fred' is an absolute masterpiece, probably the best game of our generation. It has universal themes of perserverance, the human spirit and living life to the fullest, while having a beutiful story, and amazing gameplay. The game is clearly an alagory for the life of a disabled man, presumably named Fred, we follow him on his adventure through life, as he faces life's challenges of education, love, work and getting by in this busy planet we call home. Trial after trial, the game tells his story through intriguing and immersive gameplay. The game has friendship, hardship, love, heartbreak, all packaged into this breath-taking odyssey called 'Clumsy Fred'. In the game you must pass several levels, each one a metaphor for the challenges this disabled man, Fred, is facing. Sometimes you'll just get stuck in mid air for no apparent reason, some would call this a bug, those people clearly don't understand this game, these instances are a metaphor for when life just throws something at you, for no reason whatsoever, just to put an obstacle in your way. The developers of this game are extremely creative, and msasters of storytelling, and making fun gameplay. In some levels you must take it slow and steady, in others you must rush and act on impulse, without accidently tripping or falling, thus failing a level, such is life is it not? Some levels are literally just the former one but backwards, or adding on a little extra bit to make it different. Some would call this lazy, those people are wrong, once again the developers incorporate even more symbolism, these levels are metaphors for how life becomes repetitive and boring for exampel at a desk job, wasting away each day as you come to the office, sit in your chair, do the same thing you did yesterday, and never changing. This is how life can end up if you don't live it to the fullest, another theme in the story. One could say that the entire game, is about a man trying to live life to the fullest, while having to battle his dissability, about how a disabled man lived more of a life, than millions of normal people with oppurtunnities Fred never had, who ended up wasting away in an office chair. Later into the game you come across a trampoline like mechanic, which takes an extremely long time to figure out, and even longer to use correctly and pass levels, once again this is done on purpose by the developerts to show even more symbolism, this further symbolises Fred's dissability, and how things that should be easy to use and control, are made nearly impossible, yet he still pushes on, time and time again. One of my favorite things about the gameplay is that it jsut chucks you in the game without telling you how to play at all, meaning that you complete nearly the entire game not knowing there are controls that could've helped you beat it in half the time, once again an amazing idea by the developers, because real life there aren't instructions telling you how to live and how make life easier, you have to figure everything out yourself, especially as someone who is disabled like Fred. This also gives the player complete creative control on how to complete levels, because the game doesn't baby you around or tell you how to play at all actually, which is really great. The story this game tells is absolutely beutiful and I wont lie, it brought many a tear to my eye, there's something for everyone in this game and so I would highly reccomend it to people of all ages, all races, all genders. I have no idea why this game is so cheap, for a game of this quality I would sell my house, my computer, everything, to play this amazing game. To end this review im going to say, do not trust negative reviews of this game, those people clearly weren't smart enough to understand and enjoy this game, no, this ART!

I guess it's about time I wrote a review for one of my favourite games of all time.
I've been cycling through my list of steam games; after logging thirty-or-so hours on each, I have come back to M&B Warband. I originally intended on waiting until the second installment of the series—Bannerlord—but I couldn't help myself. Some important facts for review readers on whether or not I recommend you to buy it:
1. This game released in 2010. It is now Q4 2017, and I still find it fun.
2. Mods are still very active. This gives the player almost endless replayability.
3. The learning curve is not very steep. At the beginning, I thought it was a little tough to get my mercenary band started without constantly getting pillaged. However, you get the hang of it really quickly.
4. The battles don't have much in the way of tactics, but there is a certain satisfaction to be had when fighting alongside the troops you so lovingly hired.
5. Sieges are pretty fun, if not a bit dumb. The troops just storm up tiny latters to the castle walls and pretty much instantly die, but it's cool to feel like you're trying to take over a medieval castle. Also, it is very advanced for its time. I can still barely believe they made this seven years ago.
6. Stop reading and just buy it already. The game doesn't have 98% positive ratings for nothing.

1. It's not that flashy and crowded (e.g. too much lighting, flashing bomb, etc.). I personally like this.
2. Gameplay,

Reviews down here are pretty weird. I'm not sure what people expect or what the big problem is.
But i found Human Revoltion much less amazing then others. DE Human Revolution had two serious problems:
1. Levels were almost exclusively office/industry buildings, often looking almost identical,which got INCREDIBLY boring later on! Also a cheap way to stretch a game. For some HR was apparently longer then MD.... (see point playtime below)
2. MAssive XP advantage for stealth style but then Boss fights absolutely annoying and frustrating for stealth skilled/geared players. I wouldnt have minded the one without the other. Both together were a massive problem.
----
BOTH problems don't exist anymore in Mankind divided! Levels are more versatile and different now, so are Boss fight(s). allowing different approaches. You're not locked suddenly in a tiny area, suddenly forced to play Call of duty.
The final fight offers options for shootery players, for stealthy players AND has an option not to kill him at all. THAT is the Deus Ex way.
This isn't Dark Souls. I don't see how the number of  Boss fights is suddenly a rating criteria for a Deus Ex game. If so then the annoying action Boss fights in HR are a clear negative for that!
Which makes Mankind divided actually all in all  very good. Gameplay wise it's BETTER then Human Revolution.

People seem to run thorugh the game and then complain that it's too short.

Maybe i'm a bit slow but its completely beyond me how someone can finish the game first time, normal playstyle in 20hrs or less.

I loved Deus Ex: Human Revolution.
With that said, there are a few things that really let this one down which is a shame. The first big one is the story. In my opinion it tries a bit too hard to be deliberately overcomplicated, with so much name-dropping that I personally couldn't remember who's who. The story didn't pull me in like HR's story did.
The game also ends quite abruptly, very obviously "halfway" through the story with the rest coming in the sequel (which Eidos Montreal have been working on for the past 2 years already. UPDATE: Future Deus Ex games have been put on indefinite hiatus by the publisher.) It doesn't even wrap things up like, say, at the end of a season of a good TV show. Instead, imagine a great episode of a TV show just stopping after the second commercial break (with an indeterminate wait until you can watch the second half.)
The game is beautiful, but there seems to be a lack of variance in the locations compared to in HR, and the areas you go to just seem less... vibrant.
Next we get on to the shady business practises. Microtransactions in a full priced game are instant thumbs down from me. I'm sure this has nothing to do with the clever, talented folks at Eidos and everything to do with the greedy suits at Squeenix but it smells all the same.
With that said, if you liked the core gameplay loop of Human Revolution you'll probably like Mankind Divided. If you liked HR for the story you might come away a bit disappointed. If I were you, I'd wait for all the inevitable story DLC to come out and then buy the game at a deep discount.

What is there to say? If you enjoyed Human Revolution, you will enjoy Mankind Devided.

From someone who played the original micromachines on the megadrive back in the 90s, I have waited some time now for someone to do a remake of the old classics. So now here in 2017, we finally have Micromachines World Series!
So, is it good? The short answer is yes, but it could be a lot better.... I don't expect too much from games like this so I'm not disapointed when things don't live up my own expectations but at its core, its very much micromachines all be it with few tweaks here and there to add more of a competative game to it with the inclusions of powerup weapons which I feel is actually a nice feature. Your constantly battling it out for these powerups while trying to stay on the track with the many obsticles along the way.
The race tracks themselves (maps/levels) are really well done, the graphics really are superb in my opinion, their bright, vibrant and really make the tracks pop out! For me personally, hard to pick out a fav track but they all look really good, they all play amazingly well and definitely bring back the nostalgia from the original games.
It does however, lack game modes and the menu could really do with some work as its nice to look at, but in order to play just a regular race without powerups, you have to load into local play rather then just simply an AI match and set it up through the multiplayer menu and play solo. I also didn't see an option to add more AI to matches there either, the only way to get a full match is to simply play singleplayer vs AI from the main menu but of course you loose all control of maps to choose from to play as well as not being able to disable the weapons if you wanted. Right now there is Race/Battle mode and Elimination game types, which I feel they just simply need more game modes and few more maps/tracks but I don't know if there are any plans to add more down the road.
It does have loot boxes for various upgrades on the vehicles in the game, you get them by just simply playing the game, there is no microtransactions here, but there is currency in the game which you use to unlock skins for the vehicles (for which there is a TON!) voice sounds for each vehicle which the chatter during the game the matches and decals... All above board in my opinion,
Not many playing Online Multiplayer though which is probably this games biggests downfall as this really is a MP centric game so go into this game not looking for loads of options the online stuff... Play with friends......
I may add to this review at a later date but for now I would rate this a 6/10 game. Its micromachines, not Gran Torismo or Fortza, so its very much a pickup and play game, very arcadey its in form and treat it as such. You can get a lot of fun for a few hours at a time and its much more fun when you play with friends and the banta you can rage at eachother leaves for some hillarious gameplay but the game is just simply too expensive for what it is really.
At 30$ that is a tall ask for a game like this where it only has a few hours of gameplay in it at a time in short bursts but what gameplay is here, is a lot of fun and I don't regret buying it.

A great game that I cannot reccomend enough. I bought it on a whim this afternoon when I wanted something new, and Steam recommended this based on a game I've got nearly 300 hours logged on (100 in the last 2 weeks). I've basically played this for 6 hours straight now, and if I didn't have to get up for work in the morning, I'd probably do another 6 happily.
Interface is so intuitive that there's virtually no tutorial. You can look key bindings up and there are tooltips on controls that tell you them too. Its a game thats fast enough to keep your brain active, but laid back enough that you can watch or listen to something else at the same time. Some missions are randomly generated, so that gives a lot of replayability, and there is a great spectrum of difficulty and types.
The basic principal of every level is "destroy the bug hives", but so far I've hit 3 principals. One is your standard story mission, not much to explain there, its the plotline. The second is a kind of time trial mode - you start with a clock, when it runs out, you're done. The more bugs you kill, the more you get paid. Every time you take out a hive, you get more time, and if you clear them all, then you get bonus pay. The last type is a standard annihilation mission, but almost every time you take out a hive, the aliens mutate (effects are very varied, from upping their counter attack speed when you take a hive location to aliens that spawn towers when they die, hives fighting back directly, etc). So far, I've not even cleared the second tier of that level because while an individual hive isn't too challenging to take down (though it is a real meat grinder), its when you hit groups of 3 hives at once that things get interesting. I've sent air strikes, cluster bombs and my entire squad at them and the best I can get so far is a meat grinder where neither of us win.

Despite generally poor reviews I actually really enjoy this game. The gameplay is quite fun. It's very fast paced and the controls are easy to pick up - which is good because the game just throws you into the fray with no tutorial or even a keymap screen. I've played mostly with a 360 gamepad, and that's what I'd recommend but the KB/M controls aren't bad either. The graphics are very good, if not completely stunning. And buttery smooth on any halfway decent PC. (I'm running a G3258 @ 4.4GHz and an R9 380 2GB everything turned on, Ultra 1080p with a solid 60FPS) The game is also very challenging to play solo. But multiplayer is where grimm eclipse really shines.
Now for the bad:
The game has too little variety. There are only a few stages. Only a few different grimm and only 8 characters available with 3 costumes each. (Team RWBY & JNPR, battle, school and dance) And if you want to play anything other than team RWBY in battle attire you'll be buying the DLC. No sign of team CFVY, SNNN, CMNE, Ozpin, Qrow, Raven, Glynda, Taiyang, Torchwick, Adam or any of the multitude of less relevant characters. Though I can kinda see why. There are just so many characters in the RWBY that it'd bog everything down.
Overall: if you're a RWBY fan I recommend it. If you're not, wait for a sale as the gameplay is only average.

Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon
First thing first, this game, even named Far Cry 3, ain't related at all to the previously released Far Cry 3 game. This is a standalone game, hence, the BLOOD DRAGON title. Also, it does not require Far Cry 3 to play! Now that's been sorted out...
My take on this game... entertaining game filled with action and hysterical writing, Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon is an '80s-inspired blast. Everyone who's got a soft spot for the 80's era movies will find this game to be a love letter dedicated for you!
PROS:
+Terrific aesthetics of the 80's era... neons, lasers... all flashy!
+Michael Biehn (The Terminator, Aliens, Abyss, Navy Seals) voice acting your character!
+Awesome synthetizer music inspired from... you guessed it, the 80's era!
+Hysterical dialogue and collectibles
+Lots of smart references to 1980s pop culture
+Challenging Blood Dragons, especially early on!
+Smart levels and missions make for rewarding stealth
+A lot of terrific open-ended action for a great value.
CONS:
-Game is short, even if I took my sweet♥♥♥♥♥time, 9h is not much for a sandbox style game... I want more!
-The game crashed a few times on me... could be issues with either Uplay acting crazy and Nvidia beta drivers. At least, I haven't lost any progress since the game save pretty often!
RATING:
8.0 / 10
I recommend this game if you like cyberpunk and especially 80's style brought into  a game and also, if you want to play a game for just fun!!
PS. Michael Biehn hinted on some interview that there's more to be seen into the Blood Dragon world... so, guess we should be expecting a BD2 eventually! Longer too please!

On initial download and play my first impression was that the visuals in the game were a bit bland, lackluster, and that the concept felt somewhat empty, but after about two matches I've never been more attached or hyped for a game. I've been playing quite a lot of it since then and it's only grown on me more and more. On first impression the look and feel of the game is strange but once you get a bit of dirt under your nails it sticks with you. What looks like copy paste character design is balanced hit/hurtboxes so that nobody has an advantage due to size. What seems like a smash clone actually plays very much like its own game with its own rules. This is a deceptive title and I love it.
The devs for this game are also EXTREMELY lovely people, they constantly update it (about once a week) with balance changes, and patches. Alongside this, for a free to play game with a character unlocking mechanic via in game currency, it doesn't feel like it'll take a year to unlock a character, it'll take maybe a few hours, and you can get several unlocked within a week without spending a cent of actual money.
This is the best f2p experience I've had in ages, and one of the most stable experiences overall I've gotten to enjoy. I cannot wait for it to leave the (somewhat questionable) state of open beta. I say somewhat questionable because it feels finished. there's not anything missing and they're always adding more.
I will always have a place for Sims in my gaming heart. Love this game to pieces.

A short Half-Life 2 mod set in the same universe as the game, Transmissions: Element 120 brings a new spin on the Gravity Gun: instead of pulling objects towards you, you can use it to perform huge jumps, as well as sending a shockwave (represented by the AR2's Energy Ball) that'll blow up sending stuff all over the place. I must say the new version is quite interesting, adding more mobility to the game, and I'd love to see it explored further. Other than the new Gravity Gun, the rest of the mechanics are just what you'd find in Half-Life 2, with the same guns and the same enemies. Still, it's good to see something new set in the Half-Life universe.
As for the story, it's quite minimal. You wake up in some sewer filled with headcrab zombies, and you must fight your way out, encountering Combine soldiers along the way. I'd say this mod benefits from having a minimalist story, with small bits thrown here and there through journals you can find.
The soundtrack is pretty good. It reuses some of the tracks from Half-Life 2, but it also has some new ones. They all help setting the mood of the game; and what a mood that is! The game is set at night, and there's not a lot of light in the place you're in. Not to mention that the game actually encourages you not to use your flashlight. This can lead to some scares, since, as I mentioned above, the place is filled with zombies.
Well, since this is a short game, this will be a short review. I recommend this game.

Despite it having some fairly big flaws, I would definitely recommend this MM outing. I think some other reviewers have touched upon it, but the reason it is receiving so many negative reviews is probably due to the price. It seems a lot compared to the "free" MM game I am currently playing on mobile, but when you factor in all the potential micro-purchases in that version, it's similarly priced.
Unlike the progression system in the mobile game, here you are given a load of vehicles from the beginning. I don't know if these will be added to or not, but they appear to be upgradeable via a loot system. For some reason, the upgrades I've won are only cosmetic - audio samples, skins etc - and again not sure if they'll be power-up upgrades available at some point. They don't all perform the same, as some reviewer suggested, but they are very similar it's true. I guess this is to make the 12 vehicle races a bit fairer.
The races tend to feel a little samey and random, not least because I always find myself playing bots. I do play at odd times though. However, where the game wins my vote is in the battle modes. It is absolutely manic! Each vehicle has 3 imaginatitive unique weapons, all animated well and with satisfying effects! Again, there is always 12 players, but this time it's actually very playable even with AI. When there are more humans online this mode will be the centerpiece for sure. You get killed a lot, but respawning can be fun as there is a setting allowing spawning as a different vehicle each time. This mode genuinely raised my adrenalin levels - no mean feat for a low-skilled but veteran gamer such as myself!
To sum up, you should buy this game if you are a fan of the franchise, as there is more than enough fun for your hard-earned, if you take time to look. Try not to compare it with other versions - true, many of them are more playable, but this is a worthy instalment in its own right - SEE YOU IN BATTLE MODE!!!

As one who normally doesn't care for RTS games, I'm surprised to say that this game was INSANELY ADDICTING. The graphics are very good for the style of game it is (indie, clusterf*ck of aliens, etc). The gameplay is functional, with a unique resource system. In my 14.6 hours (as of writing this review), I found myself amazed at how they handled difficulty throughout the campaign.
Here's a quick rundown of how the difficulty scaling works throughout the campaign:
Before you have many upgrades, the game feels really simple. Enemies are relatively easy to deal with at the beginning, with little to no challenge.
Then in the middle of the game, things start to get a bit tricky. At this point, you need to develop a tactic that works for mostly any situation.
Late in the game, the difficulty SPIKES AND DOES SO VERY HEAVILY. The attack and defend style of gameplay becomes frantic, and you ABSOLUTELY MUST KEEP DEFENSES EVEN WHEN RUSHING ATTACK! I can't tell you how many times my progress was completely negated because of the enemies recapturing points I've taken.
The beginning draws your interest, the late game becomes the style of interest similar to games like Dark Souls!
For those who haven't played Dark Souls: the fun and interest in it comes from finding out how you need to set up to effectively beat a certain area/enemy. While it's never 1 enemy in Infested Planet, the similarities are more than there.
Summary: If you like RTS games, but would like the ability to have a more flexible playstyle and be required to do so, and would rather have a resource system that's more consistent and engaging, GET THIS GAME NOW. Adaptability is key in this game, and the resource system allows you to change out your tactic on-the-fly. I can't say much for the story (I don't play games for the story, and didn't pay attention over half of the time), but the rest works BEAUTIFULLY.
For an Indie game: 9.5/10
Overall rating: 8/10
Almost forgot: The way the different units are handled is quite nice. While the game may tell you that the heavy gunners are the most fierce fighters or something like that, you quickly find out that even they lack in certain areas. All of the troops have their purpose, and you won't win a mission with just 1 type of them later on. Knowing your troops is just as important as keeping track of your other upgrades/buildings.
End note: I do have the Trickster's Arsenal DLC. It says on there that it improves the campaign (along with adding other tools at your disposal), so I don't know what the game is like by itself. It's all of an extra $3 to get the Delux edition, so definitely go ahead and get that while you're at it. It's worth it. :)

This game is a bit hard to recommend to a good number of people. The game recycles the same campaign three times (With five different characters), which already repeats itself twice. There's going to be a lot of repetition, so you have to love the gameplay in order to get any enjoyment out of this game.
And thankfully, the gameplay is really polished despite some hickups regarding enemy and level design. The two characters you could play as originally, Nero and Dante, are still as fun and complex as they were in the original title. The three new charcters, Vergil, Lady, and Trish are great additions to the game. Well, at least Vergil is. Lady is alright, but the gun gimmick doesn't click with me. Really didn't care for Trish. Her gameplay was so shallow I couldn't stand to play as her for too long.
A criticism I have with this game is the optimization. The original Devil May Cry 4 was notable for being one of the only good PC ports Capcom has made. The port was so good in fact, that it was considered the definitive version of the title due to it's low requirements and the edition of Turbo mode and Legendary Dark Knight difficulty. Unfortunately, SE isn't as well optimized as the original. There's a lot of unnecessary post processing effects that make the game chug and stutter. You can't turn these off through normal means, so you'd have to look up a guide on how to remove those with a hex editor. I'm hoping Capcom releases a patch that better optimizes the game and adds more graphics options.
As I've said before, you'd need to REALLY love these sort of games if you want to get any enjoyment out of this. If you're the type of person that's in to hack n' slashes and has a relatively decent PC and a gamepad, try this game out and see what you think.

If you played DMC4 (second best to DMC3) then the SE is worth it.
Vergil is better than he was in the SE version of DMC3.
Trish and Lady are what we expected and more.

Nero's game play is amazing. The devil bringer is a really unique part of the combat and allows you to do actions that are otherwise not possible. Dante's mode switching is pretty good, but I find myself sticking to sword master mostly. I also wish you had more time to use Dante's new weapons. Final boss can be annoying with the boss constantly teleporting and flying around. But other than that the game was amazing. The combos and the style ranking keeps your blood pumping, the unlock able skills and abilities make you feel stronger as you play through the game. Also Vergil is a god like mother f*****. His weapons are all good, and his play style is different but very satisfying one. You feel truly powerful teleporting around and slicing up enemies, also the concentration bar keeps you aware of how many times you get hit. Lady and Trish are also pretty cool and unique, but Vergil is the real badass here. The thing that is most sad is that this game wasn't even considered 40% done. Dante and Nero were supposed to have their own story lines and Nero was supposed to eventually get a full demon devil trigger instead of the ghost he has. Not to mention that Lucifer, Gilgamesh, and Pandora were also supposed to be their own bosses, but instead he just get these weapons without a real back story. In conclusion, the combat is one of the best out there even to this date, but the story and levels will eventually become annoying to replay over and over. I hope they make a devil may cry 5 and get everything right.
P.S there shouldn't be any micro transactions, that is a big no-no. Capcom needs to stop that.

I have clocked over 900 hours of Warband on Steam. And probably around double that time before I had Steam. Mount&Blade Warband is among the longest lasting modder's paradise games there ever has been. It has the potential of remaining an active modding scene even after Bannerlord comes out.
Let's face the facts; the native gameplay is not that amazing, though it is easily all-consuming. The graphics are even bad if judged by today's standards. The mods are what makes Warband special. It is easily moddable, I've looked into it. By my estimate even I could, given enough time and patience, make a mod for this beautiful engine of mods.
Why am I writing this today? To get the bloody Steam badge for Awards nominations. But only because I thought I had written this years ago. I came to check on and update my previous review only to find out I had not written it before. The Labour of Love is the fitting category for Warband, IMO.
For new players (if such exist in this day and age), spend 50ish hours on native without utilizing the cheats to learn the game. Then move on to mods and grasp the true magnificience of Warband. Mod scene is stronger on moddb than it is on Steam, unfortunately. Especially, if you desire to play good multiplayer, go for the moddb versions of the mods since Steam apparently since has some issues with MP mod compabilities.
If you are looking for MP, go for Bear Force II. If fantasy is your thing, go for Persino or A World of Ice and Fire. Prophesy of Pendor is also a good option. If you just feel like browsing what the community has to offer, google Warband caravanserai or look at moddb's popular mods. There should be around 30 Warband mods in top 100 at any given time.

I completed this game in around 3 hours. That being so, 11 pound might seem a trifle steep... But it isn't, let me explain why.
The game is platformer with various puzzles that are all relatively easy to solve. You contrrol two characters: the little brother, and the big brother. You often have to combine the two to negotiate the challenges the landscape poses. For example; can't yank a lever with the little brother? Well you'll need the big brother for that then. Can't fit the big brother through some railings? Thats where you're little bro comes in handy.
Aside from these gameplay features, the game features a charming art style and a folkloric fantasy world which rarely deviates from standard scandinavian fantasy tropes.
So far it seems pretty standard fare, right?
Where this game succeeds is the way it builds a strong emotional connection between the player and the game's protagonists. No mean feat considering our protagonist are speaking a different language (no subtitles are offered either).
It's difficult for me to explain how the game does this so well without depriving you of the pleasure of experiencing it all first hand. All I can say is that this is a game about family and friendship, about adventure and companionship, and about those all too human emotions that require no vehicle of language for translation.
This game is a work of art. A benchmark for all game designers trying to connect their audiences with their creations.
Basically, just pay the 11 quid and thank  me later. You won't regret it.

This game is short but awesome.  The man responsible for creating this is a genius.  Each location is like a work of art and it has an element of mystery and a little bit of scariness.  I loved the secret helpful messages only visible in the dark, the codes on the walls, and the new Zombie AI.  The two coolest locations are the big zombie fight zone and the end fight, both of these locations are very large, open areas, but have no redundancy (i. e. repeated buildings, edge of the map is creative).  The entire game gives a feel of abandonement, like a war happened but it wasn't the war that made the inabitants leave.  The game is made with the Source engine, but it feels new because there is improved AI that act differently with changes in the environment, better physics for big objects, and a fanntastic lighting job that is the polish on the grimness cake. I actually like many of the locations in the game more than 80% of the locations in the whole HL series because the lighting made it look so good and the originality of the way the locations were built.  The music of the game can creep you out or get you pumped in a fight,  ten thumbs up to the music guy.   I honestly cannot find any flaws in this game, and for one man to make most of this game is incredible.  When (if) valve starts making HL 3 include the maker in the staff (unless they already started, in that case hire him now).  10 stars, three thumbs up, 250% rating.  The game they have made is beautiful.  My advice for playing this game: mute everything except the game (phone, music), turn off all lights, and try not to pause in the middle of fight scenes.  This way you can truly immerse yourself in the game.

I grabbed this in a bundle and installed expecting a basic mahjong game with a bit of a story glommed on and maybe some light RPG elements, something like a mahjong version of Regency Solitaire or Chef Solitaire. It is definitely a mahjong game with a bit of story, if you consider the character's proceeding from a monk to a couple more monks to her true love and hearing a couple stanzas of poetry from each a story. She walks from puzzle to puzzle, and while you solve she continually pulls something out of her pocket (presumably the one ring as often as she checks to make sure it's still there) in an animation that it took me a third of the game to realize wasn't her scratching herself. But of course all of that is just window dressing and is unimportant if the mahjong itself is good.
It's not. It looks and plays like the basic mahjong you can play on any number of free or paid apps on any number of platforms. But it's missing one aspect of those that I consider to be kind of crucial: IT'S NOT POSSIBLE TO LOSE! Without the possibility of failing this is really not so much mahjong as it is just matching things until the game is over. It has a shuffle button that never runs out and will continue to rearrange the tiles until you've cleared them all. Even if you whittle the game down to two matching tiles stacked on each other it will rearrange them so they can be cleared. After about a third of the game I sort of realized this and stopped playing strategically. After about half I started actively trying to make the worst possible matches in order to engineer a loss and see what happened. I failed miserably, the game just won't let you lose.

This is a variant of the typical mahjong games, with the exception that it is not restricted to the standard count of tiles. It starts of with simpler, one-layer puzzles, adds multiple levels, and after "midnight" starts making the puzzles more complex. It will use more than four of each tile, if it needs to; don't trust counting tiles to determine if any of a specific face are left. Play time for me is about seven hours end to end, but I'm pretty good at these sorts of games; only had to hit the shuffle button 4 times in all 74 puzzles. Note: It does autosave, but runs through the opening or midpoint "cinematic" every time it starts.

This game is just.... awesome!
Bear with me now and let me explain. First of all the trailers on the store page dont do justice to the game at all. I bought this one by just looking at price.
Turns out it's as good or in some areas even better than Jets'n'Guns which is my favorite shooter. Did not expect this at all from such a simple looking shooter.
A bit about the mechanics: game has a leveling system and scrap (money) you get from doing missions, multiplayer battle challenges etc. With these goodies you buy new gear and in the spirit of Jets'n'Guns it is pretty much mandatory to test things out and find the best setups. Skirmish missions can be done if you wish to grind for some extra scrap. Configurations do matter as the Campaign start becoming harder bit by bit but the real test are the awesome battle chains where you or someone lays out a challenge to others in form of a level completion replay. Others will try to beat your score and you will see in a replay how they did it. Fun starts when someone rips the score so high you really have to think how will i beat this. You might need to re-think your setup to beat the score. (Your opponent see how many times you tried to beat his score so dont humiliate yourself too much by trying a strategy that just doesnt work)  Eventually the score will climb very high as the same challenge is bounced back and forth until either side just gives up.
Multiplayer system is very good - though be warned that it is quite confusing to use at first.  Check forums.
Game also sports a interesting notification system where you get a message to your steam notifications bar that someone has beaten your score and it's your turn to try to beat the opponents score.
In order to not just praise the game there is a bit of criticism too: Lack of feedback everywhere is annoying. menus are unresponsive for some time too yet not greyed out. In missions hitting targets does not yield much of reaction. i'd also like to see a bit more animation frames on certain enemies for a more flowing visual game experience. And just what are those really tiny white walkers that fire missiles at you? No big things but give a rough feeling to the game.

My score: 9/10
An enjoyable RTS. It's kind of like playing Starcraft against the zerg. I appreciate that there are different strategies that you can play, and there is no one set way of playing the game "right." The AI mutates, which means you have to change your strategy on the fly, and you are able to do so because you can change character class, and buildings on the spot. The game is fast-paced, and there's no resource collecting.
Some problems with the game though is that it can be rubber-bandy. You take over one spot and another one gets taken over. You retake it, and the enemy regroups somewhere else... Another problem is that the 'tidying up' phase can be a bit drawn out. Not so bad that you're looking for one peasant hiding somewhere in the fog of war, but there's a point when you can say: "I won already, c'mon..."
Pros:
Various strategies work equally well.
Fast-paced.
Good variety of buildings and character classes.
Feels good gunning down waves of aliens.
No grinding or other time-consuming activities.
Cons:
The game is a bit short. But it has decent replay value.
Graphics could be better.
Controls are not as precise, or snappy as I would've liked.
Excellent game, worthy of it's price tag, and an even better deal if on sale.

At times it can be very challenging and it forces you to think on your feet, but personally I like to be challenged! I'd love to see more games like this and sincerely hope the creator will take the basic format of this game and run with it!

This game is fantastic!
I'm surprised by the negativity this game is getting. Mankind Divided improves upon Human Revolution's formula in every aspect. So let's just see what this game does right and what doesn't.
Pros:
+ ABSO-♥♥♥♥ING-LUTELY FANTASTIC LEVEL DESIGN! There are so many ways in doing each mission with lots of alternative routes that encourage different play styles. Want to hack through all security systems? Go ahead. Or do you want to go invisible and sneak past every guard? Fine. Or how about using a vent to bypass some of the security? And maybe you are getting tired of sneaking and want to unleash your inner cybernetic rage on some baddie's♥♥♥♥♥ You can do that. This whole level design is backed by the next point.
+ Which is the great customizability. Alongside the returning augments from HR some experimental powers introduced. With all these you can turn yourself into a guy who mostly uses his hacking capabilities to complete his mission. Or someone who can use his social skills to pass a challenge. Or maybe turn Adam into a diamond armored brute.
+ No more annoying boss fights which completely ruin your non-combat oriented playthrough. Sadly there's only one boss during the entire game but personally I prefer one good boss fight than 3 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ones.
+ The gunplay is much improved over HR. It still feels a bit sluggish though.
+ I found the side missions to be much, much more interesting than the ones in HR. In HR some of the side missions made me feel bored but in MD I loved them. Especially the one with the whole cult thing.
+ Great visuals. To sum it up; Mankind Divided's graphics range from "Ok, this place looks good for a 8th generation video game" to "HOLY♥♥♥♥♥♥IS THIS A MOTHER♥♥♥♥ING ARTWORK??!!". Places like Golem City or Prague during nighttime give you a satisfying eye-gasm. Although it isn't without its flaws. Lip Sync for example is ridiculously bad and also some of the character models could've been better.
+ The soundtrack is composed by Michael McCann. Nuff said.
+ The places you visit. Prague, while being the only hub in the game, is both bigger and much more detailed than both Detroit and Hengsha in HR and is really beautifully designed which gives you that great cyberpunk feeling. But my favorite thing about Prague is how believable it is which makes it resemble our real world. And Golem City... WOW. It's a shame that we only see this city during one mission as I hoped it would be a complete hub alongside Prague.
+ Elias Toufexis as Adam Jensen.
+ PC Port: Performance is ok. With most of the settings on Very High I was getting 50-60 fps with an i7 4790k, GTX 970 and 8GB of RAM. I know it isn't perfect but it's very far from terrible. I didn't experience a single crash, bug or whatever. Also this game gives you a lot of options for customizing the visuals which also another sign of a good pc port.
Cons:
- The story. The plot starts very promising with all those mysterious golden masked augs attacking you and for the most part is OK. But the ending makes the game's story feel unfinished. There are so many story threads unanswered by the end of the game which unofficially confirms a sequel. Some returning characters from both the original Deus Ex and Human Revolution are nice. But most of the new characters aren't really that interesting as the ones in the previous games.
- Some of the voice acting for characters such as Miller isn't done really well.
- New Game + is currently very buggy. When you start NG+ there's a chance that either you get more augs than you had or worse, have an aug like Typhoon locked away. This also applies to your inventory.
Overall I absolutely enjoyed my time with Mankind Divided and so far It's my favorite game of 2016. If you are a Deus Ex fan, you owe to yourself to buy this game right now.

I was about to change my review to "recommended" after the last update that fixed the crashing.
However, now it came to my attention that this game uses very sketchy DRM measures to prevent save files from being copied.
That's right, you didn't read it wrong. This game has save file DRM to protect their precious microtransactions.
That would be all good if it worked fine but, when does DRM ever works fine? Well then. If you have the misfortune to use any microtransaction items (including the bonus ones from preorder), then apparently, you're not allowed to reinstall your game or install it from another machine or, I'm not even joking here, even moving it to a different installation directory without losing your saves (and of course, your bonus items that you PAID for, since they are one-time-redeem only).
I'm speechless.
Game companies: If you spent less time and effort developing hideous DRM and spent that effort instead into making your game work, then maybe, just maybe, we wouldn't have all these day 1 apocalypse releases.
Just look at The Witcher 3, you can get it DRM free from GOG, and it works flawlessly. Now, go ask CD Projekt RED if they went bankrupt or something for not investing on hard DRM.

I enjoyed the game and would recommend it, but found a few aspects lacking. Comparing HR and MD isn't like comparing Deus Ex 1 and Invisible War, though. It's still a solid entry. I played on Give Me Deus Ex so some of these might differ in easier difficulties.
Pros:
-Graphics upgrades. The dialogue animations are a little stiff and I have seen some off lip syncing but the graphics are definitely a good upgrade even if a little behind. It looks good.
-Good acting from the main cast
-Still multiple approaches. I found multiple ways to tackle just about every objective. I never felt railroaded into one way unless I simply lacked the augs to take alternate routes which wasn't often. Definitely the games strongest point and what I expect from Deus Ex games.
-Prague is really fleshed out. I don't think I can level any criticism against it. One of the best hubs in a Deus Ex game. There's a lot to search. It's overwhelming but the side missions make you visit all of the major areas.
-Art style, themes, etc. No yellow filter, the familiar themes of techno Renaissance return, the advertisments that litter the street are really good and thought out (the pills flowing into the mouth was my favorite). Just a really cool setting.
-Music is just as good as HR.
-Combat improved. It's not a real selling point for me since I run stealth, but it's the best in any DE game so far.
Neutral:
-Praxis points are plentiful. I put this in neutral because some people will like it, some people will feel it's too generous. I fill out a good chunk of the augs, and was able to fight and stealth pretty evenly with a little leaning towards stealth. I think if you did absolutely everything and found every praxis kit you'd be able to complete the tree. Not sure though since I Wasn't able to.
Cons:
-No bosses. At least so far. I'm super bummed about this one. The Tyrants weren't great, but with some improvements we could have seen some great boss battles. Others might not feel so strongly since really none of the bosses were very good in the series. I think they should have tried to push that boundry.
Edit: There is a final boss. It's not bad, just a little too late. But for those who do non-lethal runs you can end it without killing him. I was hoping for a dialogue option, and there sort of is but it's not like you can reason with them.
-Only 1 hub. Prague is definitely fleshed out better than any previous hub but I would have preferred to see one of the acts take place somewhere else. London would have made a great hub after Prague but instead it was just a level.
-Characters don't really stick out. There's only one you interact with any kind of regularity. The rest come and go. I think Jensen is still on point but the supporting cast is just back drop. It was nice to see Sarif again, even if they changed his VA.
-Weapon selection is more limited. No rocket launcher, no energy weapons, no crossbow. There are a couple added in the form of the launced wrist blade and taser, and the PEPS was integrated into the aug tree, and different ammo does add some interesting tactics. Still, in previous games you could use weapons to replace augs you didn't take to give you a good amount of flexibility and here it feels more limited.
-None of the non-hub settings are particularly memorable. There was one in particular pretty late in the game that I still can't figure out why it was there. I think more people will know what I'm talking about. I think the locations in HR from the factory to the Singapore facility were way more interesting.
-Performance hiccups. I haven't had any crashes, but I've seen frame dips and stutter. Nothing serious but it is there.
I'd give this a 7/10 easily. How much you enjoy it depends on where you focus. To me the gameplay carries it. While I listed more cons the multiple approaches really made everything come together. Does the series proud.
