I was really looking forward to this game but for the most part I can't recommend it. Even the most reasonable person who would always admit mistakes will eventually get p*ssed off by constant errors that weren't his/her fault. This is why I've felt so frustrated playing this game for a couple of hours. My frustration comes from a combination of these three things: the handling, the connection and the mechanics. I've enjoyed playing Toybox Turbos with a friend (and occasionally others who joined) for the past several months which is essentially the predecessor to this. I haven't had any real difficulty playing that game. It's simply enjoyable.
I'm certain they've drastically changed the handling from Toybox Turbo's. The problem is that it handles like you're always on an ice rink. Since the beginning (as far as I remember) Micro Machines games often had physics-changing surfaces, like syrup that would slow you down. These are also present in World Series. However, the older games had generally good handling on normal surfaces. This game doesn't. Vehicles seem very heavy and it's a pain to turn them. While I found obstacles in Toybox Turbos generally easy to avoid, in this at times it was almost impossible because of how awkward the handling is. What were they thinking?
Actually, I have an inkling that there may have been an ulterior motive behind the sloppy handling. It's only a theory though. There are some connection issues in Toybox Turbos, but most of the time this isn't a problem since the friend I play with is also in Europe. Sometimes people from other regions join and everything can go out of control. It seems Codemasters hasn't fixed those connection problems. Latency is important in a game like this and if Toybox Turbos has more precise handling as I believe, connection problems like "teleporting" will be much more noticeable. I think the awful handling helps mask the poor network optimisation but you will still notice a lot of "rubber banding" and sometimes it will cheat you out of a victory.
So already I've explained how frustrating shoddy controls and bad connectivity (my own connection is great) can really ruin the experience, but more than anything I think they've gone a little too far with the player count. I enjoyed Toybox Turbos because it was simple and it did what it set out to do. Having four players provided engaging and competitive multiplayer. For my favourite Micro Machines game mode, Elimination (all cars on the same screen, and the last ones on the screen get points), I believe Codemasters increased this to either six or maybe up to eight. The camera is always quite zoomed in and it's chaotic with more than four players. Maybe that's not the case for everyone and you might enjoy this higher player count, but for those who don't you're stuck with it. In the "quick game" mode there are no options at all. You're placed on a random track with five other players (some usually CPU) and I'm guessing your only way to customise this is to create private games. You're also stuck with weapons, whereas in Toybox Turbos it's easy to disable them if you wish.
There are two other game modes which are Battle and Racing. The former (not sure if there are other variants) is simply CTF with vehicles. Due to the sloppy handling I found it a chore to play. Racing is as it sounds. This mode has far more cars which of course is suitable for a race. I still ended up feeling a little frustrated due to the handling and rubber banding mentioned above. This usually resulted in either being left behind because my vehicle spazzed out, or the vice-versa and feeling somewhat guilty from getting such a cheap victory. Keep in mind the connection problems aren't always present but it has happened a lot and handling is always a problem.
So now, onto the rest of the game. I might revise my review in the near future since there's a part of the game I haven't had a chance to play yet. You have to reach level ten (you gain XP after every match) to unlock ranked mode which seems a bit much to me as it will probably take several hours. Also, for every level up you get a "loot box" (I thought these were things you bought online) with various items inside. These seem to range from extra cosmetics for your cars, user titles to display underneath your Steam name in matches and voice packs which I haven't tried. This is a personal preference, but I would highly advise turning off the character voices. Thank god there's an option to mute them as I'd have been driven insane. Oh, something else that annoys the heck out of me is how you have to exit at the end of every matchmaking game and then re-enter to find a new game. Why can't you just stay in the same lobby with the same players? Toybox Turbos does that. It's much quicker.
Toybox Turbos has a single player mode of sorts, even though it's very basic and short. Micro Machines World Series is entirely multiplayer, although the private option does allow you to play alone with AI but without any single player tasks to get through or a goal to work towards. It's a small negative for those who sometimes want to play single player or don't have online access all the time. One thing that's immediately noticeable to those who played Toybox Turbos is how flashy the new graphics are. Indeed, it looks great with ultra graphics, but I feel that if Codemasters focused more on improving the handling, connectivity and other things rather than snazzy graphics and "loot boxes" we'd have a far better game.
In conclusion, this is Micro Machines on a fundamental level. It's very flawed, but it's still Micro Machines.  If you want that and you want to play with others frequently this would probably be a better choice than Toybox Turbos which is comparatively quite old. However, if you just want to play with a few friends every now and then, not only can you find Toybox Turbos far cheaper (a few dollars at some places), but it handles a lot better and I find the lobby format more enjoyable. If you already have Toybox Turbos, draw your own conclusions and watch some videos. If you don't then definitely get it before this. If you're perfectly happy with Toybox Turbos then stick with it, or you might end up with some buyer's remorse like me.

The Sims 3 is a great game. Many people will say that The Sims 2 or The Sims 4 is better. The Sims 3 is the best Sims game because it has open world. I can't imagine a Sims game without open world. Open world allows you to travel to anywhere in the town. After the initial two-three loading screens, the only loading screens you'll encounter are when you use a mirror to change appearance, a dresser to plan outfit, or if you move, and even then these loading screens are quite short. You can customize your Sims fully, with all of the basics and many more clothing, accessories, hairstyles, and outfits available. Whatever you don't have, you can most likely get from The Sims Store, which you need an account for. You use your money to gain SimPoints, the currency used. While The Sims Store is overpriced and it will cost hundreds of dollars to buy all of the items, if you want to make an emo Sim, you will be able to buy all of the emo clothes, haircuts, and furniture without spending too much money.
Enough about The Sims Store. The Sims 3 is great because of the endless possibilities. You can have an amazing variety of Sims, all with different personalities (which are fully customizable,) careers, houses, families, and Lifetime Wishes. The game runs very smoothly on my computer. There are also Skills and Opportunities, somewhat similar to real life. Opportunities will randomly be presented to you, with a brief description of the Opportunity, usually with some humour added in too. Opportunities often require you to do something in exchange for a reward. You may have to visit certain areas, fix broken objects, make food for certain establishments or Sims, or stay in late after work ends. Rewards vary, and may include better relationships with co-workers, bosses, or other Sims, job or school performance, Simoleons (in-game money,) or Skill gain. Opportunities often have a deadline. Skills are like skills in real life. Skills include Writing (typing), Painting, Gardening, Cooking, Handiness, Charisma, and many more. You can build Skills by practicing, which is different for each Skill, or by doing tasks that improve that Skill, as each Skill is useful for a specific task. You can also build Skills by reading books, watching TV channels, learning from other Sims or by having certain Traits.
Overall, The Sims 3 is a good game that has unlimited replayability. It has its cons, however. The same old Sims get boring quickly, as Sunset Valley, the town that comes with the game, always has the same Sims when it is first started. However, the starting Sim's babies and descendants can vary. By creating an account, you get another town for free. A few other cons are that in a household of 8 (the maximum amount) Sims, it is really hard to have fun. You are constantly taking care of their Needs, which are Hunger, Bladder, Hygiene, Fun, Social, and Energy, and the rest of the time you are building Skills or Relationships, or improving job performance. Also, the stuff packs and expansion packs don't add very much, and are overpriced. The Sims Store is also overpriced.

It's a Tale about 2 brothers.
Ok, So What if i told you, it has :
+Great dual platforming.... simultaneously
+Simple yet fun Gameplay mechanics
+Beautiful Scenery+++++ Most Screenshots i've taken for a game till now.
+Epic Sense of Adventure++++++
+the Right music at the right time
+A Modest Story thats just enough to get you emotionally involved.

Well, Thats enough to make you appreciate the Game and the fact that you paid for something well worth your time. Too much puzzle solving woulda drowned the emotional ties to the game.
8/10 for me. Most of you may have played it by now, but if you have'nt, Go play it.
P.S: Best Played with a controller.

The controls are just thumbsticks and triggers (one for each brother). The triggers serve as a "Action" button which is highly contextualized depending on what situation the characters are in. It made me more focused on what's happening in the game although sometimes it caused issues controlling both brothers simultaneously, separating which is which. With this limited control scheme the game presented you with varying puzzles that didn't felt hindered or flat because of the controls, quite the opposite.
The main story may be one that's been told before, two sons on a journey to save their father. What made this game stand out to me while playing was the way the story was presented. No real language in dialogs and no lines of text. For me who personally dread long dialogs and walls of texts (think mass effect, dragon age, the witcher and the like), this was a refreshing experience. Everything i needed to know was delivered through body language and emphasis in cutscenes and through the brothers' interactions with each other and the world.
Visually the game looks stunning and made me hunt the screenshot button more than once. Now a screenshot serves as my background image.
I have nothing to complain about the ingame sounds and the soundtrack is highly memorable.
There are some replayability if you didn't explore the world fully in your first playthrough or if you want to hunt beautiful screenshots.
I give this game 8/10.

The interface is simple, but challenging as you control both characters at the same time.  The puzzles are not incredibly difficult and the interactions with the environment are limited.  But don't let that deter you from playing this game.  This adventure game is ideally for the casual gamer, or at least as a break from more demanding games.  But the story is mesmerizing and the scenery is absolutely beautiful...among one of the most beautiful games I've played in a long while.  The world is also quite impressive with each scene and chapter fitting right into the next.  You can literally stand on the side of a cliff and see the areas and puzzles you just passed through, or even see what lies ahead.
My only real complaint is that it's a bit short.  It took me only about 4 hours to complete.  I would have loved a little more.  Playing through some of the chapters a second time is possibly worthwhile to grab some extra achievements.  But don't expect to replay more than once.

If you've played Super Smash Brothers Brawl before this is very much like that in terms of the basic mechanics, with a bit less depth. In fact, among fighting games this isn't very deep. I'll explain this more a bit later.
I like how quick it is to get into a game, and the netcode seems reasonaly good, which is always a big deal when it comes to online matchmaking, especially with fighting games like this. It gets some hiccups sometimes, but I guess that's to be expected. Once in a while players get disconnected randomly after they seem to be having trouble with their controls, and you think you're still playing with people but it turns out it's just bots. (Updated 2016/02/11; this is an improvement from before where the server would just spit you out after everybody looks like they've lost control.)
I also like how the bot AI is very much integrated into the game in various ways. Not only can you use it to play single player (if you need to for whatever reason; practice or some kind of challenge mode where it's you vs. 7 bots or something), but the waiting screen for matchmaking is a free-for-all match against bots. It certainly beats waiting in a lobby doing nothing. The AI also takes over whenever a player gets disconnected, so, although they are noticeably less difficult than players in general, it's very seamless and you can continue the online match just fine, rather than being stuck with non-moving characters or people completely leaving, possibly making the match less fun.
The community is alright for the most part. Chat is actually poorly-implemented (I don't think it's possible during matches?), which is actually both a blessing and a curse in this game. It's a blessing because you don't get to see much trash-talking, and most people just leave after a match without saying anything (except a hotkeyed "gg" on the winners screen). But it's a curse because sometimes you really wanna compliment a character that you just know is playing really well, or some other thing you might wanna chat about, but you typically can't.
Music is short and can get repetitive, but is generally non-intrusive. You can also just mute the music and play iTunes or something in the background. Attack sound effects seem like placeholders for the most part, because there isn't a lot of variety and some of them are a bit strange. Why do axes sound like they're magical or something even if they aren't necessarily?
I think my biggest problem with this game is ultimately the lack of depth, like I mentioned earlier. Let me explain.
Brawhalla is intentionally simple. While within the game itself there's a fair variety when it comes to characters and how they use weapons, the weapon usage system is actually what makes this game lack the depth. Each character is limited to two weapon types, and the types of attacks of these weapons per character is fairly limited (3 strong + 3 weak on the ground, then 2 each in the air), and the most effective attacks are what get spammed the most. This also means that the best characters are the ones whose two weapons fit your play style properly.
In SSBB you had different characters with different moves altogether. You needed to learn the moves of your opponents even if you never used them yourself, just to know what they're capable of and how to defend against them. Actually that's how most fighting games work really. While that exists to some extent here in Brawlhalla, it isn't really much. It's simple; shallow even. I don't mean that in a completely negative way, because it allows novices to the fighting/brawl genre to be able to feel like they can get into the competition quickly. That even if they aren't as good as the top players when it comes to combos, cancels, etc., they can still get that lucky smash in on a whole group and triple K.O. once in a while, which feels great and gives them motivation to keep playing and learn to get better.
But it also means that the more you play, the more you feel like you've seen everything you need to see. It then becomes more a matter of whoever twitches at the wrong time rather than understanding the depths of your character's play style.
Of course this isn't such a big factor if you're only fighting one-on-one (ranked or custom games), and I've seen a lot of really skillful players who have mastered their characters, and it's amazing when you get your butt kicked by somebody who is clearly superior. But since the main mode in this game is the online 4-player free-for-all, you can be sure to see people spamming similar moves over and over just because it gets them easy points. And that can be frustrating. Not because of the losing part, as for the most part the best players win more often than not. I guess the best way to put it simply would be to say that it feels like at least in that aspect, it can get repetitive. And therefore I don't want to play this for more than a few matches a day, if even that.
However, I still think the game is fun for the most part. It gets tiring after a few matches but I think that lends to its casual nature. You log on, beat some people up, and leave feeling satisfied. That plus the fact that it's free-to-play with no possible pay-to-win mechanic (everything is cosmetic), it's a pretty good game.

Before the courts he stood, presenting evidence of that Guild Master's attempt at 2 murders and thuggery involving my family and one other dynasty. A large sum of coin earned from sheep and cow greased the palms of all three jury members, but there was a thirst for vengeance on my husband's tongue. My lady could not even leave her house without being attacked by thugs, and was basically on house arrest to keep her alive. This injustice would not stand.
As the months passed in wait for the trial, we discovered the sins of the Guild Master and her dynasty went far deeper. We were not the only dynasty suffering under her tyrannical thumb. Surely such a horrid woman, in the end, would deserve nothing less then death!
At last, the fated trial came, and the wicked woman, who thought she could feign innocence and abuse her position as Guild Master, faced the verdict. Guilty! And despite more liberal punishment laws, nothing less then death!
As she was marched to the execution block, my husband followed to proudly watch it be done. My lady, 6 months stuck inside her house and reaching age 50, was finally able to step outside and stand by her husband to watch her tormenter face justice.
We just wanted a nice farm and to raise our two daughters and son with a proper education. It didn't have to come to this. But in the end...it felt GOOD.
10/10, would execute the Guild Master again. =)

I am a big fan of RWBY. I have a strong like for Hack N' Slash games. One would think with the hours I placed into the game, having Hunter Rank 6, ect, I would be having a blast with this game. "Match made in Heaven," one could say.
Unfortunatly, it's not. It's really not.
Before reading/commenting on this review however, this is something worth noting; I have no Hands-On experience with the new Character DLC(s) outside a few matches with them that I didn't pay much attention to, so if there is any misinformation, please inform me, but in a polite manner, so I may correct things.
The game starts off with doing a couple of missions in Chapter 1 & 2, before discovering that a Once-Thought dead corporation was seemingly active again, but in a more sinister way. Chapter 3 is devoted to investigating the wherabouts, and Chapter 4 was trying to get out of a disasterous collapse, that was seemingly a trap after finding an armed bomb in the tunnel systems. Chapter 5 & 6 you encounter a boat marked with the Industry Logo, which you promptly try to investigate, but eventually you accidently get yourself Seemingly-unintentionally caught. Chapter 6 you find out who was behind it, which was the leader of the corporation, and apperently used to be good friends with Ozpin. The other chapters is devoted to trying to stop the evil man from going through with his schemes.
Don't play this for story. As far as the main story for this game goes, it's pretty forgettable in terms of how important it is. The issue with side stories like these is that, if done wrong, it can do very little with developing the characters or the whole story of the series, making it very wasted potential and/or a waste of time for playing/watching through.
And that's exactly what happened with Grimm Eclipse.
The story gave virtually no character development. The main Villain was cliche, and left little impact in what happened in the story as a whole. None of Team RWBY (or whatever other character/team is being added via DLC, because ♥♥♥♥ Grimm Eclipse's Story Coherency am I right Rooster Teeth?) had any development from this whole endevour that would be seemingly an epic achievement accomplishing. Ozpin is probably the ONLY character that had any development from this side-story, and even then the only new information given about him can be summed up as "having an old friend going their seperate ways for having different opinions, whom was also leading a big corporation that was shut down many years ago." Even THEN, that info would be seen as more of a "Fun Fact" than anything else, for how little it even matters. The ONLY Saving Grace (or as saving as it could be) Grimm Eclipse's story would ever have, would be the return of GE's villain in the Main Story of RWBY later on, with leaving an actual impact in the main story then what he did in GE. With no reference to these events within the preceding/current volumes we have as of this review, however, this game's story can be summarized as practically worthless trivia knowledge in RWBY.
So story is a bust, TL;DR. What other reason is there to play this?
...
...
...
...
...
...No, seriously, what else is there? Oh, you mean GAMEPLAY? Ha. Ha ha. Ha ha ha....
That's a Joke right?
Right?
Satire aside, Gameplay is not TERRIBLE.
It's TOLERABLE.
What I mean by that is that it does what the basic gameplay would ask of, which is Hack N' Slash: There's lotta Hacking, and lotta Slashing, so it does what it was going for.
How WELL it's pulled off, however, is a completely different story.
The attacks are very bare-bones, with very little implamented combos you can do (A.K.A, comboes intended using only basic attack commands such as Dash attacks, Heavy attacks, light, ect). You can pull off some fancy combinations of attacks here and there, but overall it's pretty bare.
The Balancing job in GE is worse than Valve with CS:GO, which is really saying something. The Weed (weak) Mobs are so pitiful because of how some of the few attack comboes given to the characters, can instantly kill them, even in the fresh beginning of the game, with little punish on the character's end. The Ranged attacks the characters possess will generally either be almost complete trash or extremely op, depending on the characters w/ their skills, and is not particularly fun to use for an extended time either way. Counters, In theory, would make you completely invincible without even having to directly attack for almost every enemy, as, while being instantly punishment if failing the timing, there is no risk in a successful counter whatsoever. Specials for the characters are the most balanced thing about this game, however they can still be even more garbage depending on the character w/ their skill choices.
Also, it should be worth mentioning that there is a Leveling-Up system, however it's also Bare-Bones. All leveling gives you is one skill point for each level-up: No Stat Increase of any kind, and the Level cap is 10. Not only that, but you have an extremely pitiful skill tree as well, with 4 different Catagories: Special, Team Attacks, Ranged, and Utilities. While 3/4ths of those trees are usually very small, and free skill-refunding before spawning in the mission is a thing, you are extremely limited in what to use the points on as well. Some skills cost 2 points, as well as having to unlock a good amount of skills by actually having to complete their unlock condition, which is annoying to have to do for reasons stated later. Some skills are also more op than others in almost every way, such as some of Blake's Ranged Upgrades, not rewarding diversity of playstyles of what an actual skill tree is often suppose to do. This overall is a very unpolished, unbalanced system.
Story Mode is just simple "kill enemies to progress" 85% of the game so it's bare bones. Hoard Mode is essentially what you did for the 1st 2 chapters of Story, but it get's harder with more waves, more control towers go up to defend as time goes on, and you can buy turrets to help protect said control towers. Hoard Mode is the more exciting game mode imo, but only because of it's concept and difficulty unlike what Story Mode gave.
Lastly, probably the only reason I played the game as long as I did, and what kills skill progression even further:
Hunter Ranks.
They are essentially like a Prestige System, giving a higher rank in exchange for completing a set amount of challanges or getting to max level, only to reset it back to 0 just for the extra point. It's only for Bragging Rights, but it's probably the only thing you can work for outside Steam Achievements. When you increase your hunter rank, however, Levels are reset, as well as Any Skill you unlocked. That means that one skill that took a good hour or so to unlock would be locked again, which was what killed the Skill System even further in terms of progression and play-style diversities, as it makes it extremely difficult to have a unique play-style you like forever (Unless you run with the most op builds not requiring any unlocks, which, I won't totally blame you for)
Gameplay is Mediocre at best compared to other games of the same genre, TL;DR

Blood Dragon is a more modern take on the games and movies of the 80's (and early 90's I guess). It's got lots of neon, dragons, a cheesy story, old school music and a lot, A LOT, of explosions. All combined into a neat little Far Cry package. Meaning it's an open world environment, and it has sidemissions and upgrades, too.
If you're from the 80's theres's a high probability you'll instantly fall in love with this game. I did. It looks great in motion, the voice acting is great (although the story is purposely ridiculous) and it has tons of action in it, thanks to some awesome weapons in it. The world feels a bit empty, however. Where Far Cry 3 was filled with wildlife, I rarely saw wild animals in Blood Dragon. But it's possible that was because of the lighing and the fact that I didn't really explore like I normally do. Nothing big, it just caught my attention.
Blood Dragon is, unfortunately, also a bit on the short side. Completing the game, doing only the main missions, took me about 3,5-4 hours to do. Enough for a downloadable game and more importantly, to keep things interesting. If you add the hunting missions and other sidemissions you can probably double that number. Upgrading your character also happens automatically (there are no skill trees) so replaying the game isn't all that interesting because you'll gain the same skills and perks every time, no matter what.
Not that it mattered, because I had a blast playing Blood Dragon, and that's all that counts. Recommended !

I love this game. Brawlhalla is like a more balanced and smoother version of Smash Bros. Each weapon is set up with a particular move set, and each character comes with two particular weapons. This combination of weapons along with the stats of the character will determine what fighter you have. Each unique character will also generally have their unique variants of these weapon types, along with signature moves to go with them. I played a particular bull character that could hook people with a hammer in a grab, then swing them off of the screen in the opposite direction. There's also a cowgirl that can lasso foes, then finish them with a hammer blow.
The paid content is reasonable, and the weekly rotation of characters never leaves you wanting. It's a pleasant suprise to actually enjoy learning each new character, and knowing that I'll have a whole set of new characters next week....at least for a few weeks. Regardless, the fluidity of combat, and the level design is extremely sound. No stun locks, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t ultra moves, and know no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t ring outs.
If you do wish to get new characters and be able to hold on to them week to week, you can essentially either play cash or put in the time to earn gold from fights and leveling. After a few hours, maybe 4, I've earned roughly 1500 coins. It takes roughly 2300 for the cheapest characters, and upwords of 5000 for some of the pricier ones. If you enjoy the game, it won't take long to unlock characters. This is a no brainer for those that want to find games they can play with friends online.
A few things it could use? Something to differentiate the characters a bit more. It became difficult at times to keep track of which one you were; you share the same shape, stance, color, and weapon of another that's not you. The game also has a tendency to throw the camera around pretty quickly in order to keep track of everything. Combine this with the aforementioned samey-ness of the characters, and it just gets more difficult to tell what's actually going on.
Otherwise, the only other gripe I would have is that there is no instant replay feature.

I played this game when it was originally released back in 2001. I got Red Faction (RF) in a bundle years ago, but haven't played it since way back then. Now that it's 2017 I decided to play through it again and see if it held up to the nostalgia I once had. Unfortunately it did not.
Please note: Screenshots in above game description do not represent actual in-game screens. These have been massively doctored. Also game was played with PureFaction a mod that allows you to play in widescreen. That's why my playtime is so low. Actual playtime is probably closer to 8 or 9 hours and that completed the sp campaign.
On to the review:
Red Faction is a game that came out in the wake of Half-Life. It breaths Half-Life. In fact, it almost feels like a mod more than an original game. Many of the weapons are taken from HL. Troops and scientist look eerily similar. There is a tram portion. There are ducts to move around in. There are big round tunnels with fans on the end. Halfway through the game they mention the soldiers are killing all the scientists.
All these things were not a thing until HL which came out only 2 or 3 years prior to RF. This was something I did not even notice playing back in '01, but now it's almost too obvious. Not to say a HL clone makes a game bad. It's just shows it's age and lack of creativity.
RF biggest selling point was that everything in the game was to be destructible. Unfortunately it's not. Only some dirt is destructible, but not all dirt. I remembered how awesome it was to destroy a wall and dig a tunnel. Somehow that memory is skewed. You are not given a pickaxe or anything to dig with. You have explosives in minimal quantity. Destructible pieces are not highlighted. Sometimes you can break through stuff, but really the mechanic was not used more than once or twice in the game. You can blow up certain walls to find extra armor or ammo, but those times are limited and usually there's 2 ways into said, "secret," areas so you didn't even need to blast anything anyway.
However, the above issues are just minor. Who really cares if it's a HL clone or its biggest selling point was a farce as long as the game is fun right? Unfortunately... it's not... and I hate to say that because I remember really having fun with this game 16 years ago. But by today's standards, the game does not hold up very well. It's not one that stood the test of time to be sure.
Weapon reloads are soooo sloooowwwww! It can take irl 5 to 15 seconds to reload and don't expect to switch once the animation starts. Oh no! You just have to break from combat and take bullets or find cover. Melee is op for mobs and broken for you. There's a baton in the game. When you select it there is a 10 second readying weapon animation that you have to endure before you can use it. Why would you ever ready melee that needs 10 sec before you can use it?!? However, the mobs run right at you and hit constantly until you kill them. They run faster than you; so you can't try to outrun. Imagine going through a 15 sec reload animation, while attempting to kite, but getting non-stop meleed the entire time.
Guns on the other hand are an entirely different level of frustration. There is no mouse smoothing; so I personally had jittery aim. It's not a problem in other games, but it could be something to do with my mouse: Logitech G502. I'll give them that. But the mobs dart back and forth so quickly you can't ever get a good shot. I wasted more ammo on walls than enemies. Also, enemies are bullet sponges, taking multiple shots before dying. It's massively frustrating to constantly miss shots because of enemies darting around and a jittery mouse. On the other hand, this could have something to do with PureFaction, the mod I used to play this game in 1080p. I don't remember it being so difficult to shot people, then again 2001 was a different time for games.
The cut scenes in this game should be turned into memes. It's beyond campy. It turns hilarious because it's so bad. It's like watching Trolls 2 for the first time all over again. This game is worth a play through just to watch the cut scenes I swear!
But overall this game just fails in everything. It fails in destructible environments (YOU HAD ONE JOB) it fails at a decent story, and it fails at smooth 'n fun FPS action. I definitely do not recommend.

As far as looks go, Red Faction is more like the cute girl next door than a hot fashion model from the Upper West Side: It’s pretty, but it won’t make a man drop to his knees and thank God for giving him sight.

-Asgard’s mini golfing and pole vaulting champion extraordinaire,
-A spooky scary skeleton,
-A demonic mosh pit ninja,
-The guy who formed the United Kingdom by subjugating Scotland and Ireland with nothing but his beard,
-The girl who made Britannia rule the waves and the sky with lots of steam,
-A cyclops alien Crip from Planet Ferguson (contrary to developer propaganda, Roldakk-9 was actually the city of Ferguson, Missouri),
-A wolf-riding elven Greenpeace activist,
-The gun-toting, law-enforcing cowgirl who inspired Chuck Norris to become a Texas Ranger,
-G.N.A.S.H. Genocidal Neolithic Abominable Smashing Homosapien,
-A heroine from a hi-tech cyberpunk future who is surprisingly adept with a primitive spear,
-A homeless guy from down the alleyway who acquired a sword and a pirate hat,
-A savage anthropomorphic tiger who drove the British out of India. Gandhi promptly took all the credit.
-A teleporting samurai who materializes wooden planks out of thin air,
And the lastest addition,
The vampire-hunting daughter of Scarlet and Lucien who whips people with bungee cords.
In your quest to savagely beat up your friends as well as strangers, you will have a variety of signature moves and weapons at your disposal. These include:
-The Helicopter,
-The Upside-Down Helicopter,
-The Black Lives Matter Hammer,
-A little Birdy,
-Mini golfing with a Battle Axe,
-Storm Surge from Hurricane Katrina,
-A Tractor Beam,
-Roundhouse Kicks,
-Old-Fashioned Uppercuts,
-Jousting,
-The Dust Bowl,
-Hiawatha Snake Magics,
-Slow-Motion Gunplay,
-Pretending to play a xylophone in midair on someone’s face with a pair of pistols,
-The Broadside Cannon Barrage,
-The Incredibly Versatile Human Torpedo,
-The Baguette Butcher,

-Spikey Balls,

Overall, after sustained play, your friends will go down in flames and your keyboard will go up in smoke. Therefore, Brawlhalla provides a satisfying experience.

Overall Trick and Treat is a well put together game. As visual novels go, the game delivers with good characterization, the story is interesting and plays off of its CYOA structure with good writing telling a singular story in such a way as to avoid repetiveness and to add context to the overarching narrative. The final ending, helps bring another aspect to what I thought was a already satisfying story and definetly brought a good amount of closure to the tale.
Now for some criticism.
- The beginning of the story before the first decision is a bit dry. Narratively your friends don't really add much to the story other then being the inciting incident. and overall they only seen at the beginning and end of the storyline and for only a small portion. Also fleshing out the legend more could help explain the motivation of the character. Also I don't believe it ever was explain where the smell of rot was coming from. But all-in-all the strength of the story comes from the events of that "Unforgettable Night" with Lillian and Ashley so this can be put aside.
- It would be extremly helpful to be able to save at the decision points instead of before or after them.
- Overall, a few more art assets would have been nice for the game but the assets and art in general where sufficient and well done.
Trick and Treat is a good visual novel and I would definitely recommend this game to you. For a Free To Play game it has a good amount of polish and was a enjoyable afternoon for something I had to pay nothing for.  Thank You.

After 100 percenting this game I feel like I lost a bit of my soul that I won't ever get back. I don't want anyone to feel the same way.
This game, while short (and I guess some would say sweet), managed to rock my very being with perhaps the most manufactured, underdeveloped, and cutesy girls (there's only 2, 3 if you don't count the TRUE ending where they fuse) and awkward kissing scenarios, that give the respective girls immense power, ever seen in my time spent among visual novels. It felt like I was reading a fanfiction of someone's OC in a fanfiction of a fanfiction and I can't say I was satisfied with this gripping feeling.
Along with those emotions, the game lacks a lot of content. You can beat your first path in 5 to 10 minutes depending on whether you die or kiss one of the girls (you have to kiss one or you die in later events a good majority of the time) and 78% of your time is spent staring at the same, bland, unmoving screen while absorbing dialog from a 2nd grader's free write journal with some doodles thrown in.
Either way, recommended or not, Ashley is the best girl here. She doesn't try sucking out blood, she just licks wounds to heal them. Because she's a cat girl. I regret everything.

GRAPHICS

6.5/10

The Sims 3 is a life simulator and well it does a great job of being so. The game mainly consists of doing well whatever you like! I really wanted to like this game. I came in with high hopes and prayed to the holy trinity, seven layers of hell, the Norse gods, the Roman gods, the Greek gods, and even ♥♥♥♥ing Yahweh. Turns out that one of them decided I was a ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and deserved to be sad. I bet it was Thor.
Tangent aside. This is literally Devil May Cry 4, but with Vergil and two mediocre characters. If you're a Vergilfriend, then by all means buy this game. You should get $25 worth of enjoyment.
That reminds me. Apparently, if you already bought the vanilla version, you still pay the full price for this barely-touched rerelease. Capcom, are you even trying? This is depressing on your collective part.
The gameplay itself is unchanged for the original two heroes, Nero and Dante. They didn't even bother to give them anything besides a new costume. I am not exaggerating. However, they have one leg up over the new three: a story. That's right, Vergil and Lady/Trish, the latter two being their own campaign like Nero/Dante, have no justification for why they're there besides the opening and ending. Vergil's story takes place long ago, and just serves to imply he's Nero's dad with his ending of, SPOILER ALERT, his shadow resembling Nero's Devil Trigger. Wow, it's nothing. Meanwhile, for Lady/Trish, they just tagged along with Dante. Well, okay, that is kind of implied in the main story so that's okay. However, the main gripe I have is they don't get cutscenes like Nero/Dante. For new enemies and bosses, it just shows them and the foes before putting you back in the game. It's lazy and insulting.
The new characters are underwhelming, frankly. Vergil is pretty goddamn strong and it shows that Capcom just threw him in with all these toys without thinking about balance, if you're a whiner about that. I'm thankful for this, but he still needs way too much effort for S ranking it up. And if you're not getting S ranks, there's no point at all to playing this game. Why do okay when you should be doing perfect? Checkmate atheists. No offense to atheists.
Lady and Trish, on the other hand, are insulting. Lady is basically Dante's Gunslinger style and has some rockin' guns. And I don't just mean her handguns, shotgun, and Kalina Ann. Fun to watch, not fun to play. Trish, however, is just a weakened Dante with no switching. She's basically the dump character for Capcom.
Besides the much less optimized engine, nothing else changed. There is nothing on the PC version that is worth mentioning. Sure, there's Turbo mode, but that's it. It'll just make you get hit more, and why would you want to break your combos? Those things are already few and far between. Plus, the new battle themes aren't even properly implemented. Yes, Vergil, Lady, and Trish have themes but you're just going to hear Nero and Dante's themes because why would Capcom make a good decision?
Oh yeah, optimization. DMC4 could play on an N-Gage. DMC4SE, not so much. While my computer's fairly strong, I've heard some horror stories about the framerates.
In short, this game is not worth a buy, especially if you already bought DMC4. Just play DMC3SE.

Devil May Cry 4 is a good game. This much is already known. But is the Special Edition worth getting? If you haven't played the original version of the game, then the answer is a resounding "Yes:" this is the version you should get. But what if you have played the original? Then, the answer is still yes. The three new characters are all fun to play, and they all feel unique. Vergil plays a little bit like Dante, with swappable weapons, but instead of Styles, he has a new Concentration mechanic. The greater your concentration, the more damage your attacks deal, and there are even a few super-powerful attacks that can only be performed when your concentration is at its maximum. Concentration is increased by hitting enemies and taunting, and its depleted when you take damage, miss with an attack, or run. This encourages a vastly different playstyle where you actually play similarly to how Vergil fought as a boss in DMC3, and once you get it down, it feels amazing. Lady is a ranged-oriented character, with many types of guns, and a massive explosion attack instead of a Devil Trigger. She has very little in the way of melee attacks, but she has so many different moves with her various guns that she remains somewhat versatile regardless. The only complaint with her is that since so many enemies are designed to be challenging in melee, she makes many portions of the game far too easy. Trish is probably the most similar to Nero and Dante in her playstyle, but even she feels distinct, with her own suite of moves. She's also fantastic at grinding red orbs, as she has a combo attack that can obtain a ludicrous number from the giant red crystals. Besides that, the game has added new alternate costumes for the characters (some of which you will need to unlock), and increased the drop rates of Red Orbs and Proud Souls, to cut down on the grind. The only complaint I have is that the DLC here is horrendous, with things that should be unlocks costing extra money. However, overall, Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition is a fantastic package, and well worth your time.

The world of Brothers is incredible. Like Middle Earth or Westeros the world is epic in scale and also in scope. The set pieces range from a snowy river, a grassy land, a mountainous Giant keep and many others without giving spoilers. These set pieces made me pause and admire their beauty and even had me take screenshots. Music

Final Verdict

The settings are more colorful and so are the characters. You play either as mage, berserk, ranger or - and that's something you don't see often - engineer. Which is giving the whole story some nice steam-punk elements.
The engineer uses handheld cannons, heavy weapons and builds robots, which means that he is pretty much the modern take on your good-old necromancer (minus the romance and plus the sledgehammer).
The story itself is pretty simple. The "alchemist" (the hero you played in Torchlight 1) turns mad, BBQs his former allies and seeks world domination the unfriendly way. Meaning: he doesn't really believe in free-speech or elections.
You are sent after him to make him reconsider.
Which makes Torchlight 2 basically a Diablo 2 with better graphics minus Lucifer and plus Steam-Punk. Also with pets, multiplayer support and Steam workshop.

It's time for my next review!
Today I will be reviewing Red Faction.
Red Faction is a game made by the makers of the Saints Row Series. In Red Faction, you play as a man named Parker and you work for a company called Ultron. Your job is to mine, and you work on the planet of mars. The story goes like this, the miners who work for Ultron are not being treated well, they're pretty much being treated like slaves, and they're fed up with working for the company. Not only does Ultor mistreat its workers, Ultor also created a plague that infected most of the miners with the help of a man called Capek'll. One day while you were in the mines, a small group called Red Faction revolts against Ultor, resulting in a revolutionary war on mars. Your job is to help the rebellion, find the antidote for the plague, defeat Ultor, and escape mars.
Throughout the game, you are helped by a man named Hendrix, and a women named Eos, you don't see the two until later. You are also helped by soldiers within the rebellion, which leads me to my first problem with the game. My first problem is that the soldiers you come across throughout the game are useless, meaning they die in one hit. In one part of the game, you get to free a miner from a jail cell. Once I freed the miner, he escaped through the front door and was killed within two seconds. So yea, throughout the game, it's just you fighting Ultor. It's like if the only patriot fighting in the American Revolution was George Washington, and he had to take down the biggest army on the planet by himself.
Another problem I ran into while I was playing was when you first drive a submarine, you have to click a button, and the submarine would fall right into the water. But, when I clicked the button, the submarine just blew up. Now I looked it up to see if this was just a joke, but no, it was an actual glitch that a lot of players run into. apparently, you have to click F1 and lower the resolution, so keep this in mind when you are playing this game, you have a big chance in running into this glitch because it has happened to most modern-day computers. Sadly, none of my F buttons work, so I had to do it the hard way, I had to swim in the water, and try to dodge as much rockets as I could. It was hard, and it took me 4 tries, I almost decided to stop playing and review with the little information that I had, but I found a way.
My third and finale problem I had with the game was the limited amount of cool and unique enemies at the beginning. Luckily, the game makes up for this by adding in robots and monsters later on, but only for a short time. I wish the game explored a bit more with the monsters, kind of like what HL2 did with its zombies.
Okay, I think we have gone on long enough, it's time for me to rate the game! I rate this game a 7/10, sure it was fun at the beginning, but the game has so much problems, that it's tough for me to give it anything higher. last but not least, I'm giving this game the "Rebellious Award". This game reminded me a lot of the half life series, not only because in plays like half life 1, but because the story is very similar to half life 2. You are one man trying to defeat an unfair corporation with a small group of rebels. Anyway I have nothing else to say, and I hope you all have a great day.

This is one of the games where I'm not so sure where to start with. Feelings are extremely mixed because many parts of the game are fine and dandy, but other parts can and will most likely put the player off (especially in the last half of the game). One thing I can say is that this is also one of the games favored by many in the past because of nostalgia, thus, the game may receive praise that can mislead newer players who haven't played it into believing it's an outstanding title. Although this is obviously a subjective perception, it's important to know the flaws of the game where fans may or may not be blind to. Preferably from someone (such as myself) who dove into it blindly with no reminiscent memories of said game.
Firstly, "Red Faction" is by no means a terrible game even though I cannot recommend it for a handful of different reasons. The game is smooth and the controls are fine (with the exception of ladders), the overall length of the game is incredibly long (but I will cover this later on), there are different styles of combat such as vehicular combat and stealth (but will also cover stealth later on) and limited destructable environments which was quite new and innovative for the time of this game's creation.
Unfortunately, the flaws I find lie solely on the gameplay and design. Yes I did mention that the environment is somewhat destructable, but this happens mainly for story purposes such as breaching a wall or finding an alternate route to progress. Combat is also either on or off. There are not a lot of variety when it comes to enemies. For the most part, you're up against guards and other times, machines. Only in the second half of the game would you finally encounter a new set of monsters to fight. But leaving the front lines alone, Stealth is where the game gets hit hard. The AI in this game are buggy and can appear to have a mind of it's own. There are stealth sections in this game where you are required to sneak past people in order to reach someone, staying as far away as possible, but I find many times that they still spot you from across the room. Despite that, you can still go in guns blazing as stealth isn't mandatory, but in these cases you only carry a sidearm with limited ammunition so 'guns blazing' may not be the smartest or best choice.
Another thing I mentioned was length. Yes, length can be good only if the story is good. The story as the description says is a revolution on a paradise gone wrong, that's about it. It isn't bad as many games do this quite well, but it drags on and on. Similar to the original 'Half-Life' series, the initial length is extremely long but 'Half-Life' wasn't as bad because they had great gameplay to compliment it. As well as graphics, 'Red Faction' and 'Half-Life' share a lot of similarities and although 'Red Faction' is more advanced, I can't help but feel as though 'Half-Life's style did it better. Many of 'Red Faction's maps are bland and for the most part contain bland colors leaving the environment plain and boring, adding on to the difficulty of playing such a long game. 50-60% of the game takes place in brown mining channels with the same texture stretched on for miles, but I can't say anything about that, it
where the revolution started. That being said though, it does justify it's price tag. There is definitely $10USD worth of content, but in comes the "quantity over quality" factor, which there is quality, but more quantity than so.
As mentioned, it's not a terrible game if you have the acquired taste (which can be said for any game) but from my experience, the cons outweight the pros therefore I would not recommend it. Don't take my review as an indirect suggestion to
take positive reviews into consideration. By all means do that, but keep in mind that some if not many of them base a huge amount around nostalgia.

I deeply love this game. I have spent an amount of time which should be embarrassing playing this glorious sandbox experience.
It is a difficult game to explain in a way which does justice to the mechanics and design.
It is not a beautiful game, when compared to the polish of “next-gen” releases, and the bare-bones game is not the most robust in the features department, however this game provides an unquestionably powerful foundation which modders have used to construct some amazing and unique gaming experiences. Many wonderful mods exist which provide fresh gaming experiences, using similar mechanics. Each mod is like an entirely new game in a genre the player has come to love.
The genre is difficult to define using comparisons to other games, as there has never been a game quite like Mount and Blade.
It's a sandbox for people who crave a world not unlike the Song of Ice and Fire. There are even a few fun mods with that focus, though they aren't my favorites.
The player creates a character, choosing from various back-stories and talents, this character is then dropped into an often feudal world (depending on the campaign mod), where they must elevate themselves. Players may choose to become bandits, preying on the weak and the unsuspecting, or join a lord's army, and become the mightiest of soldiers. The player may earn a lord or king's favor and be granted lands, their exploits helping them rise in the ranks of nobility to ultimately rule the entire kingdom or even the entire nation.
The gameplay is first or third person, predominately using medieval melee and ranged weaponry, however firearms are also available in many mods.
Players begin by roving the world-map, their player and army represented by a man or men on horseback, not unlike a classic JRPG. The player army roves from town and city, fighting brigands or rivals, or raiding for loot. When the player meets another army in the field, the game moves to an instanced battlefield, where each unit is represented individually. The player is the general, controlling their units with certain formation commands. The player may also charge into the fight or launch arrows from horseback or ground, and this is where the game truly shines. Gloriously visceral and responsive combat.
There are multiple factions, each shifting in and out of hostilities. The factions seize towns and castles from one another, each vying for domination of the world. These fiefs provide economic benefits to the lord granted rulership of them.
The player may choose to join a faction, may help a pretender king rise to overthrow the current ruler of each faction, they may even begin their own faction, and conquer the world from their own seat of power.
Frankly, I cannot recommend this game enough to anyone who enjoys high fantasy, medieval fantasy, third and first person swordplay, diplomacy or world-building.
The learning curve is not the easiest, but it's certainly not the most difficult game out there.
Give it a shot. Chances are you won't be disappointed.

Although the game is quite short (1-2 Hours to finish the story) and limited in mechanics and narrative it is fun for what it is.
The game is a hack a slash with a small variety of enemies (around 10-12, I think)which provide the same challenge to fight (button mash). These are implemented in the cliche mob pockets around the world as well as a repetitive multiple wave horde fight.
The narrative is rather weak and sometimes you may feel like a lot of information has been skipped over however you are able to follow the main direction of the story to be playable.
The world design and character models are very bright and aethestically pleasing.
The main feature that redeems this game is the multiplayer functionality. By playing with friends allows you to role play with hypothetical teams and it is rather fun.
TLDR: Rather bland and easy game, but fun with friends.
Recomended improvments:
Add more characters, the more the merrier (especially team CFVY)
Lengthen the campaign with a more deeper richer story (Mission packs with new stories)
Newmechanics to implement into levels to diversify them and to reduce repetitive gameplay (Unique Puzzles maybe)

Devil May Cry 4 Special Edtion is another excellent entry to the series. You again explore the island of Fortuna and hack-and-slash demons along the way on your quest to stop a corrupt cult leader from destroying the world, but this time, you can play as five characters (Vergil, Lady, Trish, Nero, and Dante) instead of two (Nero and Dante).
- Smooth combat, even with a keyboard
- Responsive controls, keyboard or controller can be used
- Updated graphics that appeal to the eye
- Amazing atmosphere
- Five characters to play as
- Great story
- Another astonishing soundtrack by Tetsuya Shibata
- Costumes
- Unnecessary amount of motion blur that cannot be disabled and makes the combat sluggish for those who don't have a strong processor
- Only four new cutscenes for Vergil and Lady/Trish. Nothing changed whatsoever to the story besides the final level for those three characters.
- DmC: Devil May Cry's Dante color scheme as a costume for Dante. Would of been better if his EX costume was a Nero color scheme to fit the color-swapping theme featured within all EX skins.
- Game does not feature multiple save files like the original DMC4. Not a huge issue, but I'd kinda like to start a new file while still keeping my fully-upgraded, main file.
All in all, this game is a great buy for those into or starting out with the DMC series. The story might be confusing for new players, as it takes place after the first and third games, but it's still a good game to own.

This was the first in the Red Faction series released back in 2001; the first that began the story of a rebellion against the so-called Ultor Corporation that abuses miners on planet Mars. Later entries (the 3rd and the 4th) became third-person shooters so the gameplay changed throughout the years.
At the time this game was revolutionary. Games with realistic physics were not yet released (we had to wait a couple of more years till Half Life 2, Doom 3 and Far cry came out), however, Red Faction's so-called Geo-Mod technology offered the closest experience as it had destructible environments. In practice, this meant solving our problem of a closed door by simply creating a tunnel next to it with the use of a rocket launcher.
The gameplay itself is a fast-paced shooter with the usual weapons (pistol, shotgun, rifle, rocket launcher etc.) where we basically follow a linear path and regularly receive instructions from the leaders of the rebellion. Due to an altercation between a worker and a guard we are thrust into the middle of a mutiny and our best bet is to shoot at everything that moves. For some reason the sequel continues the story on Earth - a deviation that did not make this episode famous. We had to wait till Guerrilla to pick up where the Martians were left off.
It was nice to play this game for a short while on Steam and see it was running perfectly. Widescreen resolutions, unfortunately, are missing (the highest we can pick is 1280x1024) but the discussion / guide sections offer solutions as well as workaround for making the multiplayer work. If you liked Guerrilla and Armageddon and you'd like to know which game started the franchise than feel free to pick this one up when on sale.

DXMD has a great premise - and a big promise to fulfill.
For the most part, it delivered: stellar graphics, excellent world-building and sense of atmosphere. The core gameplay features returned, and they remain largely unchaged, which is quite welcomed. Don't fix what's not broken, right?
Well, that is until you actually delve into it. All the bugs and game-breaking fails aside (you guys are probably too well aware of them by now, I assume), where the game fell short, sadly, was where it was meant to shine. Story-wise, the game feels short and unrewarding - and this is the BIGGEST letdown. I know, I just KNOW that Square Enix forced Eidos to split the game into multiple parts (DLCs, sequels...however you like to call them), considering how soon they're planning to release the first story DLC, System Rift, featuring our beloved Frank Pritchard to bait fans. I don't know about you, but I'd give up on Deus Ex if they make it into Final Fantasy. Ironic how an anti-corporate power game is controlled by a freaking corporate.
Anyways, speaking of story, they pretty much spoiled it in the trailer who the real bad guy was. There was not enough sense of urgency and threat to make your decisions have weight. The characters around Adam, while polished, are not as likeable and worth investing our emotions in. They don't feel as fresh either, there's our boss Miller (an ex-SAS who's actually the grumpier version of David Sarif), Peter Chang and Macready (take Pritchard and split him into two characters), Chikaine - a blatant pallete-swap of the friendly, likeable Malik. The villain, Marchenko, isn't as intimidating as he's supposed to be. Just another Bin Laden pretending he's something greater, speaking of greater good, preaching philosophies, justifying his "Cause" while murdering innocent people. I don't feel any sympathy for him, I did not synchronize with his issues like I did with Taggart or Darrow. I KILLED HIM in my first playthrough because I got fed up with his yammering, period.
Sound design? This one is a toughy. DXMD has FANTASTIC set of soundtrack, kudos to the spectacular Michael McCann. Highly atmospheric, the tracks fit perfectly into the sceneries and situation Adam finds himself in. The rest of the sounds...I have to take the point back. The voice acting wasn't that impressive enogh. While Adam sounds tired as he should be in the post-Incident dystopia, I think the director told Elias Toufexis to work too hard to "improve" his original work in HR, which in turn made Adam sound too forced. The rest of the cast...I'll just leave them where they are, far away from Vahalla in the zone of MEDIOCRITY.
Gameplay-wise, I absolutely LOVE the stealth gameplay. So many approaches, so many things to consider - very absorbing. Still, I find it hard to enjoy the "gun-blazing" aspect of the game: Adam dies too quickly, and the combat mechanics is clunky, unrefined (as if the developers never made references to games with better combat flow and user-friendly interface like Mass Effect, Gears of War or Dishonored...I also did not enjoy bumping into so many moveable objects. Everything just shifts and falls apart at the slightest touch, yes even the HUGH metal crates. It is a pain just stacking boxes to reach a ledge or a vent - and those freaking paper archive boxes...how in the hell do they push back a massive, not to mention AUGMENTED, guy?
While the new augs are awesome and inspiring, you have to spend more than the first half of the game working to gain your ORIGINALLY ACTIVATED augs back, which is fine if you're more into gaining XP through exploration and completing side missions.
Speaking of the side missions, I do find them interesting and surprisingly deep in terms of storytelling, mystery and suspense.
What I did not like, however, was the fact that most of your CASIE battles take place in them. Remember when you have to break down Wayne Haas to gain access to the morgue (learning a bit of Adam's past in the process), talk down Bill Taggart, Sarif and Hugh Darrow? They offered a wide variety of reaction and dialogues that took you quite a while to get a hand on - which was exactly what made Human Revolution GREAT. DXMD, on the other hand, offered little variety in dialogues - and the truly important social boss figth, with Rucker, only boils down to getting access to a keycode (which can be otherwise circumvented with Hacking skill or a simple unlocking device).
I cannot deny the disappointment I felt completing the game that feels too short and lackluster to be a Deus Ex experience, considering Eidos had FIVE years of development. HOWEVER, overall, I did have, and am still having a blast with DXMD, because I'm trying to squeeze every bit I can out of it. Would I recommend it to people? YES, I would - but only after the discount and bug fixes are in place.

This is a rather painful thing for me to say is terrible, because I, like all who play this game, absolutely ADORE RWBY. But.... This game doesn't do us justice. We showed so much love and support for this series, and they gave us something that ultimately disappointed, and it appears it's going to continue to disappoint.
Cons:
1. Paid DLC for Team JNPR. If that isn't a♥♥♥♥♥♥move, I don't know what is.
2. Just announced costume packs for $2 EACH. Okay. So, maybe THAT'S a bigger♥♥♥♥♥♥move.
3. Combat is, indeed, rather repetitve, even for a hack-n-slash, and it doesn't help that the combo system for it is about as shallow as the developer's dignity when coming up new ways to milk money out of our wallets when it comes to this.
4. The looks are okay. It's hard to really judge the overall look of the game, because I'm sure their budget wasn't anything major, but I've seen too many instances of looking through the floor and the textures of everything are just.... Meh.
5. The real lack of a single-player. I get that a good appeal of this game comes from the fact that you can play with four players and have Team RWBY fighting side-by-side, but the online community isn't faring too well, and for how expensive this game is, getting friends together is gonna be a MASSIVE cost.
6. The PRICE. My, lord, the price! They jacked it up way too much and way too soon! $20 is WAY TOO MUCH for this game! I absolutely DO NOT recommend anyone get it at this price! Get it if it's ever on a massive sale and you actually really love RWBY.
7. The real lack of variety in Grimm type. The show is chock-full of Grimm, and it was so tempting to see how they get transferred over into game form, but, all we really get is 4 throughout the game, with the second-half needing to add robots.
8. Horde Mode. It's awful and poorly balanced for teams less than 4, and it's just amazingly boring while also being the really B.S excuse as to why JNPR was paid DLC
Pros:
1. Believe it or not, I actually don't mind the story. I don't need an RPG-type story to get me invested, just give me enough to keep going. And! For those of you like me, Dr. Merlot is the same guy who voiced The General from Saints Row 2! Yes, please!
2. The variation of the levels is okay. It's nice to see the Emerald Forrest and Moutain Glenn, but it suffers a little by not really adding much to their mythos/lore.
3. Hearing the actual actors behind the characters lend their talents to the game! But.... That's not really something that we should be celebrating, but rather EXPECTING....

As if paying $20 dollars for this contentless game wasn't enough.
To start, this game is plainly made to be a cash cow for Rooster Teeth.
It is an effortless and an uninspired game with little to no innovation other than playing as your favorite characters from the RWBY show. I personally am a fan of the show, but now I question Rooster Teeth and how they would allow this unfinished game to be released with the RWBY name on it. If the RWBY name wasn't on it, this game would for sure be recieving negative reviews due to pricing and lack of content.
To put into perspective, if you buy this game full price at $20 dollars, you get:
~ 10 Story Missions
~ 3 Hoard Mode Levels
~ 4 Characters to play as
And for an extra $4.99 you recieve
~ 4 More characters (Team JNPR)
And new DLC is being made, but not to further improve the lackluster combat or add more content to the game, but it's COSTUMES for the characters you have and costumes for the DLC characters.
There are four new packs being released on Steam soon, priced at $1.99 which give 4 costumes each which add virtually nothing to the game other than to take money out of your pocket and grab the suckers who will buy anything with the RWBY name on it.
For a total of about $33 with all the DLC, this game simply is NOT worth your money and the content is not worth your time.
Buy a different game than this one, there are many more games more deserving of that $33 dollars and this game is not one of them.

Despite its shortcomings, the game is really fun. It is your basic hack and slash. If you watch the show you will have more enjoyment with it then someone who hasn't seen it.
I definitely recommend playing with friends versus playing solo. The game scales the difficulty based on how many people are in the party. so you can beat it alone. It is just that the gameply is so painfully repetitive that the only way, to me, to enjoy the game is to play with other people. If you play in "online mode" which is basically just starting a new story, you can start solo and then as you progress you will have people join your game. This really helps out because it can lead you to make new friends that play which will help out when your other friends don't have time/want to play.
All in all, I would recommend buying this game when it is on sale. $20 is a bit much for what the game offers in content. Also, I would recommend buying the DLC because that adds more characters for you to play as. Soon, supposedly, they are going to add new skins which will help with customizing your character a little more.
I would give this game a 7/10 based entirely on the fact it only provides like 2 hours of gameplay. And I would really only recommend it to fans of the show. Otherwise, you would be wasting your money on a semi sub par game.
Finally, the storyline in the game is completely stand alone from the show. There is no connection between it and the show. I am sure all of the fans know that already and only fans are probably looking to buy this game.

The state of GTAV right now is extremly poor. The negative backlash from the attempted banning of OpenIV has cost Rockstar a large amount of customers and resulting in an Overwhelmingly Negative review state. Surely thats not what GTAV, one of the biggest and best open world games deserves right? Well when you centralise your game around making money, it will innevitably be badly recieved by your customers. They dont want to spend anymore than what they paid initially to be able to access the in game content in a reasonable amount of time. And why should they? What the updates of GTAV have become are boring, slow, uninspired and repetitive missions that dont give you nearly as much money as they should. In my opinion even if the money in GTAV was tripled, it would still result in a game with an incredibly large amount of grinding. Im honestly suprised at this point that Rockstar didnt charge us for these DLCs. However the new vehicles are very fun to mess around with but they are incredibly expensive. In the end, Rockstar just wants to make you spend money on their awful shark cards and suprise suprise, even they are overpriced. The most expensive is £60 for $8 mill and that isnt even enough to buy all the new vehicles (or even a fully upgraded yacht (but who would want that anyway because they are beyond useless).
In conclusion, if you want to mess around in an open world game with friends, go for it. But if you want a good vehicle or house or garage or just about anything, be prepared to do heist after heist or delivery mission after delivery mission for what will pretty much be something that you can play around with for a few hours at most. What an incredibly unsatisfying game this is.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is the perfect game for anyone looking for a quick, casual game to play. It is short and can be played in a day, requiring no more than five of play. It is not mechanically intensive; you only need to use your left and right triggers and joysticks.
Its actually gameplay involves controlling Big Brother and Little Brother to solve lightweight puzzles. Both characters are important to complete the game and as a result it builds a feeling of teamwork and family as you play through.
Even with its lowpoly models, it is a cinematic journey with a wonderful score. It builds a sense of adventure as you play. I believe that is the game's greatest strength; enjoy the journey, and this game will not disappoint.
The story is very straightforward yet immersive, and the ending of this game is very powerful; it deals with themes in mature ways that no other game I have ever played has.
In short, this game is wonderful for anyone looking for a relaxing game. I do have to warn though the game doesn't isn't all happy-go-lucky.

This is like a free, short DLC mission for Half-Life 2: longer than Lost Coast but shorter than Episode One.
Whilst this is super short in the grand scheme of things, it was an enjoyable romp back through the sewers of City 17 with a brand new gadget to play with.
If, like me, you haven't played Half-Life 2 in a while, this might just scratch that itch; jumping back into the Gordon Freeman you know and love.

There are many good ideas here:
- the environment - exploring the Half Life 2 Universe outside of City 17 is a v. interesting concept, especially a (literally) darker city
- the darkness revealing things as well as being your ally
- the core mechanic, the new Gravity Gun, essentially allowing safe rocket jumps and encouraging them
The problem is, none of these are threaded together well; the darkness as a mechanic disappears as soon as it's introduced, when this could've led to some wonderful horror moments. Plus, the design of the levels doesn't accomodate the new gravity gun - there are no real advantages to jumping up high, and as soon as you get it all combat is obselete, as it fires a powerful energy pellet harmless to the player. Which is egregious, as the mod ends in a big battle. In addition, I was disappointed that the story didn't really go anywhere.

At about an hour, this may be too ambitious (which is an odd thing to say for a Half Life mod) but a pretty cool and fun demonstration.

This is a fun shooter with some cool mechanics. Throwing sticky bombs on people is amusing, and you can blow up pretty much any walls and dirt floors and turn this game into minecraft. The story is interesting but gets sorta James Bond like as it goes on, which seems odd given the way the game starts.
A few things I didn't like:
No auto save or checkpoints or levels. You just chug along and if you get killed, you gotta go back to your last save, possibly replaying a half hour of the game over again if you're like me and forget to manually save your game after killing every enemy. So that's tedious.
There was also this weird glitch at the submarine where it just explodes for no reason. Seems like a common issue for people. I had to swim ad got killed about 50 times before I finally passed that damn section.
There are some places where you run out of ammo and can't proceed without killing things. So you're screwed. In that case you need to use the max ammo cheat or else possibly restart the whole game from the beginning unless you have multiple saves, but your last save near ammo could well be two hours of gameplay behind where you got stuck.
There are also weird stealth missions that are nearly impossible as the guards always recognize you if you get too close, and you can't use any guns except a pistol with limited ammo, so you're going to die there a lot.
I gotta say if not for the cheats for god mode and max ammo I woulda quit this game because it's really frustrating. But I got it on sale for less than 3 bucks so it was worth it. Cheats made it way more enjoyable. Strongly recommend using them if you're thinking of quitting the game due to issues I mentioned above.

It's a little weird that the stealth sections are based on a hard distance detection zone of around 2-3m, but apart from the somewhat haphazard story and the writing that feels like at least three completely different people with different visions of the game worked on it, it's a really solid title. It's just full of these little sections that have emergent gameplay and multiple solutions to problems. Unfortunately I sometimes found them while backtracking and was like "...wait I did that the boring way." The emergent play tapers off towards the end of the game as the difficulty massively spikes, but I had a lot of fun with this title. Far more than I ever expected to. For fans of games like Half-Life and Unreal.

Certainly a Nostalgia trip for us older gamers, I'm pretty sure though a younger person would probably find this tedious and rather bland. It is an excellent port, runs very smooth, loads ultra fast, no crashes and no graphics anomalies even on Dx9. Strangely it has NO controller support, it always annoys me when console ports cross without controller support. There is little about this game that is 'dynamic' like modern games. There is a lot of level (actual level space) and very very little hand holding, no way points, no dynamic events, very clunky AI, etc. Weapons are rather inconsistent too. It feels a lot like Turok actually. Dialogue is pretty poorly read as well, again this is way back from when gaming companies who really had the budget and the tech to create cinema quality stuff like The Last of Us simply didn't exist. Still. The 'geomod' tech is still, sadly still, the best there ever was for actual destructable environments. No game has ever attempted to even touch this tech of being able to destroy everything freely, without pre-cut pieces or pre-desgined events. Just walk around with some explosives and blast through walls, doors, just about anything can be manipulated, and it is calculated in real time, you don't get some repeated damage out come. When I was a kid and to this day, I don't understand WHY this technology didn't get carried further, especially as hardware technology grew and enabled more memory. Red faction was awesome and the Ps2 had less than 512mb of system RAM I believe. Now consoles have 8 and PCs have 32 and still this kind of software tech is void in our culture. For how successful this was when it came out, for the waves it made with its tech, it is actually very curious to me that it just got dropped. The franchise I understand, RF went the wrong direction over the years, but the 'geomod' tech idea, THAT is what I don't get. My only guess is designing a game that actually put such little restraint on players was a nightmare to design for. This is an old school shooter, not much in the way of puzzles, especially since the Geo Mod tech makes puzzles mostly pointless. Just grab weapons and blast away.
