First of all, let me say that my mother used to always tell me, 'If you don't have anything nice to say, then don't say anything at all.'
Well, I'm gonna disregard that maternal advice and compose my very first negative review on Steam.  If this game had been released by a small indie team, I'd have just bit my tongue and moved onto the next game, but this is Codemasters - I figure, unlike a small indie dev, these guys can afford to take the 'hit' from a negative Steam review.
I've been a big fan of Codemasters since the glory days of BMX and Formula 1 Simulator, way back when I couldn't afford full-price games.  Their games were cheap but just oozed absolute quality.  Their name on the cassette box was all I needed back then.
I had soooooo much anticipation and high hopes for this game.  I even considered staying up until midnight last night just to play it, but couldn't stay awake.  With hindsight, my tired, old brain did me a massive favour.  When I woke up this morning, the very first thing I did was grab my phone and check the Steam page.  I was gutted when I saw the 'Mixed' reviews and even more gutted when I read the negative verdicts.  But I'm an optimist - I figured it can't be that bad... Surely!?
Simply put, this game is a disgrace.  It is nothing more than a 're-skinned' Toybox Turbos with NERF/HASBRO branding and a premium price-tag.  The gameplay is virtually identical to Toybox Turbos.  There is absolutely nothing here that warrants the over-inflated price-tag.  This game had 2.5 years on Toybox Turbos - but you'd swear it was just a Toybox Turbos HASBRO DLC pack, released a month later.
I'm a sucker for bright, colourful games and I adored all the classic MM games over the years.  They were a semi-permanent attachment in my Mega Drive.  This game should have been right up my street - instead it is a mess.  It looks good, but gameplay is where these games should shine but MMWS fails miserably in that department.  Even worse is the single-player options.
If you have Toybox Turbos, then avoid this at all costs.  Don't even be tempted.  All the negative reviews are correct.
If you don't already have Toybox Turbos, then still resist the temptation to buy this.  Instead, download an emulator or something and go play the old Micro Machine games.

-The ambient sound and sound effects of the game may be ok
-A few totally new game modes
-Can play with a gamepad
-This game can be played locally by multiple players
-Steam game achievements
-Steam Trader Cards
-Steam cloudy save system
Cons:
-It is not necessarily a fully-priced video game if you're just a single player or just a multiplayer. (In fact, playing only a single player modes.)
-The game's championship/tournament mode is missing (Where you can win cars.)
- Does not support the creation of multiple game profiles (a really important feature for me).
-The game lacks much of the general classical feeling and game feel.
-Race modes or AI difficulty level control is missing
-Even if there is some new game modes, still some orginal game modes missing.
-Not include all track types or themes.
-The overall gameplay is too soft, realistic & unaccuracy. (I wanted to be able to control the car's speed and accuracy as in the old V3 video game.)
-The player can't jumping or bounces with the car (Just like in V3)
-The player can't turn 360 degrees in place or can but, the car moves and slides, which can partly explain the poor maneuverability. (Not simple and fun like V3)
-The vehicles control & speed is generally fairly identical, depending on the vehicle type.
-AI/Bots will punish you instantly and accurately when they are next to you. (They use their own weapon.)
-The game race a speed & feeling is missing. (That's one of the things that really is this series known.)
-The range of cars is too simplified for animations and 3d models. (I mean these floating weapon solutions, which only make it easier to design games. Weapons are not like V3)
-There are no water tracks & boat races.
-Not the same category of car racing. (Everything is mixed.)
-Classic driving school is missing (The one in the V3 series was funny)
-Pretty lame pre-order bonuses. (I wish someting more, like remastered/gold version of old versions of the Micro Machines series.)
So it is not really the best version of the game series, but not the worst. Just a lot of things are missing from the game. Maybe some of them can be found in later game updates, hopefully.
The game does not replace V3 or is necessarily a better video game than Toybox Turbo.
I can say pretty much the same thing like many other games. If there is little content for you that you are willing to pay for the big price tag, that's okay.
FIN:
Haluasin niin kovasti suositella tätä videopeliä mutta, en vain pysty!
Peli ei sinänä ole täysin epäonnistunut mutta, pelinä ei valitettavasti kunnioita vanhemman pelisarjan laatu vaatimuksia ja alkuperää. Tämä näkyy eritoten pelin sisällön määrässä ja pelattavuudessa.
Kysessä on toki party videopeli, joka suosii moninpelaamista mutta, valitettavasti itse olen kuin yksinpelaaja ja valitettavasti pelinsisältö ei juuri tarjoa paljoa yksinpelattavaa sisältöä koska on pääosin moninpeli.
Pelin ohjattavuus ja nopeus on kaikilla ajoneuvoilla sama riippumatta ajoneuvo tyypistä.
Peli ei sisällä myöskään itselleni tärkeä mestaruus sarjaa, jossa voittaa uusia autoja kun voittaa turnauksen.
En tiedä onko edes pelisuunnittelijat edes itse pelanneet vanhoja Micro Machines peli sarjaa.
Peli on kuin Toybox Turbo mutta, vähemmällä sisällöllä ja Micro Machines iholla.
Kuitenkin minä aijon pitää pelin mutta, tuntuu silti että, pelinsuunnittelijat ei tunnu paljoa välittävän asiasta sekä videopelistä tai pelaajista. Myöskään codemasterilla ei myöskään tunnuta kovin paljon välittävän asiasta yleisesti. Samat ongelmat tuntuu piilevän myös muissa useissa codemasterin peleissä.
Tässä eritelty vielä ainakin muutamia asioita joista pidän ja en pidä tässä videopelissä:
Plussaa:
-Uusi peli (Edes julkaisivat sellaisen)
-Visuaalisesti hieno ja nykyaikainen
-Pelin ympäristöt pääosin jokseenkin, ok. En ole kuitenkaan varma onko mielikuvituksessa menty liika yli rata suunnittelussa tai onko ratkaisut olleet hyviä mutta, toimii.
-Pelin ympäristön äänet ja ääni effectit ovat ehkä ok
-Muutamia täysin uusia pelitiloja
-Voi pelata peliohjaimella
-Tätä peliä voi pelata paikallisesti useampi pelaaja
-Steam peli saavutukset
-Steam vaidettavat kortit
-Steam pilvitallennus
Miinusta:
-Ei ole välttämättä täyden hintansa arvoinen videopeli, jos olet vain yksinpelaaja tai vain moninpelaaja. (Itse pelaan vain yksinpeli tilaa.)
-Yksinpelin mestaruus tila puuttuu (Siellä missä voit voittaa autoja.)
-Ei tue useamman peli profiilien luomista (Itselleni todella tärkeä ominaisuus.)
-Pelistä puuttu jokseenkin se yleinen klassinen tunne ja peli tuntuma.
-Kilpatilojen tai AI vaikeustason säätö puuttuu
-Ei kaikkia ratateemoja tai tyyppejä
-Vaikka on uusia pelitiloja, useita vanhjoa klassiko pelitiloja puuttuu
-Pelin autojen yleinen ohjattavuus on liian pehmeä, reallistinen ja epätarkka. (Haluasin autojen ohjattavuuden olevan nopea ja tarkka kuten vanhassa V3 videopelissä.)
-Pelaaja ei pysty hyppii auton kanssa. (Toisin kuin V3 pystyy)
-Pelaaja ei pysty kääntymään 360 astetta paikallaan tai voi mutta, auto liikkuu ja liukuu samaan aikaan, mikä voi selittää osittain huono ohjattavuuden.
-Pelin autojen hallittavuus ja nopeus on yleisesti melko identtisiä ajoneuvosta riippumatta.
-Tekoäly kuljettajat rankaisevat heti ja tarkasti kun ovat vierelläsi. (Käyttävät omaa asetta.)
-Se videopelin kilpanopeus puuttuu. (Se yksi niitä asioita mistä oikeasti tämä sarja on tunnettu.)
-Autojen asevalikoima on liian yksinkertaistettu, nuo animaatiot ja 3d mallit. (Tarkoitan näitä leijuvia ase ratkaisuja, jolla vain helpotettaan pelisuunnittelua. Aseet eivät ole niin kuin V3 ovat)
-Ei vesikilpa-ratoja ja veneitä
-Ei saman luoka autokilpailuja (Kaikki on sekakilpailuja.)
-Klassinen autokoulu puuttuu (Se joka oli V3 -sarjassa, se oli hauska).
-Melko laiha pelin ennakkotilaus bonukset. (Olisin toivonut enemmän, vaikkapa remasteroidun/gold version vanhemmista peleistä.)
Ei siis todellakaan kyse ole parhaasta versiosta pelisarjassa mutta, ei huonoimmastakaan. Pelistä vain juuri puuttuu paljon asioita. Ehkä näkin saadaan myöhemmissä pelipäivityksissä toivottavasti.
Peli ei siis korvaa V3 tai ole välttämättä parempi videopeli kuin Toybox Turbo.
Voinkin sanoa melkolailla samaa tästä kuten useasta muusta pelistä. Jos vähän sisältöä riittää sinulle josta olet valmis maksaa ison hintalapun niin, ok.

I'll get straight to my pros and cons for RWBY: GE
* Pros
- Canon story that bridged the gap between Volume 2 and 3 (during a hiatus)
- Revisting classic locations featured in RWBY
- An acceptable plot
- The ability to play as team RWBY and JNPR (via DLC)
- Fast-paced and easy to play
- Working towards steam achivements for the game is fun for the most part
* Cons
- Almost no replayability (there is no driving force to do the same few things over and over again).
- Very short story overall (it only takes a  few hours if even)
- No progress or communication from dev team for the most part, since the game was launched (except when paid DLCs are ready).
- The game has been reduced to paid DLC costume packs, which is tragic.
This will most likely be the only RWBY game fans will see, and that is very unfortunate. There is no passion displayed in this project, and the apathy / silence has spoken for itself. It appears that this was really just a quick buck for Roosterteeth to utilize, when fans were itching for anything RWBY-related during hiatuses.
As a fan of RWBY, I cannot recommend this game to other RWBY fans (and honestly just watch a gameplay video), but most definately cannot recommend this to gamers in general.

Alright I understand that people complain about the main story. It doesn't go very far when it comes to developing anything. Instead of answering questions we already had in the first game it puts you up with even MORE questions marks and doesn't give you any answers whatsoever. It's clear that they either planned a third game before they even started developing Mankind Divided, or Square Enix jumped in mid development and told the developers to cut the game so they can release more DLC. So yes, I do understand why people don't like the main story.
What I do not understand is why people say the writing is bad. Yeah, the game does a lot of "rubbing in your face" when it comes to establishing the world around you. But this is exactly what Deus Ex is about, isn't it? It's about the world around you, the conspiracies, the injustice, the characters and I think all those things were very well established and written. The sidequests in this game are plain amazing. Theres so many little stories, so many things I didn't see coming and so much to discover. I finished the game in around 27h now on my first playthrough and it still feels like I haven't seen half of the stuff and sidemission.
The gameplay is a serious upgrade and improvement from Human Revolution. While I still think some of the cover controls suboptimal (why do I have to hold a button to turn around a corner for what feels like a second?) the gameplay itself overall is ver well done. The new augmentations are very useful and satisfying to use. Graphite Nanoblade? Icarus Dash? Hell yeah, count me in. There's not a single augmentation that I'd call useless. They all fullfill their specific roll for your specific playstyle that you chose. They also did a VERY good job in balancing stealthy and rambo playstyle. I've tried both and both are equally hard to master if you're not careful. This is partly due to the AI that received a serious upgrade. If they notice you being there they will no longer walk to the spot where they've last seen you. They will search the entire area until the timer runs out so you actually have to move around while hiding. When discovered as a threat they WILL try to surround you and if there's too many of them they WILL overwhelm and kill you.
There's even more ways to finish your mission than before. Each and every single (mostly huge) mission area has dozens of ways to achieve your goal. You can either breach through the roof, through the canals, you can shoot your way through, you can sneak your way through enemy lines, etc. The leveldesign is simply amazing.
The game looks great. The textures are all high resolution, the shaders look good, the faces are very well done (remember the Human Revolution plastic skins? Eugh) and sharp and the locations look increadibly believeable and unique. The art team did an amazing job here and that further cements the unique artstyle that Deus Ex had since Human Revolution.
However, the performance is rather meh. There's a couple of problems. The loadingtimes are absurd if you didn't install the game on an SSD (up to 2-3mins for me in some cases) and the game stutters quite a bit AFTER you've finished loading a level until the engine actually finished loading all the assets. This has gotten better with recent patches however.
I don't have the strongest rig for sure, but I've seen games that look a tad bit better that runs just better with less stuttering and hiccups.

I've played the original game and finished every mission on DMD-mode with an S-ranking. The game was great and even as an "advanced casual gamer" you could finish the hardest missions with the best results.
Now i also bought the special edition but i have to say it feels different (minor spoilers ahead!):
- Although i know how the game works I cannot dodge 50% of enemy attacks but it is absolutely essential for the game to dodge enemy attacks. (For example: 2 Frosts attack me, I fight one of them with a Yamato-combo and can see the other prepare to launch ice-bolts in the background. Of course I try to evade the attack but Vergil takes ages to interrupt the combo and start doing jumping/air tricks. Nero and Dante feel a bit slower, too. I don't know about Trish and Lady because i haven't played them yet.)
- It feels like the producer put Vergil in Nero's and Dante's place during the missions without even adapting the Style-ranking to Vergil's abilities. I tried to fight Dante in SoS-mode in Mission 1 but it is impossible to get a better Style rank than C (most of the time it was D). Nero on the other hand just grabs Dante with his Devil Buster and instantly gets a C or B rank during battle. It feels like the producer didn't even try to get S ranks for the missions and see if it is doable with Vergil (for advanced players at least).
- Some achievements are a pain in the ***. Get an S-rank in every mission in Human-mode although you already did that in Devil Hunter-mode or do the Bloody Palace 5 freaking times! It's just a waste of time for achievement farmers.
- Vergil has no double-jump nor evasion moves to get away from the enemy (unless you are transformed into a devil). In DMC 3 he had trick down to get away from enemies. Why abandon that ability? Terrible decision.
- Targeting when there are more than 5 enemies on the battlefield is impossible. Only cheap way to deal with hordes is to turn the cam away from the horde and then use roundtrip but that is just boring. Even the experts in youtube-videos have no other method to deal with increased numbers of enemies.
+ 3 new characters that feel really different from each other (Lady and Trish look like fun in some internet videos).
+ A few new costumes come with the game.
+ Playing as Vergil is really cool unless you get hit by 50% of the attacks.
+ A few new cutscenes for the new characters, but nothing special really.
+ Collecting Orbs and stuff with one character counts as collected with all others (For example: Collect all blue orbs with Nero/Dante. Then you start the Vergil campagin and he already has all lifebars.)
+ No real problems with the controller adaption.
I downvote this game because it is too expensive for the newly added content and the really, really bad Style ranking system and missing evasion moves of Vergil. I will change it once it is cheaper or fixed. (English isn't my mother tongue, hope you understood it)

Music: x/10 It's ok for me. But whether you like it or not, you have to figure it out yourself.
Gameplay: 9/10 Great game experience. Every characters have their own style. Capcom has done enough optimization work to keep it running on fps. Never feel delay in game. They are not that difficult, but if you don't know where to go next, use google.
In general, it is a great game to have.  When you get used to it, you will find much pleasure in your show time. Such a Pity Capcom stop making good games like DMC4 these days.

I already owned all Red Faction titles, but wanted to buy a digital version too.
Now that it was on sale, I immediately grabbed it.
This is the original and true Red Faction game.
All the others that came afterwards had in no way the impactful and interesting story and journey, as you can experience in Red Faction 1.
If you are interested in trying a game from the Red Faction franchise, this is the right one to play.
___________________________________
+ Graphically it was impressive for it's time, which still counts today (for me)
+ Old school FPS action with a good and unique storyline
+ Very enjoyable and powerful array weapons (all acquired as you proceed through the story)
+
+ "Geo-Mod", aka destroy those polygonal textures as you wish or so to say "the direct way is not always the best one, so make your own one"
+ Has Multiplayer
+ Different enemies and encounters scaling in difficulty through the story, plus boss fights!
~ Multiplayer unfortunately only has Deathmatch and CTF modes (no coop story).
~ Not a bad thing, but quickly forgotten: No autosaves - save your game regularly in the menu!
~ As good as the soundtrack is, the scores don't always loop and if they do, it sounds badly put together.
~ The AI's aiming is ridiculously accurate, making the end game part very tough (for example:
)
- Original game doesn't support all screen resolutions, even as a Steam release (maximum is 1280x1024)
- The ending is somewhat abrupt and the "final boss" is rather lame for a final boss. Even if it makes sense as an encounter on planet Mars, there still could have been something better, or at least bigger. You will probably be surprised when it ends.
- Story leaves the player with an "open end". The tryhard successor of it is Red Faction 3 - Guerilla, which connects to the story of RF1, but does that rather poorly. Without a cutscene or info at the end about the main protagonist's whereabouts, it ends somewhat disappointing. I personally would have liked to know what happens to him at that point.
- You need mods to fix stuff like the resolution for widescreen, a bit disappointing considering a Steam release.

To the developer's/porter's credit, I didn't experience a single bug - no crashes, no clipping, etc.  They did their jobs, yey for them.
In short though, this game was just an exercise in pushing through tedium.
For the first half of the game (and indeed the second half), I was bored.  Their storyline had nothing to get excited about, nothing to inspire intrigue nor any characters worth thinking about.  It was a long series of 'walk into room, get shot at by guards, shoot back at guards until silence, walk into next room'.
The second half, not content with simply being tedious, added in a great deal of annoyance to the experience - with most enemies able to one-hit-kill you (many through solid walls without line-of-sight) and no other way to engage them other than to run in and rely on blind luck.  All hail the quicksave button.
Granted, I brought a lot of that on myself by playing on hard, but I doubt that enemies' instantaneous reactions and ability to track you omnisciently was added by the difficulty setting.
To make matters more frustrating, there were at least three points spread throughout the game at which I thought the it would finally end, only to be denied such relief and sent on another random mission.  "Excellent, you did the big thing, now go do this".
The much-lauded geo-mod feature is just a glorified door-maker.  Nothing more.  It doesn't allow you to flank your enemies (because they always know where you are).  It doesn't allow you to bring the building down around them (because there are indestructable supports).  It doesn't allow you to blow yourself meaningful cover nor block paths with rubble.
It just makes doors.
Speaking of doors though, I really should have been making them myself because the mechanics for the real ones was utterly stupid.  To open an automatic door you must rub your face on it, should face-rubbing stop then the door will become bitter about the experience and almost instantly close.  The result is that you cannot use door frames for cover and must expose yourself to all the enemies in the room if you want to try and hit even one.
I am very glad I didn't pay full price for this refuse and am finally relieved to rid my hard drive of it.
If you feel you must play this to tick off a box (as in my case), buy it on sale and breeze through it on easy.  Better yet, wait until it becomes abandonware and download it for free.

This is the game I have been waiting for.
This is a game made by people who stopped and thought about what makes games good... and what doesn't.  Nothing unneccisary was added; no gimmick mechanics, no "surprise!" changing of the rules.  Everything is straight forward, in your face, down your throat awesome.
This game is made of win.
What you can expect:
This game is the perfect mix of frantic and tactical.  You'll find yourself pausing, issuing orders, and then madly darting around the screen trying to handle three or more fronts at once as a new mutation puts you on the ropes.  And no matter how bad it gets, no matter how harsh the mutation roullette wheel grinds you down... it's... still... fun.
So how many ways can you skin the provervial cat?
And all of that?  Those are just SOME of the ways I've beaten... THE SAME LEVEL.  That's right... any tactic you can afford (BP's pretty thin if you don't think things through)... can be made to work.  In fact, that tactic you just tried and failed?  It might just be you went in the wrong order.  Did you spread yourself too thin?  Forget to backfill some defenses?  Did you recycle your old swag and move it forward?  Oh... did you get that one mutation you don't have defenses for?  Well... TRY IT AGAIN!
I rarely rave over a game... but in the last few years I've seen so much schlock, so many shiny letdowns... to have finally been given a chance to enjoy game that doesn't 'try'... it just succeeds.
If you like real time strategy games, go find a Let's Play for this game.  I'll bet you press the buy now button before the video's over.  I did.  And I have no regrets.

I'll get straight to my pros and cons for RWBY: GE
* Pros
- Canon story that bridged the gap between Volume 2 and 3 (during a hiatus)
- Revisting classic locations featured in RWBY
- An acceptable plot
- The ability to play as team RWBY and JNPR (via DLC)
- Fast-paced and easy to play
- Working towards steam achivements for the game is fun for the most part
* Cons
- Almost no replayability (there is no driving force to do the same few things over and over again).
- Very short story overall (it only takes a  few hours if even)
- No progress or communication from dev team for the most part, since the game was launched (except when paid DLCs are ready).
- The game has been reduced to paid DLC costume packs, which is tragic.
This will most likely be the only RWBY game fans will see, and that is very unfortunate. There is no passion displayed in this project, and the apathy / silence has spoken for itself. It appears that this was really just a quick buck for Roosterteeth to utilize, when fans were itching for anything RWBY-related during hiatuses.
As a fan of RWBY, I cannot recommend this game to other RWBY fans (and honestly just watch a gameplay video), but most definately cannot recommend this to gamers in general.

Micro Machine: World Tour is kind of like when your favorite fast food place messes up your order. While it's not what you expected, it's still relatively enjoyable in it's own right.
The best way I could describe it is if Micro Machines v4 had a baby with Overwatch. The controls are basically the same as most Micro Machines games, being fast overhead view racing games with some slippy controls that take a while to get used to. The quote un-quote Overwatch elements come from it's emphasis on online play, customizable vehicles and such. While the game is still new (currently writing this review on the day of release) meaning that the online play is...lacking, It fortunately has bot play which works fine. The gameplay itself was hard for me to get into, but that's mainly because I just suck at video games in general. But after a few races and a try at battle mode, I can say that it is at least fun, which is really all that should matter in a game like this.
The available characters/classes are also a nice touch. Again, much like Overwatch, TF2, Smite and various MMOs, there's a choice of 12 characters (two of them being G.I. JOE charcaters, which is pretty sweet) which each have their own special abilities and powers. They even managed to find a way to make the obligatory Medic class work in an overhead racing game, as well as make them as fun to play as the rest of the cast. Plus, the optional skins are all unique and interesting. Pre-ordering this game was a smart decision to play as a an ice-cream truck driven by a Russian girl.
Of course, this dosen't mean the game dosen't have it's problems. Like, the lack of a singleplayer mode is a little annoying. I'm fine with online play, but the fact that I just can't set up my own races and bots like most other racing games is annoying. Plus, I do think there should be more variety with game modes. 3 is simply not enough, especially with the concept of an MMO racing game. In general, there's a lack of variety and content, so definately wait for a handful of updates to come around and iron out some of the kinks. And, the price is a bit too much, so wait for a sale if you want it.
As of writing this, I haven't even played a full hour, so I might not be the best judge. But, chances are that if you're even the little-ist bit interested in this game, you might like it. If your looking for a remastered sequel to one of the hidden gems from the playstation era, you might not see it here. But if your looking for a relatively fun racing game with decent online features, I'd say give it a shot.
Oh, and of course, Brain Blessed makes for an awesome announcer.

Alright I understand that people complain about the main story. It doesn't go very far when it comes to developing anything. Instead of answering questions we already had in the first game it puts you up with even MORE questions marks and doesn't give you any answers whatsoever. It's clear that they either planned a third game before they even started developing Mankind Divided, or Square Enix jumped in mid development and told the developers to cut the game so they can release more DLC. So yes, I do understand why people don't like the main story.
What I do not understand is why people say the writing is bad. Yeah, the game does a lot of "rubbing in your face" when it comes to establishing the world around you. But this is exactly what Deus Ex is about, isn't it? It's about the world around you, the conspiracies, the injustice, the characters and I think all those things were very well established and written. The sidequests in this game are plain amazing. Theres so many little stories, so many things I didn't see coming and so much to discover. I finished the game in around 27h now on my first playthrough and it still feels like I haven't seen half of the stuff and sidemission.
The gameplay is a serious upgrade and improvement from Human Revolution. While I still think some of the cover controls suboptimal (why do I have to hold a button to turn around a corner for what feels like a second?) the gameplay itself overall is ver well done. The new augmentations are very useful and satisfying to use. Graphite Nanoblade? Icarus Dash? Hell yeah, count me in. There's not a single augmentation that I'd call useless. They all fullfill their specific roll for your specific playstyle that you chose. They also did a VERY good job in balancing stealthy and rambo playstyle. I've tried both and both are equally hard to master if you're not careful. This is partly due to the AI that received a serious upgrade. If they notice you being there they will no longer walk to the spot where they've last seen you. They will search the entire area until the timer runs out so you actually have to move around while hiding. When discovered as a threat they WILL try to surround you and if there's too many of them they WILL overwhelm and kill you.
There's even more ways to finish your mission than before. Each and every single (mostly huge) mission area has dozens of ways to achieve your goal. You can either breach through the roof, through the canals, you can shoot your way through, you can sneak your way through enemy lines, etc. The leveldesign is simply amazing.
The game looks great. The textures are all high resolution, the shaders look good, the faces are very well done (remember the Human Revolution plastic skins? Eugh) and sharp and the locations look increadibly believeable and unique. The art team did an amazing job here and that further cements the unique artstyle that Deus Ex had since Human Revolution.
However, the performance is rather meh. There's a couple of problems. The loadingtimes are absurd if you didn't install the game on an SSD (up to 2-3mins for me in some cases) and the game stutters quite a bit AFTER you've finished loading a level until the engine actually finished loading all the assets. This has gotten better with recent patches however.
I don't have the strongest rig for sure, but I've seen games that look a tad bit better that runs just better with less stuttering and hiccups.
I really recommend buying this game. There's a lot of people ♥♥♥♥♥alking about the ingame store. Yeah, it's a bad joke but if nobody told me I would've NEVER even found out about it. I completed the game with no issues whatsoever. Just ignore the hate.
The game itself is amazing. The flaws it has are so minimal that it's almost not worth talking about them, aside from the main story. I'd say you should skip the game if you look for answers to the story. If you just want to play another Deus Ex with amazing gameplay, good dialogues and fascinating leveldesign: go for it. It's completely worth the 50€ I spent. I definitely asked for this.

After completing this game following an extensive playthrough, it's clear to see that this game was made with love, and other peoples hands were shoved inside at the last second.
The sidequests all criss cross and carry on over multiple visits to the city hub; if you do two different quests certain ways, the next time you encounter those people a new sidequest will appear featuring characters from another unrelated sidequest because you helped that person.
It creates a persistent story that makes those sidequests feel just as important as the main story on hand.
You may find yourself spending 10+ hours just exploring and doing sidequests before you feel inclined to do the next story mission.
The level design finally fixed an old problem we all had with the GTA series when we were younger: every single building has a purpose.
Sometimes you can enter one or two apartments within them, sometimes you can blow a hole in one to pass through to another street, or its roof is meant to help you access other areas, but there is not a single part of the hub that feels useless.
It's incredible level design and given that there is only one hub in this game, it feels like this may be the best hub in the series barring perhaps Hong Kong from the very original.
So much thought and care was put into it that it feels like a passionate effort.
The music is unfortunately forgettable, not because it is bad but instead because it never really picks up.
Sometimes in combat you'll notice a very different theme to the music that gets your attention just because it's such a contrast to what has happened up until then.
I was a big fan of Michael McCann's music from the CG trailers of both new Deus Ex titles, and I loved the music in Detroit and Hengsha from DXHR, but this time it's just in the background.
The new mechanics, such as an improved cover system and the WONDERFUL addition of cover-takedowns allowing Jensen to hide the bodies from sight, feels great.
Grabbing ledges when you jump to them makes the already exploration-focused Human Revolution look janky by comparison.
You really feel graceful in your ability to go to anywhere that tickles your fancy, hunting down vents and destructible walls to get every Explorer secret you can find.
The rewards for poking your nose around every corner are bountiful.
The improved CASIE augmentation makes dialogue feel a lot more engaging, the ability to cut people off mid-sentence means that there's a lot of missable dialogue if you pass this particular aug up.
Unfortunately, the enemy AI is still bad, true to the Deus Ex series tradition.
Combat feels as clunky as it did in HR, although I was playing with a controller.
The ability to sneak around and play a more reserved and quiet approach remedies this problem for me, and to be fair, I may need to spend more time trying the combat before considering it bad.
The environments and atmosphere are fantastic.
All the lore you can dig up just by being where you shouldn't be feels incredibly gratifying.
Golem City and the later visits to Prague all provide some interesting looks at the world you're in.
There are even some hints you can find that imply children are involved in a certain trafficking ring from the Czech Mafia within this game, which really changed my opinion of them and even hunt down their leader just out of anger.
You can find so much detail and love in this game, which leads to my only complaint:
Square Enix stuck their hands where they didn't belong.
They handed off the PC version of this game to another team for porting, and it's evident that the porters simply didn't have much experience with the job they were given.
While the game still looks beautiful, the game has been plagued with technical issues since launch.
Sometimes a cutscene will simply freeze for a solid 15 seconds as the audio catches upto it, convincing me that the game had crashed before finally resuming.
I've had two CTD errors with this game as well, although anyone with enough time on PC knows to simply save often and you can't have too much trouble with this.
It is comforting that just a little less than 2 weeks since launch, 4 patches for the game have already been released that have fixed a number of egregious issues.
The cash shop inclusion is also baffling, as the game itself functions incredibly well and is generous in its distribution of money and Praxis kits.
The ending is causing a bit of controversy because it doesn't neatly wrap the story up, and from what I'm learned in online research, it seems that Square Enix is forcing Eidos to cut up their story to make a trilogy.
However with the density of the package, and the amount of lengthy sidequests and fun secrets to discover, it does not feel like a short or rushed game.
Simply a longer and more drawn out experience.
If one was to focus exclusively on the main quest, I can understand them feeling like this game is short.
And so it is with that notion that I come to my conclusion.
Taken as an exploratory game with every sidequest being worth your time - and even partially affecting the ending! - this game is a meaty love letter to the Deus Ex series and deserves every minute of your time.
I'm going to get back to playing it now.

This game is the first game on the Red Faction franchise, yet to be knowns as the best one in the series (Red faction 2 pretty much ♥♥♥♥♥ed over everything) Also, other sequels like Red Faction Guerilla is more of an open-world third person based game, so maybe check those out too.

However, over the years some gamebreaking bugs appeared that won't let you to continue. You will have to download 'Pure faction' patch from internet to progress (I've heard that pure faction doesn't work with Win10)
Pros
-Great soundtrack
-Decent gameplay and story
Cons
-Gamebreaking bugs exist
-Very short gameplay (4~6 hrs if you don't get stuck on puzzles)
-Without patching, you won't be able to get resolution above 1280x1024

7 years after the original release and what we get is the usual CAPCOM routine; Milk fans with an underfunded and rushed title.
It has less content than DMC3, let alone DMC3 special edition. No new boss, a small handful of costumes (no shirtless, either), not even a music remix for playing as the new characters so get ready to mute the game's audio and play your own tunes if you're as bored of the default music as I am by this point. To add insult to injury, 2 of the costumes are DLC... a disgusting move by CAPCOM to a game that was already lacking in content so much since the original release.
This is the bare mininum of what they could've added to justify a Special Edition release. I think they were banking on the idea that Turbo and LDK (loads'a enemies mode) being new 'features' despite being in the original PC release 7 years ago. Hell, they even advertised 60fps and that was in the original PS3 and XB360 release... which back then was an actual standard and didn't need to advertise it.
I'm a huge DMC fan and I just cannot recommend this to any other DMC fan whose looking to make an informed purchase. No, it's not terrible. It's DMC4 with 3 extra characters who are not bad, but have the same flaws of Dante & Nero... rushed and lacking depth when you actually understand them. If you still cannot get enough of DMC4 to this date...  then of course buy it. If you're new to the series and happily slicing through them from 1-3, of course, get it.
But if you're like me, someone who likes DMC4 but couldn't stomach it any longer from the sheer shallowness of it compared to the previous games, then skip this. It's just not enough content and is precisely not worth your time/money. If there were just a few more costumes, none as paid DLC and maybe just one music remix in-game and maybe a sky-box change in blood palace... it would just be enough for me to give it a thumbs up. But as it stands, this is CAPCOM just trying to milk you.

This turned out to be deeper and more fun than I expected. Instead of just another indie title, it's a full, polished and compelling single-player campaign with some nice little extras like weekly challenges. While it's great in terms of gameplay and campaign, it's also fairly shallow overall, and can get repetitive after you've explored all the tech and research, but it's still very much worth at least a single campaign play-through, which clocks in at a minimum of around 6 hours, and a great game overall.
Where this shines above similar titles is the simple, refined and fun gameplay. It's not the deepest strategy game around, and the focus is on units here, rather than structures as in traditional RTSs'. Rocket Bear have cleverly added the strategy elements here, and worked on the mechanics like quick queueing of unit orders, quickly selecting and switching between units, intelligent prioritization based on weapons, and plenty of little things that make strategy and micro-control matter more as the game gets harder and fuller and you progress through the campaign. It's a nice switch of focus from traditional RTS, and it's done very well.
The difficulty has been optimized well too, and this game can generally be played very casually, with a focus on brute force and repetition for those who don't want to think or micro too hard, but at the same time it doesn't take away anything from those who do, and even encourages faster times for completion which means getting smart, fast and learning to hot key and micro really well will be rewarding for you in a way many other titles don't offer.
* The soundtrack too, is pretty under stated and very good at keeping pace and mood while also being fun tracks. I found myself humming along with the title screen and in game a few times. The artist and a couple of
. It's just a shame there are so few tracks.
There are a few annoyances and perhaps mis-steps here, but they're mostly unnoticeable and overall don't harm the game in any big way. The most encompassing problem I kept running into was the lack of solid tutorial/guide elements which meant that I'd continually reach a stage in latter maps where I didn't know what to do to get further, and only by experimenting over and over with new strategies til I found something that worked on different parts of the map could I move forward. This isn't necessarily a bad thing in most strategy games, since the player is expected to learn to progress, but even with the few intro missions, there are so many aspects of this game that you often don't have any clue on possible strategies as a new player and may simply hit a brick wall over and over.
The other thing worth mentioning is that the menu system is somewhat discombobulated and annoying. Units, for example, are listed on the top left in a bar, the unit buy/sell select at the opposing side, and the structure/research menu trees and further option/triggers to the bottom right. This means that unless you're 100% familiar with the hot keys then you'll continually find yourself staring at opposite corners of the screen to view information and select options. Add in the game options being in a middle menu, the progress buttons being further down on title screens, the screen swap selections being in another location on different menus and other strange placements and things get even more erratic. It's a strange albeit minor issue that could easily be refined.
Priced at £10.99/14.99€/$14.99 and £13.59/17.99€/$17.99 for the Deluxe Version (which includes the DLC) at the time of review, Infested Planet does seem a little steep on price, especially when compared to competitors. Creeper World 3: Arc Eternal, for example, is cheaper and offers near countless re-playability and content. However, clocking in at around 6-8 hours for the campaign and at least double that for completionists and when considering the harder difficulties and skirmish mode and weekly challenges, it's still good value for money if you're likely to sink a lot of time into it. For everyone else I'd recommend waiting for a sale of -50% or lower to make this a fantastic deal.
* The Trickster's Arsenal DLC is priced at £3.99/4.99€/$4.99 and a worthwhile addition, adding a level of difficulty with new enemies and mutators, and new weapons and abilities that mix up gameplay. However it's also quite small in terms of content and since the price of the base game is already a contention issue, I feel the content should have been included in the game, or reduced in price. If you've played through the campaign and want to sink more time into Infested Planet, it's a great buy, for anyone else, it's worth waiting.

As you can see from the videos, the graphics on this game are on par with many website Flash games.  So the real question becomes "is this worth the price".  That really depends on what you are looking for in a game.  So let me try to enumerate what I've found playing it so far.
Game Scale:
There are roughly 20 offensive mechanisms to choose from at varying prices that become affordable as new bases are conquered, and items can be salvaged back for a 100% refund.  That's the basic gameplay mechanic.  It's not very deep, but it is somewhat satisfying.
You are defending against -- I'm guessing -- no more than 15 different types of units, which show up as mutations occur for every base conquered.
Game mechanic:
Once you set up a stable defense, pretty much the board is stable and you've got all the time in the world to figure out your strategy.  The bugs might change direction, and there might be race-conditions that show holes in your defenses, but generally a stable defense buys you infinite time to figure out what to do.
The interesting part of the skirmish game is mapping out a strategy for a randomly generated map.  For example, attacking the nearest base might not make any sense as it may trigger units you can't afford to defend against yet.  So you have to find some alternative that is easier to take down.
I also like the mechanism for pulling resources from out of heavy fire.  That's fun.
There's also a campaign, which is mostly a tutorial, but other reviews seem to imply it is worth trying out for some difficult final boss battle - I haven't gotten that far.
Game saves!
There are no game saves, but in skirmish mode you can replay the current board!  At least that feature is in beta as of this writing.  So that's great!
Pricing:
On sale this game goes for $5 which is overpriced.  If your budget is tight I would NOT recommend this game at this price.  There's better gameplay out there from indie developers that might cost a little more, but are more feature rich (Factorio comes to mind even though it's a different genre, and also people have compared this title to Creeper World).
Personally I wanted to study the gameplay mechanisms to see if there was something new here.  Unfortunately, really there is not.  Will I keep playing?  Maybe, but not very much, and I really hesitate keeping the title around when it doesn't even let me save the game.

That's how I'd summarize The Guild II. It's part social/life simulator, part business simulator, RPG and strategy all mixed together to create one of the most unique games I've played. You create your family's first member, then from there, you must choose a career path. You then must go about managing your business, obtaining wealth, climbing the social ladder of your town, ensuring your bloodline continues after your inevitable death, and trying to become the most powerful family through whatever means you wish. One thing worth noting is that while I fully recommend controlling your own business 100%, if this isn't something that interests you, you can choose which aspects of your business you want the AI to manage (can be nice for those who hate micromanagement of inventory, production, employees, etc.) or have the AI manage it fully.
To expand on a few things mentioned, we'll begin with the jobs, which vary enough that certain careers can make the game play entirely differently from others. You can produce raw resources, such as wood/paper, metals, and ingredients to sell to the blacksmiths, alchemists, and priests. Or you can be the ones making armors, weapons, potions, and scrolls that sell quite well in the markets, but have the overhead cost of raw resources. Or you can be the ones using the weapons and armors to beat up opposing families who are either competing with you, or sending their cronies to attack your buildings simply because you looked at them wrong in the market yesterday. Or you can just go to the highways, and rob trading carts that are transferring valuable supplies between towns and businesses. Likewise, if you are a businessman, your own cart is subject to the risk of thievery, especially when travelling outside your city. Or you can be like me, and become a church priest, who can make documents that give social bonuses, and sell for quite a bit, in addition to being able to give sermons. With a high amount of speech, you can get a lot of money for just talking to your attendees about a magical man in the sky. Stupid blacksmith, having to buy metal and make items of value out of them, while I just prophet and profit. This is also one of the easiest ways to butt-kiss your way through the political ladder of your town.
Speaking of the political and social aspects, they are quite entertaining as well. If you're good at speaking, and have some charisma, you can try your luck at earning one of the town positions by manipulating votes and your fellow townspeople. Each town has a certain amount of positions available, each offering little perks and abilities to the holder, and the amount of positions is based on the size of the town. There is also a justice system in place, giving a legal alternative to murdering the thieves that keep robbing your carts, or that one family that keeps sending henchmen to attack your buildings. If you visually witness any crimes, you obtain evidence, which is all listed and can be viewed at any time. Evidence is rated on severity of crime, believability, and time elapsed since crime was committed.  Believability is typically dependent on how you obtain the evidence. If you saw it with your own eyes, it's 100%. If you sent your henchman to town to investigate rumors, it's typically 50% or lower. Once you have a few severe crimes, or a lot of little ones on someone, you can probably get them the death penalty. But if you accuse someone, you are the prosecutor, so make sure you show up to the trial. If you're a criminal, or the thieves guild, it's in your best interest to make sure your prosecutors are unable to arrive to the trial by whatever means necessary.
Overall, this game's unique gameplay and combination of genres makes it worth a purchase. From what others have said, I'd advise looking into The Guild II: Renaissance over this particular version though. Each of the Guild II titles are stand-alone games, so you are not required to own this to play Renaissance. I've been playing Grimm Exclipse and following it's progress from the beginning. There have been a lot of changes from the original release, and while there are some features I miss, (Being able to stand in one spot and hold back an entire horde of Grimm with nothing but Yang's shotgun gauntlets was OP, but endlessly amusing) I do feel like the final product is well balanced and polished, especially for an indie game coming from a company that's better known for their video content.
Personally, I think the best feature of this game is the adaptabily in play style.
- If you want a fairly relaxing but fun hack and slash game where you simply run around spamming the left mouse button, you can do that and get through the game, especially if you party up with some friends.
- Or, if you wanna throw together some sick combos intermixed with perfectly timed dodges and counter attacks, really challenging your situational awareness and sequencing skills, that's also an option.
Both will win you the game without too much difficulty, but the results are progressively more satisfyingly lethal depending on how complicated you choose to make it.
The models all look great, though I do miss the fact that the originals looked exactly like the show. I understand that caused performance issues... My hope is that RT will elect to continue making content for this game, possibly including alternate oufits and other graphical effects for those who have the rig to run it.
Story-wise? It's not going to keep you on the edge of your seat or anything, but to me, this isn't meant to be an intense game with lots of twists and turns, as the show can be. I still think the story is interesting and fun, especially with all the banter and wit from the playable characters, but on the whole, I feel the game and it's story was mostly meant as a casual and easy-going game that you can mostly breeze through when you need a break from the intensity of competitive play.
After all; in a game, what's more relaxing than oblitering dozens of Grimm without breaking a sweat? (Though some of the later levels will challenge you PLENTY if you're not paying attention)
Overall a great 4 player co-op game that I definitely recommend, so long as you focus on the casual, easy-going fun of it and don't take it too seriously.

As a big fan of the show, I really was looking forward to playing this game, and putting some hours into it
But after 4 hours, I completed the game at level cap on my first playthrough, all skills unlocked for Blake (for those of you who aren't familiar with the show, that's black hair, cat ears).
The game was all very familiar. You go through linear levels (chapters), fighting monsters until you get to the end. Occasionally you'll have waves of monsters, or you'll need to defend a point, or push a bomb on a cart to the end of a track. There are a few things to do, but it's rather same-y. The level design is beautiful, but they're empty, minus the occasional crate or artefact.
The combat is fast, and feels as if it mimics the show. But you'll be attacking an enemy for a few seconds until you realise that you have actually done no damage. The enemies seem to be able to block most of your moves, and you need to get a few hits into a combo to be able to do any damage, and even then you don't really do much damage.
When you first play, you choose a character and you are thrown straight into the game. No tutorial, no prompts on controls, no explanation of the mechanics whatsoever. The dialogue really lacks in terms of character development, and relies on knowledge of the show to be able to feel as if you can get to know the characters. Any cutscenes are bland.
The other mode, Horde mode, is horribly unbalanced. You're going to need a full group of 4 players to get anywhere in horde mode. It just seems impossible with any less. No spoilers here, but the final boss also should be played with 2 or more players, or it can take a real long time.
There's a lack of real story and character development in the short campaign, and the attempt to add such comes late in the game. There's little variety in combat and the characters don't really feel different enough to be able to play over again with the other characters.
However, my review isn't all negatives.
The multiplayer works pretty much flawlessly. I couldn't fault it at all, although it could do with voice chat for when you're playing with friends. I didn't notice any server-side lag and the graphics are beautiful. The controls feel natural, and despite the lack of any form of tutorial, are very easy to pick up.
The battle mechanics are rather straightforward. You have 2 primary melee attacks (light and heavy), your ultimate attack and your ranged weapon. An icon shows above an enemy's head just moments before it attacks, giving you just enough time to dodge out the way. Or, you are often given the chance to counter, which stops an enemy from being able to block. The game also feels a lot more fun when you have a friend to play with. I wouldn't recommend soloing unless you need that solo achievement.
Overall, I think that the game felt a little rushed. With large open areas that are most of the time just empty, minus a few crates, explosive barrels and hidden artifacts which provide XP boosts, rather repetitive levels and a lack of any tutorial. There were small things in the game that could have been added which would have made a lot of difference to the quality of the game. It just needed a tutorial, a bit more freedom to roam around, a little more thought on balancing the Horde mode and boss, and a bit more to do. I would recommend trying it only if you're a die-hard RWBY fan and you have friends to play with and some money to spare. Try and get this at a discount, because I really don't feel like it was worth £15/$25. Try get it on a 50% sale. As a massive fan of the show, this was a little disappointing.
Don't get me wrong, it's great fun playing with friends and all, but don't expect hours and hours of this game without seeing everything.

Microtransactions in a Sp game made a lot of people angry then the game had optimization issues with game breaking bugs as well, story cut in half etc. Initially  no one spoke about the game itself, only about how corporate greed destroyed a venerable franchise.
The good thing is that even if Square Enix did everything to screw this game up, they couldn't. Eidos made one of the best games this year, and if you liked previous Deus Ex titles or stealth games in general you will enjoy this game for sure.
The gameplay was improved from Human Revolution. New augmentations, better controls for gunfight, and a way better and intricate level design we have here. There are more options how to solve situations and honestly the gameplay reminded me more to the original Deus Ex than to Human Revolution which is probably the best compliment which this game can get.
Side quests are excellent some of them are memorable such as some areas which were great to discover or stealth/fight through.
The story of the game is not that bad as everyone says. It is a competent, well told and deus exish story. The problem is that it's unfinished due to publisher orders. It definitely feels like a first episode of a sequel or trilogy whereas previous Deus Ex games had grandiose, epic and complete stories with definitive endings. We won't get these things in Mankind Divided.
While optimization is still considered an issue, I could run this game on medium settings with a GTX 660, 8GB Ram so you actually don't need a monster rig to run it. They patched also the game breaking bug which prevented players to finish the game, so it's definitely a playable product now. I personally enjoyed the hell out of this game, if you are not sure how you would like it, wait for a sale, or skip it or do whatever you wish. But it's a good game.

This is to CoD what Duke Nukem 3D would've been to Wolfenstein 3D, if Wolfenstein didn't have Mecha-Hitler or a gatling gun.  The weapons are fun as hell, the situations are fun as hell, and your character tosses out a gloriously awful one-liner after about every third mook he kills. Like in FC3, the nonstandard-in-a-good-way stealth system allows for ultra-stealthy infiltrations, semi-stealthy Arkham Asylum-style mook-terrorizing campaigns, tactical assaults with a stealthy start to shut down alarms / plant explosives / dispose of priority targets followed by a noisy finish, or just waltzing in with an unnecessarily large gun and murdering everyone and their reinforcements; all are viable, all are effective, and all are extremely entertaining, with many ways to carry them out, and many opportunities to do so in elaborate enemy complexes, filled with hiding spots and sniping perches.  FC3:BD also adds the option of luring a big angry monster into the base after deactivating a shield, which, while hilarious to watch, does feel a little overpowered.

It doesn't fix some of the fundamental problems with the original 2008 release (replaying about half of the levels as filler) but it adds enough replayability and style with the 3 extra playable characters to warrant a purchase from anyone who wants to support the original Devil May Cry series, or from anyone looking for a decent character action game. Seriously fun, seriously stylish, what more could you ask for from a Devil May Cry game?

I've been a huge fan of the franchise for a long time. From the very first game in the early 2000s to the most recent western reboot, I just can never get enough of the immensely satisfying and stylish hack-n-slash action. With DMC1 having the best story progression, DMC2 a complete tragedy, DMC3 SE being my all-time favorite and the original DMC4 being slightly disappointing; and the western reboot though excellent in its own way, doesn't quite feel the same--- So the release of this game is an absolute delight.
After spending dozens of hours playing through the game, I am confident to say that this is the definitive Devil May Cry experience to any newcomers or veterans alike.  This is not just another HD remaster game like many tend to be in the market; this is a different beast on its own. First is the graphic upscaling and the new 60fps cap which render much detailed and sharper images and textures, smoother animations which only enhances the gameplay’s fluidity so much more than ever before. Turbo mode is a welcoming return from DMC3 SE. The biggest edition of this version of the game is the three new playable characters, Vergil, Trish, and Lady, which offers 3 new distinctive play style in an already excellent action-packed experience. Vergil can play through all 20 missions, while Lady and Trish plays Nero and Dante’s missions respectively. One really noticeable thing is that the new characters is clearly designed around the new Legendary Sparda mode in which majority of their move sets consist of huge AoE and crowd control effect which made them seem really overpowered, especially Vergil. Though I wouldn’t say they are completely unbalanced but to get the most out of their skills, playing on a harder difficulty is highly recommended.
About the brand new “Legendary Sparda Mode”, it’s a silly idea on paper, and even more ridiculous in actual gameplay. Having an overwhelming number of enemies swarming at the same area, it’s hard to keep up or even see what is going on at times; enemies would just keep spawning and flying all over places as you press buttons. Not to say the game becomes a button masher in that mode, just the fact that the combat becomes mindless and instinctive rather than being grounded and tactical. I guess it can be both a good and bad thing depends on you play style, it is not a mode to be taken seriously, but one thing for sure that it is still tons of fun to play with. It also showcase in a technical aspect, despite all the explosive actions and the sheer number of things happening on screen, the gameplay still runs smoothly at a stable 60fps throughout, with no screen-tearing or slowdowns, which is definitely impressive.
Loads of contents plus hours of fun at only half of normal retail price. Not to mention that this is an excellent PC port and really well optimized. Easy to pick up and learn, hard to master; this is the spirit of any DMC titles (except 2, that game sucks so much). Greatness through and through, anyone looking for an over-the-top action game, this is a must-buy. Any fans of the franchise will without a doubt, adore this gem.

I'll try to ignore the Take2 chaos, though because of that this might be the last GTA i buy.
It was a good journey, seeing that i started playing GTA 1 on my first PC, when i was a kid.
Single Player:
-V is clearly a masterpiece and there's nobody doing games like this at the level that Rockstar does. They basically build on  the same game, just adding to it, so their decades of experience makes it a loosing battle for new starters like Watchdogs(Driver) and all those cash grabs, that don't dedicate their life for making the perfect game in a certain genre.
With that said, i miss the vibrance of GTA2, with the crazy gangs they had, and a certain lore. A remake of that with this new engine would be a crazy hit for them, in this age of repackaged classics. It wouldn't work to go goofy with a new story, cause that's why Saint's Row exists. Speaking of that, the Zaibatsu car in GTAV as an easter egg, brought a tear to my eye. Thanks Rockstar for that.
Multiplayer:
-oh boy oh boy, where do i start with this one. I know many kids love it, and take two made sure to mess it up really good, cause i guess making billions selling the game is not enough. I won't go too much into this, cause as a game developer myself, i see the pointless nature of it. I've seen the parasites among us that have no respect for what they do, and just want all the money. Not just money.....all of it. Micro transactions in a full priced game like this are just♥♥♥♥♥♥ simple as that.
Last time i've entered the online feature, i waited forever to load. I play most games that launch these days, and GTA5 online is by far the slowest affair ever. By the time it loads i'm questioning if i was in the mood to play or not. Los Santos is a shadow of it's single player version, with just a handful of cars in variety, everything seems baren, and it's crazy how an online game can look more deserted and feels more lonely than it's single player story. Except the crazy random explostions from you're generic "let's create chaos" kinda player.
For me, GTA multiplayer was always about the fun of actually having fun in the same city as the campaign but with other players, and just roaming around, not going into "paralel universes" like the missions at the moment are playable. It's a mixed bag. Some are pretty good, but the city is now just a hub for those, and it's not the actual game. Long discussion but i feel it lost focus.
I bored people enough, so in short, even if i find the single player as a masterpiece, the money they make on the Online component, and seeing they have another Online focused expansion coming up, all i can say to Rockstar, is to be careful. I understand Take2 will make a bunch of money for their corporate overlords while they are still alive, but in the long run, it damages the brand, and people won't have the same feeling and aura around GTA. It worked and made billions cause it was a respectful build up to this point. So as long as the next entry will be as solid and will stay on it's feet, not rely on online, and as long as Red Dead Redemption will be as focused as all products till now, i think we're good. There's a bright future ahead.
P.S. Rockstar...speaking of Read Dead....us PC gamers literally made you in the 90's. We were the ones that spread the word of GTA. You already have all the money in the world, so don't sign some exclusive contract. Just launch the next game on all platforms. We're here, we'll support you, don't let us down.

I really should play this more often. Nothing quite like battling against swarms of alien bugs with increasingly murderous weaponry. The at times seemingly unstoppable swarms- depending on which mutations the enemy happens upon- provides very tense gameplay requiring quick decisive movements lest you be fought to a standstill and trust me, you want to be on the defensive for as little time as possible. Alien mutations will punish slow playstyles. This fine balance between hold and push has the momentum shifting constantly particularly at the higher levels/difficulties.  The fast paced gameplay coupled with charming visuals means Infested Planet is a great strategy game for those looking for that quick adrenaline fix.

Bought this largely because of the great reviews, and yes, it is that good.
It's just the right balance of difficulty, where you don't feel overwhelmed but you will lose sometimes. And the thing about it is, the gameplay changes so much on the fly. A mutation of the enemy creatures will change the dynamic of the level, or suddenly they start sending a huge attack towards a lightly defended area.
You also have a certain amount of 'credits', don't remember the actual term they use in game, that allow you to buy soldiers or powerups on each level. Because you can cash in units for a full refund at any time, that means that you also can change strategies mid-level when you see that a plan isn't working like you'd hoped. That is, you can sell cheap soldiers and equip your existing ones better, buy turrets with the extra money, or any other variety of different approaches.
There are a lot of indie games on here with great concepts that suck because they have terrible execution. This game is the opposite - a concept that doesn't sound like much, but it's executed perfectly. I don't even usually like these types of games but Infested Planet is an exception.
Outstanding game - if you're curious enough about the game to read this review, then trust me, it is worth buying.

Im usually not a fan of simulation games. I play "The Sims" for a day and call it quits, its just not for me. Ive only been playing "The Guild 2" for half a week and ive already invested nearly 40 hours at the expense of work and sleep, for me this game was very addictive. Its practically the sims but based in the dark ages where you grow a family and basically conquer your village with money, economic strength, and political power. This game features an abundance of mechanics, marriage, work, religion, politics, assassinations, blackmail, ect but there are various areas where its broken. For example there are times when my building was being attacked and i couldnt defend it because the attackers were glitched inside the house while not actually inside the building. (this can be countered by sending your men inside the building, then exiting the building with the camera and re selecting your men and ordering them to attack, then they exit and fight properly...assuming that there are no obsticles in the way). The game allows you to upgrade your cart to move faster, but you can only move as fast as traffic will allow, sometimes the streets are packed (it may be intentional to force you to strategize timing). My only other complaints are with its options menu, you cannot run this game windowed unless you alter the .ini file, and even then it pauses when you click away to another monitor, and you cannot remap buttons which you might assume isnt a big deal but when your speed keys are + and - it takes much longer when it could have simply been remapped closer to WASD. Oh and the game crashes on me once in a while so i recommend turning on autosave. Otherwise this is a game that i HIGHLY recommend if youre into sims and historical themes, yes it has a few problems but the positives outweight the negatives. Just be sure to get it on sale.

I love Gone Home and Dear Ester and tend to enjoy platformers and pretty, somber things, and from what I'd heard I thought I'd be really into this short/sweet experience. Unfortunately, there's not much sweet (or effectively somber) about it. The game's tone switches from "adventure!" to "prevent a survivor from committing suicide" to "adventure!" to "free a maiden from a somewhat offensive spear-weilding tribe" too often, and not with the art that allows better dramas to make you laugh, cry, and laugh again.
The problem, I suspect, is that the game offers up very little to think about as you blindly push Forward from setpiece to setpiece. The world is full of sadness and loss, clearly meant to echo the loss of the Brothers' mother and the potential loss of their father, but there's rarely much commentary or depth to these scenes, just flavors of loneliness. Then, when the game abruptly moves on to riding mountain goats for fun, it's clear that the action scenes don't serve as meaningful counterpoint to the sadness you keep being witness to. During these patches of straightforward nagivation puzzles, there's simply not much to think about. The relationship of the brothers doesn't change, nor do their fears or hopes. They're curiously static against a constantly changing backdrop of sadness and lighthearted adventure. It's hard to put into words, but the game's insistence on dwelling on the world's misery without considering it more deeply makes the whole experience feel like spending a room with a person in the middle of a bad breakup: neither insightful nor very much fun.

When you first hear of the gameplay of trine 2, you may think that's a little bit out-dated, because you only have only 3 characters, move left or right (and jump),  2D-graphic... But when you are playing, you get sucked into an very impressive fantasy-world with loving characters, astonishing graphic, great sound, challenging riddles and realistic physics.
Pontius the Knight, Zoya the Thief and Amadeus the Wizard are 3 unique characters with completly different skills, lovingly animated and with nice vocals, always good for an appropriate comment. Pontius is the guy for close-combats, also capable to protect his friends, Zoya is the stealthy lady, good for long-range actions, and Amadeus can build blocks and planks, levitate objects and even some of the enemies. These complete different abilities have to be well coordinated to get through many different levels of mazes, gnomes, carnivorous plants and ... wait, didn't i hear the growling of an angry dragon???
To get through the levels, you must sometimes use you fighting skills, but more often find your way through blocked gates, dealing with gated, surving killer-plants, fire, acid, and so on. All these riddles can be solved with logical solutions by combining the different abilities of our three heroes.
Oh, and did i mentioned the very impressive graphic? 2D never looked so gooooood. Combined with the great underlaying audio, it brings the world to life. The leaves of the trees are waving in the wind, the frogs are croaking in the swamps, fireflies are dancing through the air - dont forget your jacket, it's really cold in the ice caves... Still not convinced? Then look at the screens, and watch the trailer, then you are.
Playing solo is possible, but in my opinion this game makes most fun when played with 2 other friends, each controlling one of the three heroes.
To come to the point: is it worth the money?
Hell, yes!!!

Red Faction is a FPS released in 2002.  You play as Parker, a average man that decided to go to mars to work in the mines to make money for his family. Its not that easy. The working conditions are horrible. There is a plague killing the workers, the miners are mistreated and there is no way to leave, since Ultor (your employer, also the same ultor from saints row) controls all the transport between earth and mars. The story is ok. The cutscenes are just bad, with bad animations and the worst lip syncing I have ever seen. The gameplay on the other hand is excellent. The difficulty is spot on, except for the bossfights. The guns are varied and fun to use. The game mostly consists of shooting enemies, but there are a few stealth sections and vehicle sections to spice things up. Red Factions real claim to fame is the GeoMod engine. It allows for destructible environments. This is heavily under used. This is probably due to the techical limitations of 2002. There are areas where the environment is destructible. Its really impressive to see buildings crumble in a realistic manner. The biggest problem for me is the games length. I played it two times and each time the game took me about 3-4 hours to complete. Give this game a try, but if you don't like old games wait for a sale.
P.S. The first time was cheat free. The second one was with cheats. the cheats are :"bighugmug" and "vivalahelvig". bighugmug gives you all the weapons with max ammo and vivalahelvig activates godmode.
P.S.S. the best parts of the game was the two times a random gaurd yelled at me and said "Stop right there rebel scum". This was worth the price alone for me. Seriously. it was great.

Incredibly addicting with a great learning curve, this indie game presents a challenging, although fair, experience for any RTS fan. Instantly one of my favorite games ever. By commanding a squad of variable size throughout random missions (although there is a story mode, and it is quite fun), the player is tasked with taking control of command points from a never-ending swarm of aliens. If you like Starship Troopers, you'll love this game. It has a few nods here and there and somewhat matches the feel of the film(s). I never noticed any bugs (outside of the endless swarm that you'll find your space marines constantly firing at) so it is a well-programmed affair.
My only real complaints reside with the marines themselves, I do wish that they had proper voice-acting and dialogue. Like the marines of the earlier Halo video games, I think it would really spice up the experience. If there is ever a sequel, I'm certainly buying it. It'd be neat to see a CO-OP mode where each player commands squads, but it isn't terribly necessary.
All in all, it's a fantastic experience that kept me enthralled to the point of forgetting to sleep. On a side note, I purchased this at about the same time as I purchased Dawn of War 2, which is another RTS. I can honestly tell you with complete certainty that I like this game more.

Okay, this game is pretty fantastic.
Infested Planet is similar to World in Conflict (or an older game Ground Control) in sense that you take control of a small squad and have a limited way of expanding or upgrading it, resulting in a game where winning mostly comes down to how well you can manage your units.
And, oh boy, how much fun that is.
Each mission starts with a certain amount of points, that you can spend on upgrading your marines to different classes, building supporting structures, or calling in for additional units. Because there is no way to lose those points, you are free to mess around and experiment with them as much as you like. At any point in the mission you can reclaim your invested resources and instantly spend them on something else. Which, as the game progress, will actually become an essential tactic in your path to victory.
At first you will be having fun by simply killing the aliens the hundreds, but as you become better at the game so does the aliens start evolving. Sooner or later they will start countering your favorite tactics by dynamically developing new forms of attack, which is exactly why it becomes so important to be comfortable with reusing your resources and reforming your squad to use a different set of units.
Although the game starts rather easy, it ramps up in challenge quite nicely, and by the end reaching a point where you will be forced to use every possible weapon in your arsenal.
Infested Planet is easy to get into, offers quick action, fast missions, and most importantly tones of fun.
