Heroes and Generals is an incredibly frustrating game because at it's core there is a great game with some really unique and fun mechanics but all of that is completely burried by an unacceptable grind, punishing maintenance costs and terrible to non-existant balancing.
The first thing everyone should know is when you first start playing the game you'll only go up against other realtively new players. After a certain point however you unlock other classes and the overall game. That would be great but it's like going straight from Kindergarten to being a graduate in college. Where as before you were doing pretty well and had a good handle on the game, now you're absolute trash because everyone else has been playing for two or three years straight and have unlocked all the good stuff, know the maps like the back of their hand, and are generally just light years better equipped than you are. That's not a huge problem by itself but it's a huge leap in difficulty you really need to be prepared for.
Now onto the core issues that plague H&G.
I have played a lot of free to play games and most of them have a steep grind in one way or another. H&G is on another level. Literally everything there is to acquire in the game, and there's a lot, requires a significant grind. A submaching gun you like the looks of not only requires the experience and monetary grind to get the gun itself but also the prerequisite weapons, ribbons and skills. So a single gun can take weeks of constant grinding just to get. You then have to actively grind just to maintain the weapon since every single bullet you fire is costing you money. Things like vehicles can cost an exorbitant amount of ingame currency. That's a huge issue by itself.
To make the matter even worse buying premium does little to make the grind any easier. In most games, for example War Thunder, the free to play grind can get pretty steep especially towards the end game. But spending a few bucks on Premium time can really alleviate it and make the whole thing pretty doable. For whatever reason H&G doesn't prescribe to this idea. With premium something that would normally take you three weeks to grind will take you two weeks and five days. Other than having an extra perk slot there didn't seem to be much value in premium so even if you have the means you can't pay to win. Nothing short of spending hundreds of dollars to outright buy items and unlock gates will make the grind any noticeably easier.
Just about everything you do in the game will cost you in game currency. Most players recommend rarely using grenades or good ammo solely because you'll be spending more in maintenance costs than you'll be making per match. So in just about every way you'll be constantly hamstringing and limiting yourself to the absolute basics because anything else is sheer luxury. That's not fun or enjoyable and really starts to wear on you over time.
I'm going to mainly talk about the tanks side of things since that's what I had the most experience with and where the balancing issues were the most pronounced for me. Do note however that while other sides of the game aren't as unbalanced they're still nowhere near enjoyably balanced especially with certain nation's weapons.
Tanking is one of the things that should be a lot of fun in H&G. There's some great mechanics that makes tanking pretty unique such as being limited to the narrow in-tank view unless you stick your head out of the hatch and risk being shot. That alone is a great mechanic for making tanks not the omnipotent infantry killing machines they are in other games since they're easy to sneak past. But, as usual, the fun and interesting parts get overshadowed by the BS.
So tank balancing: Tanking in H&G is split up into fourish categories. Light, Medium, Tank Destroyer, and Heavy. In most missions you'll play there will only be one or two of those categories. Usually Light by itself, Medium and Tank Destroyer together and on rare occassions Heavy. Light is very common and the only one you'll be playing for a while as you grind up the tank trees. For the most part light tanking is pretty fun and is overally pretty balanced. That is until you meet a Chaffee. The Chaffee is the only tank in it's tier that can two shot every other tank. It's faster and cannot be two shot by anything else other than another stolen Chaffee. Meanwhile your faction's best Light tank takes two shots to be killed and requires at least three shots to kill other tanks. The Chaffee can absolutely dominate games because of this and is just abysmal to play against. This kind of balancing is pretty par for the course in H&G tanks.
The same applies to the Medium/TD tier as well. The US again gets some great top tier tanks in both the Sherman Easy 8 and the M18 Hellcat. Both tanks can reasonably two shot every other tank in their tier while being able to take multiple hits themselves. Prior to the Panther being added, which US tankers were crying about for months because apparently the Panther would be super OP, the best Medium Tank Germany had to offer was the Pz. IV H. A buggy tank that would get absolutely slaughtered by US teams. Whats worse is there are at least two Medium tanks for each faction that are never played because the top tier tanks will demolish anything that isn't another top tier tank. The same goes for Heavies. Seeing a Tiger 1, Sherman Jumbo 76, or KV-85 is like seeing a unicorn. Which is a shame because these and the unplayed Mediums are fun tanks but are just completely unviable and a waste of currency.
However enemy tanks aren't the only source of salt you'll be shedding in your burnt out hull of a tank. Infantry can be a huge thorn in your side as well. There are a slew of anti-tank weapons available to infantry and for the most part they're not that bad. They either require wasting a lot of grenades or munitions to actually kill a tank or require good positioning and the tanker making mistakes. The problem is you'll only ever run into these types of infantry anti-tank weapons when you're facing newer players. Because anyone wanting to kill a tank that's worth their salt carries US sticky grenades. Sticky grenades will kill your tank in two hits, three if you're in a heavy, and can be applied very quickly. They are the bane of your existence and will mean you constantly fearing infantry sometimes more than enemy tanks. Don't even worry about bazookas or panzershreks in most situations because they're incredibly expensive to use so no one ever does.
Overall Heroes and Generals can be fun but it's very bittersweet because you'll quickly realize that while the foundation and mechanics are fun and unique everything is ruined by♥♥♥♥♥♥poor decisions from the developers. In other hands H&G could be a fantastic game but currently your time and money is much better spent elsewhere.

I previously wrote a review on this game, which was then answered by the developers, who did find fault in my review, but did so in an strange manner. I was asked to "reconsider my review." So here it is. Overall the online multiplayer is a blast and doubles ranked is just as fun, but the game isn't ready for competive people to play, and to be honest, the community is terrible. If you want a game that is casual and you don't mind bugs, this is a great game. But if competitive is not fun, and extremely angering. At almost every end game screen, if I won, would be assaulted with insults ranging from "get gud n00b" to paragraph texts on how the legend I am playing is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, and how all I do is spam. The next, problem is with one legend, Hattori. I wrote about her before, and was responded with Hattori's win rate, around 55%. To be honest I don't care how much she wins because I abhor playing against her. Even if I win, I feel bored and angry by this legend's repetitive playstyle and soon exit the game, only to play again the next day because it is really fun without Hattori. This is a free to play game, but it does feel like they are going a little overboard with the micro-transactions. I am fine with paying for cosmetics, but denying the game, just to make more money is a little annoying, especially because I want to try every legend, and not have to wait for them to become free for a week. This game is in beta so there is a little leeway, but some of them really affect the game. Many tiumes the sound, animation, and color would flash making it seem like the character was hit, but then negated, disrupting the game. As I also brought this up last review, they attributed this to lag; however, I live fairly close to Atlanta, Georga, so I am not sure that is the case. After playing this game for 24+ hours, I would reccommend it for the casual gamer, but for anyone competitive, wait a little before the game improves, both in terms of bugs, and equality. This is also not going to stop me from playing, just there is a lot of things I would like to get off my chest.

Considering that the sight of the ocean fills Kiwi with mortal terror, he has never actually seen a surfboard, let alone gone surfing. What research Kiwi could bring himself to perform suggest that this game is quite an accurate simulation of the sport of surfing. As if maintaining balance to avoid the ocean's deadly embrace isn't enough, there are the varying tides and many tricky waves that will try to pull you into the abyss. But to merely survive is not enough, you must also out-do your fellow aqua-braving madmen in what death-defying stunts you can do on your sliver of safety.
As you progress through the games story, even more dangers are placed in your path: sharks, other less alert, but infinitely better balanced surfers, and your own mermaid clones. The latter, Kiwi assumes, is the result of the mermaids stealing your DNA during one of your many "wipe outs." Some may suggest that it'd be more appropriate to call them mer-people, but that's silly. Any one who's studied the English language knows that the correct way to refer to the collective of them is "mermaids." Their ability to clone you implies many unpleasant things about the aquatic civilization, not least among them is a lack of laws against identity theft. Unfortunately, these implications are not explored in the game's story, most likely the developers plan to revist it in the sequel.

I've always had a love-hate relationship with RTS games. Loved the strategy and tactics, the power progression, but I'm a terrible micro-manager, so "real time" more often meant "turn based": pause, issue orders, unpause for a few seconds...pause again, survey the field, make minor adjustments to orders, unpause...
As such I eventually gave up on the genre, the myriad of unit types and a sprawling battlefields was too time consuming.  I came back into it briefly with Dawn of War 2, with its small roster of "Hero + Squad" and RPG elements.
Infested Planet scratches that RTS itch in a casual way, which is perfect for me.  Quick battles, small fire teams intead of unweildly armies, an evolving enemy that plays different each time and requires you to pay attention and switch up your tactics.  I still play it "turn based", but it plays so fast it doesn't matter as much.

I'd like to start of by saying that I am leaving a review of the game, not an ethical deiscussion about decisions made by the publisher, not a rant about older hardware not being able to max out every setting, nota  bug report, not anything else other than the game and how it plays.
Gameplay:
The Gameplay in Mankind Divided is similar to other Deus Ex games, offering a wide variety of ways to complete each objective ranging from silently hacking your way through doors never to be seen to gunning down every cop, merc, civilian and door that stands between you and your objective as a literal living war machine. Edios has greatly improved the dialoge interactions between Adam and NPCs in terms of animations. Characters stand and gesture naturally while expressing facial animations that are greatly improved over Human Revolution. When Adam turns off his sunglasses, you can really see the emotions in his pretty, green, robot eyes. Voice acting is very well done, although generic characters tend to have repeat voice actors. However, there is sometimes a delay between when you pick a dialoge option, when adam actually says it, and when the NPC responds. Not a deal breaker, but worth noting.
The Story:
Like many of the "Do not reccomend" reveiws will tell you, the story is in no way as expansive as Human Revolution, which was a bit disappointing, but, in my opinion, not a reason to pass on this game. Here's why. While very contained, Prauge is a very very very detailed overworld. Compared to Detroit and Hangsha from Human revolution, it is a much more immersive and detailed world, that changes depending where you are in the story. NPCs will be having a plethora of different conversations at a cafe that, depending on the owner, may not serve you because you're a cyborg. While I really wish I would've gotten to spend more time in Golem City, London and go and find Janus, what the central plot lacks in story, the game makes up in side missions. If all you do is the main story, you're probably going to be upset. The side missions are really worth checking out, some even have parts that span over time as the main plot progresses, and bring up things that eventually could be crucial to the main story. Yes, the ending really could have been stronger than seeing Eliza Cassan's biased reading the of the missions you chose to do, but if you want to know what happens after Human Revolution and play a Deus Ex game, you're gonna want to get it. I enjoyed all the stories for what they were.
The Controls
It's worth noting the controls are slightly different in Mankind Divided, for the worse in my opinion. RMB is now iron sights and cover is now a toggled F key. Fire from cover (To spook enemies) is gone and you have to peek out to shoot, getting hit. Controls in menus/hacking is obviously a second thought in the PC port. You have to use WASD to scroll around in hacking and select a node, and the different software menues are really obtrusive and get in your way, often causing you to click on nuke software you didn't want to use. On the Map, you have to use WASD or click and drag
to scroll the map under a fixed crosshair to see objectives and details. Mousing over a waypoint does nothing. Also, the mouse seems to be accelerated, and I had to turn sensitivity down both in game and on my mouse's DPI. If you want to select a previous mission, you cannot click on it, you must scroll with WASD. While Nixxes did a fantastic job with the performance of the port itself (the graphics, engine, ect) the controls are terribly optimised for PC and were clearly designed with consoles in mind. The controls are easily the worst thing about this game.
The Graphics
The game is gorgeous. If you have the hardware, running it with ultra textures and high quality lighting really is something. I know I said I wouldn't get into it, but Demanding =/= poorly optimized. I have a pretty great rig (at the time of writing, lol) and I can't max it out. Turn of MSSA (Under display, not graphics) and turn down advanced lighting, texture filtering and cloth physics if you want to maximize performance with higher textures.

EDIT 06/9: I've 100% completed the single player campaign and Breach mode. I'm surprised this game is getting so many negative reviews. I'm not a pro reviewer, but below are my thoughts:
The things that are good:
1. Graphics - a vast improvement from HR, and gosh darnit, everything looks pretty.
2. Gameplay, especially stealth - I'm a huge fan of stealth playthroughs, and I had a lot of fun doing a pacifist/foxiest run on the highest difficulty. Stealth is greatly improved in this game in comparison to HR, and I'm especially happy that the battery drain during cloaking is not as bad as HR. There are more pathways to discover, things to hack, and it's very enjoyable.
3. Music - music was good. It was really good.
The things that are okay:
1. Story - The story could use a little more fleshing out, and there are some unanswered questions. Judging by the way the game ends, I believe it's something the developer did so that they can make a new installment, or another DLC to continue the story. I wouldn't say the story is "bad", I think it has some great moments.
The things that are pretty bad:
1. Breach mode - I personally hate platforming, and Breach mode so far is very eh for me. It's quite pay to win, and the similarity of some of its' aspects to hearthstone is kinda laughable (booster packs, "cards", etc). Come on, Squeenix. Get your♥♥♥♥♥♥together.
2. One-time use DLC - I'm sure many of you have seen people complain about this a lot on the store page, and I have to agree. It really sucks. I won't go into much details here :P
3. DLC missions - At the moment, I've only played "Desperate Measures", and I'm a bit disappointed. I expect a little bit more gameplay, but instead I only got around 20 minutes' worth of content, and it's a very small one. It does shed some insight on the stories, and I hope the next DLCs will be a bit bigger and better.
So should you get this game? I believe so. I had a lot of fun playing the game, and I think you'd have fun, too. I'd give this game a 7/10.

“Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons” is an atmospheric adventure indie game done perfectly. The story is rich and includes a few puzzles too. The main idea of the story shortly - two boys who have already struggled with the loss of their mother, and are now faced with the reality of a sick and dying father, must save him by retrieving "The Water of Life". And so their journey begins.
The story is excellent, it immerses you into the world immediately. I've experienced a lot of different emotions - happiness, fear, wanderlust, compassion and grief. The game successfully tells a consistent, intelligible, fulfilling and mature story without the characters saying single word which you could understand because if I'm not mistaken it's in Finnish (which confused me at the beginning, to be honest), but it entirely relies on pure interactive game-play. That genuinely leaves a deep emotional impression on the player.
The world is elaborate, charming and spirited, and despite its story being only ~4 hours long, it takes you through a lot  of various environments, every chapter feels fresh, captivating and interesting. There also can be found some mini side-quests that reward you with achievements and extra contents. It would be a sin if I don't mention the brilliance of the soundtracks -  truly atmospheric and moving.
You control two individual characters at the same time (the brothers) to solve interesting, varied puzzles in order to progress through the level. Even if it's told that the game is supposed to be single-player, I think that it can be an amazing local co-op too. Playing by myself was unique expierience I have never had before because simultaneously controlling two characters can be quite challenging sometimes. There's a notice that game requires a controller to play - I played with keyboard (wasd, space bar, ctrl and arrows) and I hadn't any problems with that.
“Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons” is truly fascinating game. It had captured my heart. This is one journey you will never forget.
To be honest, the ending has broken my heart. But it was worth it and I'll definetly play this game again.

is a short, standalone Half-Life 2 mod set in the HL2 universe.
On the positive side, production values are good, there's a completely new "special" weapon, and the mod offers a few unique puzzles. There are some QR code graffiti scattered around, but they don't really offer much beyond enhancing the creepy ambience. What combat there was seemed random and senseless, and the puzzles, while interesting, felt isolated and lacking overall direction.
As advertised, Transmissions is
. I apparently spent 2.1 hours playing through it, of which a solid hour was retrying the spontaneous and unexplained final boss battle, and another 15 minutes setting up the steam controller configuration.
If you
loved Half-Life 2, particularly Ravenholm, but you didn't like all the blabbing breaking up the action, Transmissions may be for you.

Before I begin let's talk about the cash shop. They have one, it only sells cosmetic character skins and weapon skins, You buy the characters with earned in-game gold, not money. Don't avoid because of its f2p.
Very easy to pick up with an active community and skilled players. Four modes of online play, ranked 1v1,2v2, 4 player free for all and custom lobby's that let you set the match to all sorts of things ((up to 8 players in one map)).
In the ranked matches, expect spammers in low tier with skilled players being in low gold and up. Spam happens, but you will eventually be able to read the attack patterns and punish them easily.
Single player is lackluster at best, but the training mode lets you try out all the legends((and check out the skins)) before you buy them with game earned gold.
Why do I like this game? Because I lose to players who are better than me. I do not lose to spam or "cheap" characters because the game does not reward these things. It is up to the player to learn how to play the game. At the start, you might win some matches by spamming. More power to you, if your opponent does not know how to counter your spam you will always win. Once they do, however, you can either keep mashing the keys hoping it works, or you can improve.
This is a game of skill, pure and simple. Luck does not play a part of it, and I can honestly say after 100+ hours, there is not one single character better than the other. They all have strengths and weaknesses, but the game allows you to the main one and win if you are better than the player on the other side. In the immortal words of our forums, "git gud".
*Edit Six seasons later, I can still say they have not implemented any pay to win features, cash shop exists only in cosmetics.

Red Faction is an entertaining FPS that doesn't stray too far from 1990's shooter conventions.
It features a wide selection of weapons (most of which have an atrocious spread), some bullet-spongy enemies, levels with more than one way to traverse, a campy B-Movie style narrative and, what now seems to be a Volition staple, a huge spike on difficulty in the later levels.
It's a shame that the destructible environments are not a very prominent aspect of the game, but it's understandable that it would break the game's scripting and so it ends up being just a gimmick.
Parker, the protagonist, comes off as both a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and a simpleton, some of his interactions with other characters are cringe-worthy but provide some chuckles, and you end up wishing someone would wipe off that stupid smirk of his face.
As released on Steam, the game needs Pure Faction to work properly, prevent the bugs mentioned in other reviews and support widescreen resolutions.
It's a fun ride, a bit rough around the edges, sometimes a bit frustrating, but works.

I'm surprised how much I enjoy this game! It's very much like the popular game Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo consoles, but with it's own spin on the "arena brawler" genre. So far the mechanics are pretty good, although I look forward to see more depth added to the system. Smash bros beats it mechanically- rightfully so, as it has been around since 1999- that's over 15 years! For being in beta this game offers lots of entertainment, expecially for being a free game.
I have been playing it for a day now, and my first impressions were mixed. The graphics are going to be hit or miss for people, as it's style is "cartoonish", however, the characters are well designed for the art direction they have chosen and have personality. Weather you like it or not is going to depend on personal preference, but I think it works well.
However, one thing that I was surprised about was when I entered training mode. Much like Smash Bros, you have several tools for training at your disposal, including the ability to see hit boxes! This is a feature that the Smash community enjoys on Project M. I’m not sure if the feature is native to the unmodified game of Smash, but it is a pleasant surprise to see it in Brawlhalla. This gives me the impression that the team behind Brawlhalla care about the community, and are listening to what they want. A welcome change! This only fuels my excitement for the future of this game!
The game offers a variety of characters to choose from, called “Legends”- but free to play players will be disappointed to know that they do not have the entire roster unlocked. This turns out to be less of a problem than you would think. Although each character offers unique heavy attacks, many of the legend attacks are identical to the other characters. This is a negative, since the game doesn’t offer as much character diversity as Smash. Still, each character has it’s own stats. These stats can be modified however, in the form of taking different “stances” which change up the numbers. Each character has two “weapons” they use in combat, but the game has a limited weapon selection. The real difference between each Legend is the combination of weapons they use. Want a character with a guns and a hammer? How about a spear and a sword? What about a bow and an axe? Not all the possible combinations are in the game, but quite a bit are.
In the end, this game offers lots of enjoyment for being FTP. I have already dropped some cash to support the developers as well as unlock all the legends. Ohh, and one last note on the FTP model. It’s pretty good mostly. You can unlock all the legends just by playing the game, although it will take some time to do so. Cosmetic items are on sale, such as Legend or weapon skins, so no “pay to win” elements are here. This is good!
Give it a try!

Overall, I think this game is fantastic, but it is held back by a few flaws.
1. Microtransactions. Just as a rule, I'm against this. It does not impact the game and is clearly thoughtlessly added on top of the finished package, so it does not tarnish what is otherwise a good game, but be aware that they are there.
2. Some lack of mechanical gameplay polish. Overall the game is very well polished but certain mechanics seem like they needed more testing. One specific thing that drove me crazy was the Icarus Dash ability (this game's take on blink). It is a really fun thing to use... when it works. It should logically lock on to things (targets, cover, ledges) but it doesn't, making it very difficult to aim. There are several small mechanical problems like this that can lead to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t deaths and general frustration. This sounds like a nitpick, but these mechanical issues are perhaps my biggest problem with the game. The resource management can also be slightly frustrating, as you really only have one energy bar to work with, unless you use a consumable, which will expand that bar temporarially. This sort of limits gameplay, making it more restrictive than it should. I couldn't say if this is an imporvement over Human Revolution. I would say it's slighty different from its predecessor, but not better.
3. Scope. Although this game has that same global consipracy story that Deus Ex is known for, the general scope of this game is smaller and feels like more of a setup for the next game which is definitely the most obvious in the ending. It is clearly designed to be expanded by dlc as well, and that is frustrating when compared to the original. As a complete experience, Human Revolution is superior, despite the improvements brought in by this game.
As a sequel, it could have improved in more areas than it did, but overall it's still an excelent deus ex experience. The level design is phenomenal, the writing is still compelling, and the art design is definitely a step up with better graphical technology. The side quests are some of the most fascinating and interesting aspects of the entire game, and that's saying a lot. The world is also filled with hidden stories that add to the setting and the overall story in a really satisfying way. The music is fantastic, however there are no standout tracks like Icarus from the previous entry. Despite the criticism I made about some issues with polish in certain mechanics, this game excells in the concept of augmentations more than ever. This is how RPG progression should be done. Literally ever augmentation is well thought out and changes the way you interact with the world in massive ways. Every time you get an upgrade, it heavily impacts gameplay and can completely change the way you play the game. This system truly expands on the already phenomenal level design in a way that's almost akin to metroid.
As a side note, I am not a fan of how this game seems to implement DLC. It has a section called "Jenson Stories" which leave a bad taste in my mouth.  They are completely separate to the main story and you can't even use your build to play  them. The one that was released with as day one dlc feels like it was literally ripped out of the main game to be put in as this little episode that you play separately. It feels small and dumb, especially if you play it as a follow up to the disappointing ending. My only hope is that the dlc that they add in the future is actually lengthy, better designed, and better implmeneted than this.
Despite frustrations that lead to save scumming, and a vaguely disappointing plot (due to this story cearly being desinged as a 2nd act in a trilogy), this is still a fantastic game. Especially after the patches, I would definitely pick this game up if you have played the previous entry. I would suggest reading about optimizing your settings though, because this game is very demanding.

TL;DR:  While I personally enjoy this game to the fullest extent, I simply cannot recommend this game to any but perhaps the most die-hard RWBY fans.  This game has come a long way from its Early Access days, but not enough has been done to bring the game to its full potential.  While this game attempts to add something to the RWBY-verse in an interesting way, optimization errors, content pricing, and a community-wide chant of lack of content have brought me to not recommend this game.
I have written 3 reviews for this game prior to this one, and each one I have removed from the store for various reasons.  My first review was an Early Access one which did not reflect the changes that had occured around that time, and the other 2 lacked something in description that made them overall unhelpful.  In all three, I recommended this game.  This one I did not.
RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a hack-n-slash action/adventure game where you can play as the characters from Team RWBY and, as of recently, Team JNPR.  The game features a campaign, where you must find out who or what is tampering with the security network protecting Vale from the Grimm, and a horde mode, where you must fight through waves of Grimm to protect security nodes.
The game has the two main teams from the show:  Team RWBY comes with the game and has stronger, more focused attacks, where as Team JNPR is DLC and focuses more on the team dynamic.  Overall, the characters each have something unique that makes them different from the other, but a lack of combos hinders that diversity greatly.  Basically, if you learn one character's combos, you know them all.  The only diversity comes from their ultimate, team, and ranged attacks which can be upgraded through a skill point system.  Prestiging is also a thing, allowing players to increase a "Hunter Rank", but that's about all it does.
The campaign is, depending on how quick you are, no more than maybe 3 or 4 hours long.  It is linear with some boss fights sprinkled throughout.  You encounter new enemies and more of them each level, and there are 10 levels as the game stands right now.  Horde is a new mode that was added last year which has anywhere from 8 to 10 waves to fight through on 3 different maps.  This mode adds a money system in the form of Lien, which you can use to purchase defensive turrets.  This mode is where most of the action is.
If you are thinking of purchasing this game, be aware:  You will at some point encounter some form of crash or glitch.  This game has had optimization issues since the beginning, most of which have been taken care of at this point.  But ever so often I find myself facing a crash screen or some other error that should not have happened.  Furthermore, computer specs play a great deal into this.  AMD's, as far as I know, seem to have some issues with this game, and graphics cards are required.  Don't expect a smooth framerate, regardless if you have high-end specs.
Pricing and content go hand-in-hand.  Honestly, this game is a tad expensive for what it is offering:  a 10 level campaign, horde mode with 3 maps, 4 characters all for $20.  Pay another $5 and you can get 4 more characters.  I have no issue with the JNPR DLC.  I think it was well made and reasonably priced for what we got.  $20 for the base game is $5 more than what I would consider reasonable, $10 for anyone else you ask.  I think the game needs a few more horde maps, campaign levels or just campaigns, and more things to reward the players before I could consider $20 reasonable.  Furthermore, I don't particularly like that JNPR is far more diverse than RWBY when RWBY comes with the game, and the lack of attack combos in a hack-n-slash game doesn't make it better.
One last point I would like to make:  There is a mod following for the game.  If you find the game to be lacking in replayability but still want to put in some more hours, drop by the modding threads in the RWBY GE forum.  They are a swell crowd can have made everything from gamemodes to texture packs.
If you managed to read this far, thank you and I hope this helped you.  Like I said, I genuinely like this game, but I find that I simply cannot recommend it to anyone other than hardcore RWBY fans.  I've had many great experiences in this game, and I will support it as content development continues for it.  Whether you end up buying it or not, keep those things I have mentioned in mind.  GG and Good Hunting.

I've played this on and and off since it's release and the game has gone through several changes which have all improved gameplay.  From Blake's wonky dash that looked like an incomplete backflip and zoomed the camera, to a much smoother looking animation and better combo flow for everyone.  Overall, I'd say this game is not quite worth it at the moment.  This is a game to play with friends once or twice, then forget about it until the next pack comes out, if ever.
The game's balance has gotten better in terms of combat difficulty, which skill to "master," and less cheese mechanics.  Gone are the days of spamming AAA-H and infinite stun enemies.  Counter time is rather flexible but is punishing on a whiff.  Learning specific animations and sound queues will guarantee victory.  Playing with friends allows a plethora of combos and executiwon techniques.  Watching Wiess freeze multiple enemies while Yang and Jaune pummel the enemy is satisfying.  Also certain skills will benefit your team, some a little but more OP than others.
The game's combat is not perfect though.  The characters each have the own unique strengths and ultimates, but I feel like the balance of the characters aren't that great.  Pyhra is probably one of the best mobile characters in the game.  IMO, she has the easiest time to attack into dash cancel into air jump dash, attack.  She also has the best counterskill in the game allowing you to chain multiple enemies into hitstun and killing them. However, her damage is on the weaker side, forcing you to always be on the lookout for counter timing and extended fights which may not be what you want.  I like combos, but I also want to see some sort of damage ramp up to make it feel like I'm having some sort of impact.  Perhaps, some players enjoy longer fights though.

On the otherhand, Nora is a power house and can decimate enemies, but the animations are somewhat lackluster with repetitive spins and janky looking attacks.  Watching and playing as Yang is much more entertaining.  I was quite excited to try her after buying the character pack, but I found her the least appealing.
Grimm types are rather repetitive with only a handful of changes per type.  The real changes occur in the final two levels.  I'd like to see an expansion with more levels or changes to the current levels to allow more enemy types to spawn.  I also feel like some levels require certain team compositions, or else the difficulty increases dramatically.  I think this is more of a personal preference than game mechanic, but I still think that its a flaw requiring certain characters to be on the team to be more effective and guarantee wins.
I'd say the real meat of this game is its co-op mode, and mostly I'd rather do co-op horde instead of story.  The story mdoe is very basic and is worth playing through maybe once with friends.  Maybe twice if you're introducing someone to the game.  Co-op horde is a better test of your skills as you defend bases from an endless siege of grimm.  The difficulty curve is surprisingly short as more bases to defend spawn and more enemies are thrown at you within the first few levels.   Without coordination, it's pretty easy to lose within the first few waves.
Pros:
Playing a RWBY/JNPR character
Playing with friends makes for interesting combos
It's brevity
Cons:
Short and forgettable
Limited combat mechanics
Only Pyrha can extend her combos, I think this should be expanded to the other characters
Variety of characters =/= Viability
Lack of enemy types
Certain levels feel like they 'require' specific team compositions

DMC4:SE is fun and a step up from it's orginal game with 3 extra characters (Vergil, Lady and Trish) with their own skill sets from past games like Vergil from DMC3 and Trish from UMVC3, Vergil how ever has a couple extra moves not seen before or somewhat changed from orginal moves like his rapid slash when in DT being able to go back and forth repeatdly.
Story is pretty much the same except for the added start and end cut sceens for Vergil, Lady and Trish though at the same time I felt this to be a bit lazy, Vergil's should have had his own story as it has been confirmed that Nero is Vergils son and this could have been capatalized on as Vergils story for the game in terms of finding out who Nero's mother is, how Vergil came to be with her and so on. Trish as we all know came with Dante on his first visit so I saw nothing wrong with that other then using Dantes part of the story to fill in the gaps and Lady was pretty much replaces Nero's part of the story with no real changes.
Combat I find to be flawless with combos and possibilitys in fighting styles, Lady has her guns and trademarked rocket launcher while Trish uses the Dark Knight Spardas sword and magic capabilitys, Vergil also comes with his trademark weapon Yamato along with Beowulf a punching and kicking weapon taken from DMC3 as well as his Force Edge sword that gives you almost the same style as Dante with his Rebellion.
Thing's to do would be the main story of course on whatever difficulty, Human(Easy), Devil Hunter(Medium), Son of Sparda(Hard), Dante Must Die(Very Hard), Heaven and Hell(1 hit kill on either you or the enemy so take that as what you will), Hell and Hell (Just a plain old nightmare) and my fave Legendary Dark Knight(Pretty much Dante must die with a hell of a lot more enemys at one given time).
Bloody Palace mode has also made a comeback with 101 floors and a boss at every 20 floors, makes for a good time and to learn the characters moves and combos, if you have played Bloody Palace before then you already know but to thoughs that don't. Bloody Palace is a floor based mode where you defeat all enemys on that floor to proceed with bosses jumping in from the story at ever 20th floor(20, 40, 60, 80, 100) and Dante being on the very last floor at 101, the higher you go the more hard it get's(so if you think you had a hard time with Creedo or Dante on normal to hard then boyyyy you about to have some fun). You're also timed on this mode but I do believe you can turn the time off (I may be mistaken) but turning it off will also make it so you can't get the achivments for completeing in under 2 hours or beating Bloody Palace(Again maybe wrong). It is worth a play through to test yourself as it does help to learn the combos making this the perfect place to learn, one downside though is you have to unlock this mode by beating the games Story on Devil Hunter mode.
Graphics have definatly been given a boost as the game on very high looks beautiful, it runs smooth and the optamization is great, it also has a preformance check so you can see what frames you are about to be running( I have some Screen Shots of this)
DLC: I honestly don't mind that you can do this for this game as it's just a pay to skip type deal when it comes to the diificultys so you don't have to go through each to unlock the next but it's whatever to the ones that do.
The extra outfits for Trish and Lady is up to you but I wouldn't really bother as the Gloria outfit is a bit ugh to me.
Now the Super Nero/Dante/Vergil(Permernant DT for all three and always maxed guages for Nero and Vergil) is something that can also be unlocked in the game so is also a pay to skip deal only thing about it is if you was planning to go through the game with super characters and get that final S rating, you will be disapointed( S for style, time and orbs, still gave me a B rating) but it's fair as it's more for the after you done just show everything how OP you can really be type fun which is a great addition.
All in all if you're a hack and slash lover or a DMC fan like me, I would pick this up and would give a solid 7.5/10

Never before has there been a more storied example of Games Publisher vs. Game Developer than the Grand Theft Auto franchise. Rockstar games has put out several middling to excellent installments in its 20 year history churning out these open world sandbox story driven criminal-based games, and GTA V is about a 7 out of 10 by comparison to all of the other GTA games. Gone is physics-based water, enemy stagger, movie theater sound effects, and a compelling, thrilling narrative throughout, as was the case in GTA IV. In its place is a larger map. More vehicles. Compelling online play. And a new story gimmick called 'Heists'. Which give the player multiple options, crews, and equipment loadouts to try and take some of the most sought after scores in San Andreas.
Graphics: GTA was one of the most visually stunning games to look at of its time...and yet its detailed graphics menu allowed players to play on last gen computers as well. Now, the engine and the objects are starting to show their age. Polygonal hard edges, distant traffic stand-ins (which can't be adjusted), foliage pop-in, and ugly online player models are the seams in this game's visual cloth. These problems are not the only graphical ones, but none of them are significant enough to ruin the experience by itself.
Gameplay: Mileage always varies in GTA. When choosing what you want to do in this game, you're always going to seem like you have a number of different options, both in online and offline modes.
The story is long and touches a lot on GTA's lorebase a number of memorable times. But when those strings of narrative are woven together to make a cloth, the result is pretty mediocre. By contrast, in GTA IV, and even the game's 2 excellent expansions, we saw characters grow and develop over the course of the story, changing their views and stances on certain issues. Nico Bellic, who starts out as a cagey, quiet, soldier, despite numerous transgressions and setbacks, finds it in himself to trust those he loves and makes a new home for himself in Liberty City. This kind of development doesn't happen in GTA V's story mode. That's pretty disappointing. The characters at the end, are the same sarcastic, gun toting badasses that they are at the beginning. Nothing really changes of importance.
Car handling is different. GTA IV's cars were floaty and drifty. Even the most hardcore supers had flex in the suspension when you showed them quick turns in rapid succession. In V, all of that has been dumbed down a little. Cars are twitchy and responsive. Some have so much grip that they will not bite back unless you're driving around with your right trigger pressed full down at all times. Not all cars are set up with such leeways, but especially in the next gen versions, driving is a bit of a cakewalk.
Shooting is VERY different. Every time I return to GTA IV, I'm floored by how simplistic its shooting system is. Weapons can't be modified, and the cover system gets confused very easily. In V it seems they cracked it. Not only is there a 1st person element to shooting which has you looking down the sights of your weapon, but the accuracy of all firearms has been ramped substantially. Unfortunately, enemy AI still seems especially weak, with Rockstar doing more of its "Quantity over quality" approach to enemy design. Not once did the AI succeed in tricking me, or scaring me to the point where I had to rethink my strategy. Despite a few times with the cover not locking on to the right object, it's very serviceable. This reviewer would like to see nuances like (lenient) weapon condition, and windage at long range play a factor in future games. Sizeable improvements in AI are also urgently needed.
Flying is well done. Especially in helicopters, but it's clear Rockstar stuck with its guns and revamped the same chopper system from GTA IV, which was good. The aircraft have a good weight to them, and the momentum they carry feels realistic. Swimming/boats are well done. Probably the most underrated experience in GTA history if you ask me. At least since Vice City, the need for awesome pilotable boats has been certainly needed. The game's only sailboat, however, cannot be sailed. It's motor only.
Online/Expansions are where the game really starts to disappoint. Every one of the game's DLC packs have been free, which is excellent, but what's not excellent, is they've all been for online only, which indicate that Take Two's marketing strategy has triumphed over the gamer's desire for more things to do in singleplayer. Online itself has its own independent heist system, which is like Payday Lite. The 5 heists have a decent narrative component in which you learn why it is you're doing what you're doing, and occasionally see parts of the story mode's backstory. Unfortunately, the online lobbies are plagued with some of the worst flagrant examples of cheating and poor matchmaking that I have ever seen in a video game. I have, on multiple occasions, had all of my character's weapons and ammo drained from my inventory.  On all occasions I reported the incident to Rockstar, but their policy on griefing is more of a confused shrug than a commitment to do anything about it. You can get killed in passive mode by god choppers. You can try to complete a daily objective for your business only to find out the VIP you're supposed to be defending got killed by a grenade teleported onto his head from a mile away. These are just some minor examples that Rockstar doesn't seem to have a handle on.
Sound/Audio: GTA V's soundtrack is great, except for a few glaring omissions, like a lack of an electronic station. Worldwide FM, which is the closest thing is often a very confusing mix of tracks that seem like they were just thrown against a wall to see what sticks. Other sounds like those associated with driving and combat sound great. I wish that they'd done a few more engine samples though. Some of them are quite overused. I am so glad they finally decided to update the gunplay sound effects. Many of them from GTA IV were tedious. Especially that police pistol one. You know what I mean.
Replay Value: This one's tricky. That's going to depend on what you want to do in this game. If you're flexible and want to do everything, there's no deeper game on the market for satisfying all of your chaotic sandbox desires. If you just want a driving game, there are some competitive racing crews out there, but the physics model is just a little too limited, and at times buggy, to represent a polished racer. Also, it's automatic transmission only, which will rightly irk some racing game enthusiasts. If you want a shooter, there are a lot of compelling reasons to choose GTA V. First person and third person modes are both very satisfying to play with, and it's versatile enough to support KB/M and controller setups. Still, its weak AI, and sometimes annoying bugs with cover mean you should be considering dedicated shooters as well before GTA V.
Management/Direction: Awful. Appalling. Ghastly. Dreadful. Worse than you're imagining right now. Take 2's ponderous approach to its marketing scheme has been recently underscored by its tonedeafness toward mods. Something that takes GTA V's playability and improves upon what's already there. This is even more glaring because they have failed to fix the obvious problems with cheaters in online mode. It's pretty laughable, really. The only logical reason I can figure that they haven't fixed the issue is that they can't be bothered, or don't care about the gaming community that they are responsible for. And that makes perfect sense as Take Two continues to ruin everything good about its games in steady slow succession.
As it is right now, I can't recommend this for 59.99. It's probably worth about 9.99, given how large TTI's profit margin has been so far. If that.

An exercise in absolute pointlessness. Transmissions: Element 120 offers nothing to the HL2 universe, and its inclusion in the setting essentially just serves as an excuse to recycle models, and its sole gameplay innovation is a variation on the Gravity Gun that creates a blast of force to blow open obstacles and increase your jump height.
Worst of all in my opinion is that the game is full of points of no return, a serious and entirely unnecessary design fail in a game that encourages exploration, which the game never warns you about before your way back is cut off for good. There are only two reasons to add a point of no return to your level design: 1) if you need to artifically shrink the level to be easier on the engine, and 2) as a cheap way to encourage replay by arbitrarily cutting off access to certain areas after specific checkpoints. Obviously one of these reasons is utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, and it's not the first one.
It's short and free, but not even worth that much. Little more than someone's level design practice that got released to the public. Plus the controller support is♥♥♥♥♥♥on a biscut, so there's that too.

But enough of that, I'll give what people like in reviews...lists.
Pros:

The biggest pro, saved for last!
-IT'S FREE
Cons:

So, let's add a bit onto this. It IS free, so what's the issue? I see no reason for it to be praised the way it is, and there is no "It's okay." rating, which is what I would pick had I not read any other reviews...but I did. Words like "Unique" "Equisite" "Perfect" and, the one that really gets me, "Atmospheric" are being thrown around like candy on Halloween, and I can't really see why. The gravity gun is, without a doubt, interesting, and fun! But reworking that is all that the game has to offer. The maps aren't intruiging, the fights are either quick, or drawn out, and despite the new and "unique" weapon, only one actual instance is given to use it largely to your advantage. The purpose of the weapon could have been entirely ignored if stairs, or worse, even a simple ladder were to be placed. A "game" like this should be based around the gun, making for a diverse experience that changes from player to player...but that's not what you get here. If you were to watch 20 people play this to completion, there would be very few differences, such as the following;
-Found all secrets / Found some secrets / Found no secrets
-Used only Gravity gun for fights / Used guns and Gravity gun / Used only guns
-Took the 2 opportunities for environmental help / Didn't use the only 2 environmental chances
And...that's about it. That's about the same as saying a Call of Duty game is diverse in gameplay because somene could choose to play on Easy, Medium, or hard, while also adding in that they can choose their guns, or may even just go with a knife! It's not actually diverse, it's still the same scenery and action.
There is nothing inherently wrong with the game, which is why I am going out a bit on a limb saying it's still not worth one's time. It doesn't lie about what it is, and even states it is a short "experience". But it's nothing new or breathtaking, especially due to the lack of content. The maps aren't great, the action isn't really any different than the original HL2 game, and the "atmosphere" is literally just set with a dark sky. It is no different from Ravenholm, so I'm perplexed by people praising it for that.
All the same, not a bad game, but not even worth the hour I spent on it. I'm not a fan of Techdemos that use a pre-existing Engine and only offer 1 new thing.

I already had a ton of fun playing Deus Ex: Human Revolution and I'm very happy that I can now enjoy the continuation of the story. The
of this review is that yes, there are a few controversies surrounding aspects of this game like one-use pre-order consumables, a separate tacked-on game mode that likely siphoned development time off the main game, and microtransactions which you really don't need as the game isn't grindy at all. To the contrary, it's fairly easy to get XP as well as credits (which you also don't really need, at all). I will chalk of these up to Square-Enix being greedy. I will blame the publisher for this, because I think everything else that has been crafted here is tremendous, resulting in one of the most entertaining games I've ever played. I'd like to think this means something after playing over 4,000 hours of Steam games, not counting my console or other PC gaming platform histories.
I'm bad at listing pros and cons. I don't think I'll be able to express my admiration for this game by listing a few bullet points. You may see me as a fanboy, but the fact is that, at 30 years, I've outgrown that kind of phase in my life. I simply like to style my Steam profile according to my current main game.
On to the topic at hand, this game is simply beautiful. The hubs have grown so much since Human Revolution and are much more dense, varied, and populated. I'm running the game above 60 FPS at 1080p with everything on HIGH, boosted by 2 x MSAA and Double Buffering VSYNC to eliminate screen tearing. I've also enabled all the fancy graphics options. I recommend switching textures to VERY HIGH if your GPU can handle it. The game warns you that you should have more than 4 GB of VRAM available for this, but I don't seem to have any problems with my MSI GTX 970 Golden Edition. This setting makes a big difference, because now I can really appreciate the banners, ads, little computer screens, and other details placed throughout the world. I wish real ads were this nice to look at! I can appreciate the work that went into creating these details and populating the game's world with them.
Praha simply looks great. It's refreshing to have a game take place in something that isn't a generic American city. We're getting less of those these days, but as someone living in Germany, as someone who's been to Praha many times, I can appreciate this story setting. People speak English with weird, European accents, some people talk Czech using accurate translations (AFAIK). The mission areas are generally very large and dense as well, decorated with lights, fog, lots of people, and tons of details.
You don't get loading screens when switching between buildings anymore. When you do get loading screens, e.g. when starting the game, moving between hub areas, and starting story missions, they're all nicely disguised with story summaries, little pre-rendered cutscenes, and even story cutscenes after which you're immediately back in the action.
The refurbished augmentations as well as the new ones are quite interesting, even if they are a bit flashier than necessary for playing Deus Ex in pacifist ghost stealth mode. Taking out 3 enemies with the taser fist as well as the camera watching them doesn't get old though. The offensive battle augmentations are nice as well, but relying on them isn't really the Deus Ex way. At least not for me, and this is
review after all.
Hacking has been given a new coat of paint - but most importantly, they've balanced the experience points properly this time. Acquiring codes and passwords is now a viable option. There is no need to hack your way through the missions to get some XP.
There is a decent number of side quests and points of interest. Some show a lot of love for fans of the series, others encourage exploration (Of which there is a lot. There's even vertical exploration.) Also,
.
I suppose there is a reason to wait until all of the bugs are fixed, but I've only ever run into one bug, which causes the game to crash if I don't enter the TF29 shooting range with a full inventory. I have to clear it all out before entering the shooting range. Other than that, I haven't run into any problems. I'm sorry if you have.
At this point, I've played 75 hours of Mankind Divided. It took me 46 hours to finish my first playthrough, which consisted of a pacifist stealth run and all the side quests. I'm halfway through my second playthrough and I'm enjoying every minute of it.
If you can immerse yourself in great video game worlds, you can have a great time playing Deus Ex: Mankind Divided - especially if you're already a Deus Ex fan and enjoyed Human Revoltion. Not everyone can. I, however, love doing it and the fact is that I adore this video game. It's a tremendous work of art that will hopefully continue as a franchise.
Thank you, Eidos Montreal. Square Enix, dial back your greedy corporate BS a bit, please. Trust in the developers and let them create their games as they envision them.

I'm giving this game a 7/10.
Graphics were good, sound was good. Musical tracks weren't anything memorable but the ambiance they created was generally good.
Story was... well it was the story we've been seeing throughout the DX franchise, and specifically since the beginning of the Jensen Arc, everything necessarily needs to build to the beginning of the JC Denton Arc, so we all know where it's heading. I think they've done an alright job of that, even if there aren't really any big surprises along the way, at least not in this installment.  I am looking forward to seeing how they tie everything up.
Augmentations received a big boost in this one. Whereas in DX:HR I felt like the augmentations were largely superfluous and not terribly useful or interesting, there are several in DX:MD that are very useful, and the ability to more easily toggle the active ones on/off was a welcome change.
The UI is a mess, and I'm giving the game a -1 for it. Kudos to DX for being one of the games to eliminate the anachronistic falling damage feature, but inventory management is still a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ and seems to be in the game for the sole purpose of giving people something to upgrade. The inventory itself is also a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to navigate.  All of your items have a strange stickiness to them, and moving things around is unnecessarily wonky. Combining items, modifying them and using them requires you to click on an item, wait, then click on a popup menu that appears.  It's all just very inefficient and made dealing with items considerably less enjoyable.  This seems like a small quibble until you realize that picking things up and using/combining/dismantling/modifying them is a sizeable chunk of the game.
There are a few things that, while playing the game made me think: "Do game developers even play their games?"  The forced mouse acceleration was one.  It's not a huge deal and you do get used to it, but it is aggravating nonetheless.  Why not an option to turn that off?  The game also seems to have a sizeable memory leak that requires a restart every couple of hours.  It doesn't seem to affect everyone, but it affected me.
Finally.  Unskippable credits, seriously? In 2016?  Not just unskippable credits, but plot-revealing cinematics mixed in with the unskippable credits just to ensure you sit there for the full 15 minutes staring at names of people you don't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about.  Pretty scummy.
I'd give the game another -1 for this, but I don't honestly believe DX:MD deserves a 6/10.  It was fun.  I enjoyed it, if maybe just a little bit less than DX:HR.  Everything felt just a little less streamlined, as if this game were the original and DX:HR were the sequel.  Instead of just running up to cover and holding a button, now there's a weird cover system with F that seems superfluous since you could just move behind cover manually and accomplish the same thing.  And I already mentioned the inventory management stickiness...
I didn't penalize the game at all for all the microtransaction BS people are giving it low scores for.  I simply don't care that other people can pay to win in a single player game.  It doesn't affect my playing experience whatsoever.
So... I dunno.  If you liked DX:HR, then this one is sorta more of the same. I enjoyed that game, and I enjoyed this one, but I still feel like the series as a whole is moving away from the elements that made me love the original Deus Ex.  It's got to be hard to write a deep and compelling storyline in a series of prequels though, since we already know where things are headed.
TL:DR - If you liked DX:HR, you'll probably like this, but it's not perfect by any stretch of the imagination.

Right, I believe I should post a review about the game, considering the recent controversy that has put GTA in a bit of a spotlight, this time negative imstead of positive.
As folks know already, the modding tool OpenIV has recieved a Cease and Desist notice, essentially terminating Singleplayer modifications (Important note: Singleplayer)
This essentially makes the singleplayer component of the game stuck with essentially the same old same old, that being the same game with the same protagonists with the same you know already. No room for customization like that Rick Sanchez mod that was a thing.
I will admit, it has been noted that Modding was not exactly a welcome sight, due to Take Two (Mostly them) and their concern that Singleplayer modding would leak in to their Online portion. Something that was pretty much impossible with OpenIV as it was not designed to cheat in the game.
So of course that is the whole backlash thing. I guess I can also talk about the game, since this is a review after all:
Singleplayer: Everyone and their amoeba probably know what the singleplayer is about at this point in time, so no need to talk about it. Except that it used to have extensive modification options, but not really now.
Multiplayer: Something that is literary the only reason most people play the game for, except some people still on the Singleplayer (Because honestly, SP is still a pretty solid story to play through), as it is the main thing that is being supported by the developers. Although I would say that ovee time, it started from what sounded like a good time in to a game of "Whoever has the biggest gun". I started it off as a street urchin, and I gotta say it was pretty exciting, but now that my character is quite a high level, I feel like it is no longer a fun game, but more of a slog of "Eh, another day, another dude with a fighter jet nuking me".
Not to mention that hackers/cheaters are also quite frequent, folks running scripts that make them immirtal, make money drops or just screw with people. It is something that is simply not fun.
This was written on a quick notice, so some things might sound a bit odd, so there's that.
Anyway, would I recommend the game? For the singleplayer, I would say yes as it is a pretty solid experience. For Multiplayer? I would say no because it is a dismal place that multiplayer, where you are forced to either grind for a long time to get somewhere, or spend hundreds of your money to get something nice and pretty. Not to mention Take Two's controversy being a sore thing.
Overall: No, I wouldn't say that the game should be purchased.

I'm fairly certain no one outside Ubisoft saw this game coming when discussions of a Far Cry 3 expansion were making the rounds, but developers absolutely need to be encouraged to make more offshoot experiences like it. Blood Dragon is a standalone title which takes everything that was cheesy, campy, ridiculous, and hilarious about 80s action/sci-fi B movies and packs it all into a big open-world island full of cyber-soldiers and laser-shooting dinosaurs.  The storyline and characters are perfectly hammy and over-the-top, the graphics are appropriately lurid, the synth-filled soundtrack is note-perfect, and it's funny as hell.  You don't need (or need to be familiar with) Far Cry 3 to play it, and it won't make a dent in your wallet either.  The lack of mission replay is one of the only bad things I can say about it.  Get it and play it; if you're at all familiar with the craziest the 80s had to offer, you'll have a big dumb grin on your face the whole way through.
It's got great gameplay, lots of references and the in-game jokes are hilarious.

If you enjoy (or at least remember) 80s and 90s american films starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and Dolph Lundgren, learnt your swift karate moves from Mr. Miyagi and  imagine a glowing red eye halfway through word "Cyborg", then you should immediately buy this game. From the first cutscene (which are crafted in a small cartoonish G.I. Joe style interludes) it starts to parody every 80s and 90s films sereotypic scene. Name one and you'll find it in the game. And almost everything in the game is hilarious. During tutorial I laughed maniacally non-stop and 6 hours later during the final battle game again ran me into laughing hysteria.
FPS component of the game is pretty good, yet not great. Player can carry up to 4 weapons of overall 8. Every weapon handle differently and serves different purpose, ammo for every type is limited, that force you to pick weapons according to your playstyle. Which is almost crucial because game throws at you packs of enemies in a variable combinations. There are standart soldiers, rushers, snipers, heavy gunners... and then there are dragons. Those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s are a game changers. Throwing a cybernetic hearts ripped from the chests of your fallen enemies and trying to just stay alive if  one is on to yourself.
And there goes PROBLEMS:
First of all dragons are incredibly strong and enemy cyborgs are equally weak. You can avoid them but main story will put you in a fight against one and later two dragons simultaneously. To kill them effectively you'll eventually start exploring the island and doing sidequests to level up and get your weapons upgraded. Soon you'll get too powerful for enemy cyborgs therefore FPS part will be too easy ro be interesting.
Open-world component is kinda decent but still it feels like a filling space between main and side missions. Multiple ways of approaching every side mission and base capture are barely enough to carry you through roughly 60-70% of them without yawning.
Graphic style is moot. Sunny and bright colorful jungle of Far Cry 3 became a dirty and dark grassland with a terminator-vision red filter which make you want to close the game or reap your eyes off at least for a first hour.
And the biggest problem of the game is its short length. It took me 6 hours to complete main campaing, every side mission and  base capture, find every collectable and getting every (uplay) achievment on medium difficulty.
Still it's a great game and even greater parody.And if for a game it might be 7/10, but as comedy its a 9/10 parody and a must-own for everybody who get this setting. I've played this on and and off since it's release and the game has gone through several changes which have all improved gameplay.  From Blake's wonky dash that looked like an incomplete backflip and zoomed the camera, to a much smoother looking animation and better combo flow for everyone.  Overall, I'd say this game is not quite worth it at the moment.  This is a game to play with friends once or twice, then forget about it until the next pack comes out, if ever.
The game's balance has gotten better in terms of combat difficulty, which skill to "master," and less cheese mechanics.  Gone are the days of spamming AAA-H and infinite stun enemies.  Counter time is rather flexible but is punishing on a whiff.  Learning specific animations and sound queues will guarantee victory.  Playing with friends allows a plethora of combos and executiwon techniques.  Watching Wiess freeze multiple enemies while Yang and Jaune pummel the enemy is satisfying.  Also certain skills will benefit your team, some a little but more OP than others.
The game's combat is not perfect though.  The characters each have the own unique strengths and ultimates, but I feel like the balance of the characters aren't that great.  Pyhra is probably one of the best mobile characters in the game.  IMO, she has the easiest time to attack into dash cancel into air jump dash, attack.  She also has the best counterskill in the game allowing you to chain multiple enemies into hitstun and killing them. However, her damage is on the weaker side, forcing you to always be on the lookout for counter timing and extended fights which may not be what you want.  I like combos, but I also want to see some sort of damage ramp up to make it feel like I'm having some sort of impact.  Perhaps, some players enjoy longer fights though.

On the otherhand, Nora is a power house and can decimate enemies, but the animations are somewhat lackluster with repetitive spins and janky looking attacks.  Watching and playing as Yang is much more entertaining.  I was quite excited to try her after buying the character pack, but I found her the least appealing.
Grimm types are rather repetitive with only a handful of changes per type.  The real changes occur in the final two levels.  I'd like to see an expansion with more levels or changes to the current levels to allow more enemy types to spawn.  I also feel like some levels require certain team compositions, or else the difficulty increases dramatically.  I think this is more of a personal preference than game mechanic, but I still think that its a flaw requiring certain characters to be on the team to be more effective and guarantee wins.
I'd say the real meat of this game is its co-op mode, and mostly I'd rather do co-op horde instead of story.  The story mdoe is very basic and is worth playing through maybe once with friends.  Maybe twice if you're introducing someone to the game.  Co-op horde is a better test of your skills as you defend bases from an endless siege of grimm.  The difficulty curve is surprisingly short as more bases to defend spawn and more enemies are thrown at you within the first few levels.   Without coordination, it's pretty easy to lose within the first few waves.
Pros:
Playing a RWBY/JNPR character
Playing with friends makes for interesting combos
It's brevity
Cons:
Short and forgettable
Limited combat mechanics
Only Pyrha can extend her combos, I think this should be expanded to the other characters
Variety of characters =/= Viability
Lack of enemy types
Certain levels feel like they 'require' specific team compositions

RWBY: a Good Start to a Great Game
For those of you reading this, you're probably thinking "Should I buy it?" My blunt answer is Yes. This will be explained in a moment.
THERE WILL BE SPOILERS IN MY POST. If you do not want to know what happens without experiencing it for yourself, please turn away.
I just recently had the pleasure of being sweapt into the world of "RWBY". It seems that with each passing season there's more to love. The animation, the characters, and the world created by Mr. Oum all get better by leaps and bounds. When I saw there was a game my heart lept for joy. So in a moment of impulse, I dusted off my steam account and purchased both the game and dlc with team JNPR.
First Impression: Pretty cool.
The gameplay is really straight forward. progress forward, battle the goons (generally Grimm) that come your way, and get to the end point of the level while searching for artifacts and leveling up your character in the meantime. You choose from any of the four members of RWBY to play as (Yang ftw baby), or if you have the DLC then you can also choose from the members of team JNPR. Each character has their own set of moves, strengths and weaknesses making each character their own experience. As you progress, you get calls from Professor Port, Dr. Oobleck, and Ozpin explaining certain objectives for the current level. You get through the ten levels and then Yippie, you've beat the game.
Here are some Pros:
-The game features the original voice actors, each portraying the quirks that we love about each character.
-The music. 'Nough said.
-The waves of Grimm, and the enemies in general pose a pretty good challenge. I found myself kind of surprised at how challenging it can actually be.
-The game features an original story pitting Team RWBY against Dr. Merlot, a character that hasn't been revealed to the show (yet, that is unless I missed something.)
Here are the Cons:
-The repetetive/predictable gameplay. As you progress through a level, the map takes you through some passageways leading to some wide open areas where almost inevitably, a horde of Grimm spawns. This predictability cripples most of the surprise factor. When Im running up on an open area, I can usually assume that Ozpin and Merlot are going to have some kind of banter followed by a few waves of Grimm, resulting in the only surprise being "what's the new enemy I'm going to encounter on the last wave?" Then the next passageway opens up and it's rinse and repeat.
-The lack of variety. When I say lack of variety I'm mainly pointing at the waves of enemies and the character stats. The waves usually feature a main type of Grimm (or Merlot's creations) with MAYBE one or two other types of enemies sprinkled in. And as for the characters, while I praised the game earlier for giving each character their own strengths and weaknesses, It doesn't accentuate this enough between characters (namely the aura, base attack stats, and attack pattern.) I've found that with each character, I can pretty much left click three times and follow with a right click and have a pretty decent combo.
-A lack of true boss fights: There is only one real boss in the game and that's the Deathstalker. I found it to be pretty challenging and actually enjoyed it. Unfortunately, it made me ask the question "where was this in some of the earlier levels?" Fans of the show will recall the Nevermore, the Griffons, the Dragon, and King Taijitu. There's four potential bosses that could have each posed a different challenge on their own. Not to mention potential appearances from rival characters such as Roman Torchwick, White Fang members or even a sparring session with ole Uncle Qrow.
Of course, if my understanding is correct, the game is still under development so some of these things could still be adjusted. And if not, who's to say they won't come out with another game?
That said here are personal suggestions to the devs (Not really Pros or Cons):
-The artifacts: I was excited when Professor Port told me to look for artifacts through the level. I was a little sad when all it did was give me experience, Which is fine but searching for artifacts becomes pointless after reaching level ten. So what about incorperating some sort of incentive for finding them. For example, each artifact unlocks a new concept art, or development screenshots, or a funny RWBY Chibi clip. This would make looking for the artifacts worth something and open up more possibility for hidden passages or puzzles.
-PVP: Imagine if you will teams of four on four, one on one, or any number in between squaring off against each other online. Fans should already know what I'm hinting at. A Vytal Tournament would be awesome for a game like this. Wouldn't it be cool if each character were good against certain characters and weak against others? it would kind of be like a moba but with teams of four. That could also just be me fanboying.
-More playable characters. How cool would it be to play as Qrow? Or use Sun Wukong's multi-form? Even just shooting at things with Roman's cane?
-More immersion for the plot: I didn't mind the way this story was told, but personally I feel like the story lacked some of the substance that the show brings. While i did enjoy Dr. Merlot as a villain, I think it would have been cool to have some cut-scenes of Merlot goading the protagonist(s) in person from aboard an airship, behind some forcefield, or even have him watch certain fights from the background commenting as the battle goes (kind of like the computer screens in the last two levels. the art for those shots of Merlot gave him a certain menace that I loved btw). Or as I mentioned, side stories that interfere with the main plot sometimes like sparing with Unkie Qrow, or stumbleing upon Torchwick and the White Fang amidst your travels.
-Super Saiyan Yang: I really missed Yang's semblance. This is just a suggestion: but perhapse instead of her quake ultimate (which was actually pretty cool in its own right) her ultimate bar fills with the damage she takes as well as she dishes out, and then when its activated, she gets about a 10-20 second boost of attack power and speed? I'm only saiyan.
-A block button: 'nough said.
Overall, the title of this review sums up my thoughts entirely. The game is a good start to what could be the ultimate RWBY game. I while there was some meat to my Cons list, I did appreciate the overall idea of the game and the hack and slash style. It isn't a bad game by any means, It's just missing a few things that would drive the game to greatness. In my oppinion, the game just barely earns the $20.00 pricetag as it stands. So should you buy it? Yes. I believe they deserve the support. And in doing so it'll pave the way for bigger and better games, be it this game or a new one entirely.
